articles.title: Age and intensive care unit admissions following opioid overdose.
articles.abstract: Older adults are increasingly impacted by the opioid crisis, yet age-related differences in overdose presentation, management, and outcomes leading to intensive care unit (ICU) admission remain poorly characterized. This study examined age-related variations in drug exposures, interventions provided, and hospital utilization among patients experiencing an opioid overdose. The Toxicology Investigators Consortium (ToxIC) Fentalog Study was conducted at 10 US medical centers and collected data on patients who presented to emergency departments with confirmed non-fatal opioid overdose, and available waste serum samples between 9/21/2020-4/14/2026 were included. Chart reviews captured presentations, treatments, and hospital utilization. Toxicologic analyses were performed at the Center for Forensic Science Research and Education. Nested multivariable logistic regressions assessed whether age improved predicted ICU admission, after accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and drug classes detected. Among 1930 patients, 15.3% were admitted to the ICU, 7.8% received cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and 5.8% were intubated. Length of hospital stay varied by age, with patients 65 + years old staying longest (median: 22.0h, IQR: 87.0, p < 0.001). Illicit opioids were less commonly detected in older adults (p < 0.001), while prescription opioids were more common (p < 0.001). Age cohort did not significantly predict ICU admission, although prescription benzodiazepine (AOR: 1.4, 95% CI: 1.1, 1.9) and opioid (AOR: 0.7, 95% CI: 0.5, 0.9) detection did. Older age was associated with longer hospital stays but did not predict ICU admission after adjustment for relevant covariates. Benzodiazepine and opioid exposures showed a modest association with ICU utilization. Further work should clarify how pharmacologic combinations influence clinical severity across age groups.

articles.title: Management of the Critically Ill Patient with Opioid Use Disorder.
articles.journal: Emergency medicine clinics of North America
articles.abstract: The management of critically ill patients with opioid use disorder presents a unique challenge, as overdose, withdrawal, or concomitant intoxication, due to an unregulated drug supply, leads to physiologic changes that potentially impact standard treatment. This review article outlines an emergency medicine-focused approach for early recognition and stabilization of opioid overdose or withdrawal. Topics include naloxone, use of medications for opioid use disorder, recognition of concurrent intoxication, treatment of α2-agonist withdrawal, multimodal analgesia, and sedation for opioid-tolerant patients. The acute management of opioid use disorder is an opportunity to prevent withdrawal-related decompensation, improve comfort, and support ongoing engagement in treatment.

articles.title: Empirical linezolid target attainment in critically ill patients: integrating local susceptibility data and dosing strategies.
articles.abstract: Linezolid is important for treating infections caused by Gram-positive bacteria resistant to first-line agents. Severe infections often require empirical therapy before pathogen identification and susceptibility testing. This evaluation aims to compare different empirical linezolid dosing strategies in intensive care unit (ICU) patients to improve pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic target attainment while minimising toxicities. Three dosing strategies were compared: (i) standard dosing, (ii) therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)-guided dosing, and (iii) a theoretical model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) strategy based on Bayesian forecasting with a population pharmacokinetic model. Each scenario was combined with an ICU-specific minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) distribution comprising more than 19,000 isolates collected over 10 years. Data from 117 critically ill patients with 2184 TDM samples were available. Linezolid resistance was highest in ICU isolates (9.6%) compared with isolates from the intermediate care unit (4.3%), general wards (3.6%), and emergency room (1.6%). Among ICU isolates, resistance increased significantly over the 10-year study period, from 6.3% in 2015 to 11.4% in 2024. Empirical target attainment was 36.6% with standard dosing and 48.5% with TDM-guided dose adaptation, in two different ICU cohorts that showed 35.9% and 59.4% baseline target attainment, respectively. Theoretical MIPD projected target attainment in 71.4-81.6% of patients. After excluding resistant isolates, the corresponding values were 40.5%, 53.7%, and 79.0-90.3%, respectively. Integrating a large contemporary ICU-specific MIC distribution with patient-level pharmacokinetic data, our results suggest MIPD may represent a promising strategy improving target attainment, in contrast to standard regimens and TDM-guided dosing which failed to achieve adequate target exposure in ICU patients.

articles.title: Vitamin D supplementation is associated with reduced requirement for mechanical ventilation in patients with pneumonia: a large-scale, propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study from MIMIC-IV.
articles.abstract: Vitamin D plays an important role in host immune defense against infection. However, the potential prognostic benefit of vitamin D supplementation in patients with pneumonia remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between vitamin D supplementation and clinical outcomes among patients with pneumonia. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. Patients with pneumonia were included and categorized into early vitamin D supplementation and non-supplementation groups. Baseline characteristics were balanced using propensity score matching. The primary outcome was the requirement for mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, new ICU admission, in-hospital and 28-day mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. A total of 13 092 eligible patients were included: 859 in the vitamin D supplementation group and 12 233 in the non-supplementation group. After PSM (n = 1716), early vitamin D supplementation was significantly associated with a lower requirement for mechanical ventilation (5.83% versus 9.56%, P = 0.004) and lower 28-day mortality (9.32% versus 13.87%, P = 0.003). The association between early vitamin D supplementation and the requirement for mechanical ventilation remained significant among female patients, patients without chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, patients with relatively low serum total calcium levels, and patients with relatively high white blood cell counts. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed delayed onset of mechanical ventilation in the early vitamin D supplementation group. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis showed that early vitamin D supplementation was independently associated with a reduced requirement for mechanical ventilation. No significant association was observed between vitamin D supplementation and length of hospital stay, new ICU admission, or in-hospital mortality. Among patients with pneumonia, early vitamin D supplementation was independently associated with a lower requirement for mechanical ventilation and reduced 28-day mortality. Future studies are warranted to explore these associations.

articles.title: Airway Pressure Release Ventilation Versus Conventional Ventilation in Adults With or at Risk for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract: To assess whether airway pressure release ventilation (APRV) reduces mortality compared with conventional invasive ventilation in adults with established acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), acute lung injury, or conditions considered to confer a high risk of ARDS. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception through August 15, 2026. We analyzed parallel-group randomized trials using random-effects models. Mortality at trial-defined follow-up was the primary outcome. We used Cochrane RoB 2 to assess risk of bias and GRADE to assess certainty of evidence. CRD420251170819. Nine trials involving 585 participants were included. No mortality benefit was demonstrated (risk ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.72-1.26). Ventilator-free days showed no clear difference (mean difference [MD] 3.83 days, 95% CI - 1.69 to 9.34; I²=83%). APRV was associated with a higher PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio (MD 56.21 mm Hg, 95% CI 24.63-87.79; I²=84%) and shorter ICU stay (MD - 2.53 days, 95% CI - 4.43 to - 0.64; I²=71%). Ventilation duration showed no clear difference (five trials, 413 participants; MD - 2.44 days, 95% CI - 4.96 to 0.09; I²=78%). Peak airway pressure was lower and mean airway pressure was higher with APRV. This synthesis does not establish that APRV improves survival, ventilator-free days, or ventilation duration. Oxygenation and ICU-stay findings require caution because populations, protocols, outcome timing, and risk of bias varied. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. These data do not establish mortality equivalence or superiority over contemporary lung-protective ventilation. CRD420251170819; registered 17 October 2025.

articles.title: Postoperative Delirium in the ICU: Not One Syndrome, but Many?
HEMATOLOGICAL AND RENAL BIOMARKERS IN CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS WITH COVID-19 IN A BRAZILIAN ICU: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY.
articles.abstract: and Objectives: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is associated with high morbidity and mortality, especially in critically ill patients. This study aimed to evaluate the behavior of hematological and renal biomarkers and their association with mortality in brazilian ICU patients with COVID-19. This retrospective cohort study included 52 adult patients admitted to a Brazilian ICU between June 2020 and September 2021. Hematological parameters, urea, creatinine, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were assessed at admission and at the final outcome. Statistical analyses were performed in two stages: first, comparisons were made between sexes (male vs. female); subsequently, patients were stratified into survivors and non-survivors for group comparisons. Between-group analyses were conducted using the Mann-Whitney U test, with paired comparisons performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality. Patients who died during hospitalization (non-survivors, n=29) showed higher levels of urea, creatinine, leukocytes, and neutrophils, and lower hemoglobin and platelet counts compared to survivors (n=23) (p<0.001). Renal and hematological alterations were independently associated with mortality. Dynamic changes in hematological and renal biomarkers are strongly associated with mortality. Serial monitoring may improve risk stratification in critically ill COVID-19 patients.

articles.title: The hidden work of vigilance: a phenomenological study of how intensive care nurses recognise deterioration in older adult patients.
articles.abstract: Older adults represent a growing proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, yet deterioration in this population is often subtle and atypical, requiring heightened nursing vigilance. This study explored how ICU nurses recognise early deterioration in older adult patients and how experiential knowledge shapes clinical judgement. An interpretive phenomenological study was conducted in tertiary hospitals in Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia. Fourteen ICU nurses participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analysed using hermeneutic thematic analysis, and reporting followed COREQ guidelines. Three themes emerged: seeing beyond the monitor, describing recognition of subtle physiological and behavioural changes; embodied and experiential knowing, reflecting intuitive concern grounded in clinical experience; and legitimising intuitive concern, highlighting nurses' efforts to translate tacit knowledge into actionable clinical communication. Nursing vigilance is essential for detecting deterioration in older ICU patients. Clinical systems should support nurses in articulating early concern alongside physiological data and should strengthen geriatric-sensitive assessment and escalation practices.

articles.title: Defining best practice for very old patients following unplanned intensive care admission: protocol of the Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract: Very old patients (≥80 years) represent a rapidly increasing proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) admissions across Australia and New Zealand. Care of this population is characterised by substantial prognostic uncertainty and variability in ICU triage, treatment limitation and post-ICU pathways. In particular, the role and implementation of time-limited ICU trials remain inconsistent. To establish multidisciplinary consensus on best-practice management of very old patients following unplanned ICU admission in Australia and New Zealand, including the role, structure and implementation of time-limited ICU trials. We will conduct a modified, multiround Delphi consensus study. A multidisciplinary, multispecialty panel of expert clinicians (intensive care, geriatrics, emergency medicine), doctors in training, nurses, allied health professionals, ethicists and health service leaders across Australia and New Zealand will be recruited through purposive and snowball sampling. Participants will rate statements using the Likert scale across multiple rounds. Anonymised aggregated feedback will be provided to participants between rounds to facilitate convergence of opinion. Consensus will be defined a priori using predefined thresholds and median scores. Quantitative analyses will include descriptive statistics and exploratory subgroup comparisons, while free-text responses will undergo thematic analysis. The primary outcome is to establish multidisciplinary consensus on best-practice management of very old patients following unplanned ICU admission, including the role and implementation of time-limited ICU trials. Secondary outcomes include identifying areas of agreement and variation across groups and convergence across Delphi rounds. A tertiary outcome is to explore barriers and facilitators to implementation to inform a structured decision-making framework. This study will generate consensus-based recommendations and a structured framework for the use of time-limited ICU trials in Australia and New Zealand ICUs. By addressing current practice variability, it aims to support transparent, patient-centred decision-making and inform future research and policy in the care of very old critically ill patients.

articles.title: Methiodone (IC-26) a case series: an old, but novel, opioid substance causing severe toxicity.
articles.abstract: Methiodone (IC-26; 4-ethylsulfonyl-N,N-dimethyl-4,4-diphenylbutan-2-amine) is a synthetic opioid derivative of methadone that has recently emerged on the designer drug market. Data on its clinical toxicity and pharmacokinetics remain limited. We describe four cases of severe methiodone intoxication requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission, taking place between July and November 2025. Clinical presentation, treatment, and outcomes were evaluated. In addition, systematic toxicological analysis was performed including Liquid Chromatography - High Resolution Mass Spectrometry (LC-HRMS) and targeted Liquid Chromatography - tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). All patients presented with a classical opioid toxidrome, characterized by respiratory depression, miosis, and decreased consciousness. Naloxone administration resulted in clinical improvement in all cases. Methiodone plasma concentrations ranged from 0.20 to 0.64 mg/L. The elimination half-life in plasma was estimated at approximately 13 h based on one case. Metabolite analysis revealed N-dealkylation as an important metabolic pathway, with additional hydroxylation and limited glucuronidation. Methiodone was variably detected in routine immunoassays, depending on assay specificity. No electrocardiogram (ECG) clinically relevant abnormalities were observed, in contrast to observations in methadone intoxications. Methiodone is an emerging opioid capable of causing severe, but treatable, intoxication. Increased clinical and analytical awareness is essential, as further cases are likely to emerge with the ongoing evolution of the new psychoactive substance market.

articles.title: Outcomes and Complications of Axillary Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Axillary intra-aortic balloon pump (axi-IABP) support has emerged as an alternative to femoral access for patients with advanced heart failure, offering improved mobility and potential benefits in pretransplant conditioning; however, data on associated complications remain limited. We conducted a retrospective study of 55 patients who underwent axi-IABP placement between January 2019 and July 2025 at our institution. The cohort had a median age of 59 (interquartile range [IQR], 52-65) years and presented with cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Axi-IABP successfully bridged 87.3% of patients to advanced therapies. A total of 83 complications were identified in 60.0% of patients, most commonly malposition in 23.6% of patients, gas leak alarms in 16.4% of patients, and kinking in 16.4% of patients. Serious vascular complications were infrequent. The median time to first complication was 10.5 (IQR, 2.75-25.5) days. Female sex was associated with a higher hazard of first complication when controlled for height (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 2.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.04-7.27; p = 0.041). In conclusion, axi-IABP is an effective bridging strategy that enhances patient mobility but is associated with a high rate of device-related complications, predominantly mechanical in nature, underscoring the importance of careful patient selection and monitoring.

articles.title: Types of adult intensive care units and admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract: Türkiye has one of the highest intensive care unit (ICU) bed capacities among middle-income countries but also globally. Nevertheless, little is known about the characteristics of ICUs in Türkiye, their temporal trends, and ICU admissions and readmissions. We sought to analyze the structural characteristics of all adult ICUs and the clinical profiles of ICU admissions across Türkiye. We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using data from the Turkish Ministry of Health National Electronic Database. We analyzed adult ICU admissions across all levels and types over 6 years (2018-2023) and documented patient demographics, comorbidities, admission diagnoses, and ICU outcomes. We retrieved data on 3,362,539 ICU admissions. Among 22 ICU types, mixed ICUs accounted for the highest proportion of admissions (31.4%), followed by coronary (23.7%), anesthesiology (14.3%), medical (6.1%), and surgical (6.0%) ICUs. The proportion of mixed ICU beds decreased from 44.0% in 2018 to 25.1% in 2023. Most ICU beds were in state (public) hospitals (50.8%), followed by private hospitals (34.8%). The number of ICU beds increased from 2019, with a notable rise in state hospitals after 2020. The average number of ICU admissions was 659 per 100,000 population annually. The median patient age was 65 [interquartile range, 39-91] yr, and the ICU mortality was 15.5%. The leading admission diagnoses were respiratory failure (10.1%), cerebrovascular disease (7.1%), and acute kidney injury (5.2%). Hypertension (67.5%) and coronary artery disease (44.8%) were common comorbidities, particularly in nonsurvivors. The 7-day ICU readmission rate was 3.0%. The present comprehensive analysis of ICU admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023 highlights a shift toward specialization with a decrease in mixed ICUs. The impact of ICU diversity on resource use and patient outcomes requires further evaluation.

articles.title: Longitudinal evaluation of a multidisciplinary infection prevention and control bundle in a high AMR prevalence ICU.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a major threat in intensive care units (ICUs). We evaluated changes associated with a multidisciplinary infection prevention and control (IPC) bundle in a high-AMR-prevalence setting. This longitudinal quasi-experimental ICU study (2022-2024) involved sequential, cumulative implementation of a bundle integrating infection prevention, rapid diagnostics and colonization screening, antimicrobial stewardship, and surveillance with data feedback. Hand hygiene compliance increased from 29.5% at baseline to 64.6% during sustainment, while PPE compliance increased from 67.1% to 73.3% after monitoring was introduced. Piperacillin/tazobactam consumption increased (+3.33 DDD/100 patient-days per phase; 95% CI, 1.92-4.73), whereas colistin (-5.85; 95% CI, -9.17 to -2.54) and tigecycline (-2.50; 95% CI, -4.25 to -0.75) decreased. Klebsiella pneumoniae meropenem resistance decreased (OR per phase, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.43-0.69), whereas colistin resistance showed a borderline increase in Acinetobacter baumannii (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.00-1.65). ICU-acquired bloodstream infections decreased across implementation phases for CRE (IRR per phase, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.26-0.51) and CRAB (IRR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.46-0.68), as did CLABSI (IRR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.56-0.73) and ICU-acquired rectal colonization with CRE (IRR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.63-0.84) and CRAB (IRR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.70-0.87), whereas CRPA ICU-acquired colonization increased (IRR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.32-1.85). IPC bundle implementation was followed by improved IPC practices and reductions in several ICU-acquired infections and colonization outcomes; continued surveillance and stewardship are essential.

articles.title: An Approach to Navigating the Lorazepam Challenge Test for Catatonia in Critical Care Settings.
articles.abstract: Catatonia often occurs in the setting of psychiatric illness; however, it is also found in other medical conditions, especially within critical care settings. The lorazepam challenge test (LCT) is a key diagnostic and therapeutic intervention for catatonia; however, no specific guidance exists for patients within the intensive care unit (ICU). This review synthesizes psychiatric and critical care literature to propose a structured LCT framework adapted to the ICU. Specific indications and contraindications across gradients of catatonia likelihood and medical complexity are reviewed, along with practical dosing and monitoring recommendations. An interdisciplinary collaborative workflow is also outlined along with post-LCT documentation standards. Our structured approach offers a practical foundation for future standardized protocols, education, and catatonia research in critical care.

articles.title: Application of Electrical Impedance Tomography-Guided Pulmonary Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients with Respiratory Failure.
articles.abstract: This study investigated pulmonary rehabilitation strategies guided by electrical impedance tomography (EIT) in patients with respiratory failure. A total of 92 patients with respiratory failure admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of a tertiary Grade A hospital in Chongqing from July 2024 to January 2025 were selected and randomly divided into a control group and an experimental group, with 46 cases in each group, using a random number table. The control group received conventional pulmonary physical therapy nursing strategies. The experimental group additionally received EIT-guided positioning, vibratory sputum clearance, and early mobilization. Relative regional tidal-ventilation distribution, PaO₂/FiO₂, respiratory rate, and pulse oxygen saturation were assessed at baseline and on the following three days; ICU stay, and delirium incidence were also compared. Finally, 44 cases in the control group and 44 cases in the experimental group completed the study. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant time effects across the four ventral-to-dorsal layers and significant group and interaction effects for the dorsal layer. Dorsal ventilation share was higher in the experimental group on days 2 and 3, but not significantly different on day 1. No significant group, time, or interaction effects were found for the four lung quadrants. The experimental group had higher PaO₂/FiO₂, shorter ICU stay (6.55 vs. 7.75 days), and lower delirium incidence (25.0% vs. 45.5%). Respiratory rate decreased, and pulse oxygen saturation increased over time in both groups, without significant group or interaction effects. The EIT-guided strategy may improve regional ventilation distribution and oxygenation, shorten ICU stay, and reduce delirium in patients with respiratory failure.

articles.title: Levosimendan and Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Weaning: Still an Open Question?
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

articles.title: Excessive Tidal Volume During Noninvasive Ventilation: Mechanisms of Harm Leading to Worse Clinical Outcomes.
Tunneled Dialysis Catheter for KRT for Acute Kidney Injury in the Intensive Care Unit: CON.
Robotic-Assisted Partial Nephrectomy in a Solitary Kidney in a von Hippel-Lindau Renal Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease is a rare autosomal dominant tumor syndrome caused by germline mutations in the VHL gene. Patients may develop multiple, bilateral, and recurrent renal cell carcinomas (RCCs), posing a major therapeutic challenge, particularly in those with a solitary kidney, where preservation of renal function is critical to prevent end-stage renal disease and dialysis dependence. This case demonstrates the surgical management of multiple renal tumors in a solitary kidney. A 37-year-old man with VHL disease (c.257C > G, p.P86R mutation) and a solitary right kidney following previous left radical nephrectomy presented with three progressive clear cell RCC (ccRCC) lesions, the largest measuring 4.8 cm, despite ongoing treatment with belzutifan, a HIF-2α inhibitor. A transperitoneal robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) was performed. A fourth tumor was identified intraoperatively. Complete excision of all tumors with negative surgical margins was achieved. Postoperatively, severe acute kidney injury (AKI) developed, requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), which was complicated by forearm necrosis resulting from calcium substitution paravasation. An additional complication included a right pneumothorax. Following intensive care management, including pleural drainage, renal function gradually recovered, and CRRT was discontinued on postoperative day 8. This case demonstrates that RAPN can provide tumor control while preserving renal tissue in patients with VHL-associated multifocal RCC and a solitary kidney. However, the procedure carries a substantial risk of severe postoperative AKI requiring temporary renal replacement therapy.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Nafamostat Mesilate Injection in Patients Receiving Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: The objective of the study was to assess the efficacy and safety of nafamostat mesilate injection in patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Dichotomous and continuous outcomes were analyzed using fixed-effect or random-effects models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) or mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Eight studies involving 1,189 patients were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with no anticoagulation, nafamostat mesilate injection was associated with lower mortality (OR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.44-0.76; p < 0.001) and longer filter lifespan (MD, 7.00; 95% CI, 1.50-12.50; p = 0.01). These estimates were derived predominantly from nonrandomized studies and should be interpreted with caution. However, no significant difference was found between nafamostat mesilate injection and no anticoagulation in bleeding complications (OR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.51-2.34; p = 0.82), total duration of CRRT (MD, 4.46; 95% CI, -0.13-9.04; p = 0.06), the proportion of patients requiring transfusion (OR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.54-1.03; p = 0.07), and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (MD, -0.24; 95% CI, -3.85-3.37; p = 0.90) in patients receiving CRRT. The available evidence suggests that nafamostat mesilate injection may be associated with lower mortality and longer filter lifespan compared with no anticoagulation in patients receiving CRRT. However, no clear difference was observed in bleeding complications, total duration of CRRT, the proportion of patients requiring transfusion, or ICU length of stay. These findings are limited by the predominance of nonrandomized designs, small numbers of studies, and substantial heterogeneity. Additional adequately powered randomized studies are needed before clinical benefit can be considered established.

articles.title: Maternal Intensive Care Admission, Unplanned Peripartum Hysterectomy, and Breast Milk Feeding by Hospital Discharge: A Population Based Repeated Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract: Characterize trends and factors associated with breast milk feeding among patients undergoing maternal ICU admission or peripartum unplanned hysterectomy. Population-level repeated cross-sectional study. United States National Vital Statistics System data between 2016 and 2023. Liveborn singleton, non-anomalous deliveries from 34 + 0 to 42 + 6 weeks. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression reported as annual average percentage change (AAPC). Multivariable logistic regression models were fit to assess the association between morbidity and breast milk feeding by hospital discharge. Temporal trends in severe morbidity defined as maternal ICU admission and/or unplanned hysterectomy and associated breast milk feeding by hospital discharge. Of the 23 589 073 births included, 33 121 (0.14%) were complicated by severe morbidity. Any severe morbidity increased from 102 to 157 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.1%, 95% CI: 1.3% to 7.2%) with increased hysterectomy only from 15 to 24 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.2%, 95% CI: 0.7% to 8.2%), ICU admission only from 75 to 117 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.5%, 95% CI: 1.5% to 7.8%), and no change in concurrent hysterectomy and ICU admission. Patients with any severe morbidity had lower breast milk feeding by hospital discharge (65.2% vs. 84.1%, adjusted OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.45-0.47). Despite temporal increases in breast milk feeding by hospital discharge for patients without severe morbidity, the same was not seen for those with severe morbidity. These findings identify a population in whom additional support and services would help individuals who wish to breastfeed or provide expressed breast milk, when clinically appropriate.

articles.title: Nocturnal intravenous gamma-hydroxybutyrate and sleep architecture in non-sedated intensive care unit patients: a polysomnographic experience.
Association of Neutrophil-to-Prognostic Nutritional Index Ratio With Prognosis in Critically Ill Patients Undergoing Gastric Procedures.
articles.abstract: Inflammation and malnutrition frequently coexist in critically ill patients, yet single inflammatory or nutritional indices capture only part of this state. We examined how the preoperative neutrophil-to-prognostic nutritional index ratio (NPNI), a composite of both, relates to mortality across follow-up in patients undergoing gastric procedures. We studied 1821 adults in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV database who underwent a gastric procedure. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included 15-d, 30-d, 60-d, 90-d, 1-y, 3-y, and 5-y mortality. Logistic regression, time-window Cox models, and landmark analysis were used to assess the association between NPNI and mortality. Receiver operating characteristic curves were generated to calculate the area under the curve. The signal source of NPNI was explored through interaction analysis between the inflammatory axis (neutrophils) and the nutritional axis (Onodera Prognostic Nutritional Index). Higher NPNI was associated with greater odds of death at every horizon (per 1 standard deviation, odds ratio (OR)in-hospital = 1.24, 95% confidence interval: 1.10-1.40; OR5-y = 1.28, 95% confidence interval: 1.15-1.42). NPNI demonstrated "cross-temporal stability," maintaining significant associations in both the early mortality (0-30 d) and late mortality (30 d-5 y) windows. Time-window analysis revealed that the nutritional axis was associated with early mortality (heart rate = 0.81, P = 0.032), while the inflammatory axis was associated with late mortality (heart rate = 1.13, P < 0.001). The interaction between the two axes was subadditive (relative excess risk due to interaction = -0.32). NPNI showed modest discriminative ability (area under the curve: 0.568), inferior to Simplified Acute Physiology Score II (0.647) and Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score (0.625). Elevated NPNI is an independent risk factor for mortality in critically ill patients undergoing gastric procedures. Its value lies in cross-temporal risk integration rather than discriminative ability.

articles.title: Implementation and Impacts of Maternal and Perinatal Quality Collaboratives across U.S. States: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Maternal and Perinatal Quality Care Collaboratives (M/PQCs) are voluntary state-based initiatives that leverage shared data systems, evidence-based toolkits, and quality improvement science to reduce preventable maternal and infant harm. A scoping review of academic and grey literature was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and registered in Open Science Framework. Seven databases were searched for U.S.-based M/PQC studies published between January 2000 - November 2024, analyzed in 2025. Two independent reviewers screened 456 deduplicated records; 31 met eligibility criteria. Quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by implementation theme and intervention topic. Thirty-one studies spanning 16 states and one national analysis were included. Five themes were identified across two domains. Implementation approaches included: (A) building statewide governance infrastructure; (B) translating evidence into practice through standardized toolkits; and (C) strengthening communication, teamwork, and process outcomes. Impacts included: (D) demonstrated reductions in maternal and birth morbidity, including 45-95% reductions in early elective deliveries, 76-87% improvements in timely hypertension treatment, and national-level reductions in eclampsia and intensive care unit admissions; and (E) expansion of the collaborative mission toward contraceptive access, opioid use disorder care, and racial health equity. M/PQCs function as a form of primary and secondary prevention, institutionalizing evidence-based protocols before obstetric emergencies occur. M/PQCs' evolution from clinical safety bundles toward equity, access, and social determinants signals an expanding mandate. Future initiatives should prioritize disaggregated outcome reporting, health equity frameworks, and inclusion of community birth and outpatient settings to ensure M/PQC gains are equitably distributed.

articles.title: Impact of Showering Methods on Driveline Exit Site Microbiology and Driveline Infection in Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Devices.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Driveline infection (DLI) remains a major complication in patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD). This study evaluated the impact of different showering methods on bacterial colonization at the driveline exit site (DLES) and the incidence of DLI. Patients who underwent LVAD implantation at our institute from 2008 to 2021 were included and classified into two groups: the open group, in which the DLES was exposed and washed with running water, and the covered group, in which the DLES was sealed with a waterproof dressing during showering. The primary outcome was the incidence of DLI within 3 years following hospital discharge. A total of 103 patients were included (the open group, n = 47; the covered group, n = 56). The DLI-free rate was significantly higher in the covered group than the open group (77% vs. 49%; p = 0.003). Pseudomonas aeruginosa was detected less frequently at the DLES, and DLI caused by P. aeruginosa was significantly reduced in the covered group. Multivariate analysis suggested that the open showering method was an independent risk factor for DLI (hazard ratio, 2.816; 95% confidence interval, 1.325-5.984; p = 0.007). The covered showering method was associated with a significantly lower incidence of DLI, particularly infections caused by P. aeruginosa.

articles.title: Cardiac toxicity and dysrhythmias in acute poisoning: a ten-year cohort study.
articles.abstract: Cardiac toxicity is frequently cited as an important cause of morbidity and mortality following acute drug overdose. The true incidence of direct drug related clinically significant cardiac complications and malignant dysrhythmias in more recent toxicology practice remains poorly defined. We aim to determine the frequency, nature, and outcomes of cardiac complications in patients presenting with acute poisoning. We conducted a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained clinical toxicology database over a 10-year period. Patients with acute poisoning managed by a specialist toxicology service were included. Cardiac complications were defined as hypotension (systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg) or a primary cardiac dysrhythmia considered temporally related to the poisoning. Sinus tachycardia was excluded. Demographics, exposures, treatments, and outcomes were extracted. A total of 9,743 poisoning presentations were included. Cardiac complications occurred in 473 patients (4.9%). Hypotension occurred in 368 patients (3.8%), primary dysrhythmias in 164 patients (1.7%), and both hypotension and dysrhythmia in 59 patients (0.6%). Most dysrhythmias were isolated bradycardia (139/164, 85%), commonly associated with clonidine (40%) and beta-blocker/calcium channel blocker poisoning (35%). Only 25 patients (0.3% of all poisoning presentations) developed primary dysrhythmias: atrial dysrhythmias (3), conduction abnormalities/delays (10), ectopic rhythms (5), asystole (1) or ventricular dysrhythmias (6; 0.06%). Malignant ventricular dysrhythmias occurred in six patients and were associated with sotalol, methadone, escitalopram, dothiepin, and nortriptyline poisoning. Twenty-one deaths occurred during the study period, but no death was attributable to a primary dysrhythmia temporally related to poisoning.Discussion: In this large cohort of almost 10,000 poisoning presentations, cardiac complications occurred in approximately one in twenty patients. However, almost 95% of these were either hypotension or isolated bradycardia. Only six patients (0.06%) had ventricular dysrhythmias. Our findings support previous studies demonstrating that clinically significant ventricular dysrhythmias are uncommon among unselected populations presenting with acute poisoning. We found that only a few individual drugs, such as sotalol, methadone, tricyclic antidepressants, and escitalopram, were associated with ventricular dysrhythmias, and that such events were rare overall. Cardiac effects occur in approximately 5% of acute poisoning presentations but are predominantly hypotension or sinus bradycardia. Clinically significant ventricular and supraventricular dysrhythmias are uncommon, occurring in less than 0.3% of cases. Death directly attributable to a primary poisoning-related dysrhythmia is rare.

articles.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90. RESULTS: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group. CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

articles.title: Effects of perfusion-guided permissive hypotension and early vasopressin initiation in adults with septic shock: protocol for a multicentre 2×2 factorial randomised controlled trial in Japanese intensive care units.

Artificial Intelligence-Assisted, Electrocardiogram-Derived, Sequential Rule-Based Decision Tree for Exclusion of Acute Coronary Syndrome as the Etiology of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: After out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), deciding which patients without ST-segment elevation warrant emergency coronary angiography is difficult, as standard electrocardiogram (ECG), troponin, and echocardiography are limited in the early post-arrest window. We aimed to develop a sequential rule-based decision tree to identify post-ROSC patients in whom acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is unlikely to be the arrest etiology. In this single-center retrospective study, adult patients with OHCA were divided into development (2020-2024; n=329) and temporal validation (2025; n=71) cohorts. Post-ROSC 12-lead ECGs were analyzed by a deep-learning platform generating ten digital biomarkers. Five candidate biomarkers were combined into a rhythm-stratified sequential decision tree under a zero false-negative constraint; its performance was compared with that of individual biomarkers and validated in the temporal cohort. The tree classified 171/329 (52.0%) and 32/71 (45.1%) patients in the development and validation cohorts, respectively, as "ACS not likely," with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified at any node. Yield concentrated in the non-shockable subgroup, in which the model excluded 169/261 (64.8%) non-ACS cases (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC], 0.824), outperforming each individual biomarker. In the shockable subgroup, which carries a high pretest probability of ACS, 38/40 patients (95.0%) were retained as "ACS not excluded." A rhythm-stratified, rule-based decision tree combining AI-assisted ECG-derived biomarkers classified approximately half of post-OHCA patients as "ACS not likely" with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified, principally in the non-shockable subgroup. This transparent, bedside-deployable framework warrants prospective multicenter evaluation.

articles.title: Ventilation Monitoring in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Care.
articles.abstract: Adherence to American Heart Association (AHA) ventilation guidelines during cardiac arrest is challenging. Prospective, Before/After quality assurance study determining adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines in adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by Milwaukee County Emergency Medical Services and Kenosha Fire in Wisconsin using (Before) end tidal carbon dioxide [ETCO2] to monitor ventilations - Real BVM Help® applied but blinded versus (After) Real BVM Help®. mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in-target for rate, tidal volume, and both rate and tidal volume. AHA 2020 guidelines were followed. From 9/29/22-12/22/23, 278 patients were entered (148 Before/130 After). Average age: 62.3±16.7 years; 185 (67%) male. Mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in Before/After Groups in-target for rate (47.7±25.1% vs 74.4±24.1% respectively, p<0.0001), tidal volume (15.3±15.4% vs 45.4±23.8% respectively, p<0.0001), and rate and tidal volume (7.5±9.6% vs 39.0±23.3% respectively, p<0.0001) were significantly higher in the After Group. In the Before Group, using ETCO2 to monitor all ventilations (N=22,037 ventilations), only 43.8% were in-target for rate, 13.5% in-target for tidal volume, and 6.8% in-target for rate and tidal volume with a lower-than-target tidal volume delivered in 58.2% of all ventilations. Real BVM Help® was associated with statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines. ETCO2 monitoring failed to approach both rate and tidal volume guideline adherence with a lower-than-target tidal volume being the most common parameter delivered out-of-target (58.2%). Ventilation rate and tidal volume monitoring with real-time feedback should be considered during treatment of cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Early Identification of Recurrent Out-of-hospital Cardiac Arrest Using Clinical ECG Features.
articles.abstract: Recurrent cardiac arrest (rearrest) after initial return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is associated with relatively poor outcomes. Early identification of rearrest might allow for intervention to prevent rearrest. In this study, we sought to determine whether clinical ECG features can predict rearrest. We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients who achieved ROSC between 2018-2024. We evaluated the association of ECG features (QRS width, standard deviation of NN intervals, root mean square of successive NN interval differences, and percentage of NN intervals that differ by more than 50 milliseconds) within individual 15-second segments throughout a 5-minute window prior to rearrest as well as their temporal trends over the 5-minute analytic window. Of the 1,489 OHCA patients achieving ROSC, 1,298 were analyzed; 528 (40.7%) experienced rearrest. Rearrest patients were older, less likely to receive bystander CPR (48.7% vs. 61.9%), and had lower survival (20.4% vs. 43.1%) and favorable neurologic outcomes (7.8% vs. 21.2%; all p<0.001). We found lower heart rate, wider QRS, and higher HR variability in those with rearrest. Identification was highest 1 minute prior to rearrest (AUROC 0.74), declining beyond 3 minutes. Models using temporal trends achieved AUROC 0.67; strongest predictors were heart rate variability measures and QRS width. Established ECG features achieved good prediction for rearrest with identification improving closer to time of rearrest. Future work leveraging novel features or more advanced artificial intelligence models may further improve prediction.

articles.title: Dynamic Early Postreperfusion Physiology Is Associated With Organ Recovery After Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Prognostication after extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) predominantly relies on characteristics available before or at initiation of extracorporeal support. We investigated whether the early metabolic response to extracorporeal reperfusion provides complementary information on subsequent recovery. We retrospectively analyzed 91 patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated with ECPR. Lactate was assessed before and 12 h after extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) initiation. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, successful ECMO weaning, cerebral edema/hypoxic brain injury, and favorable neurological survival. Associations were adjusted for low-flow duration. Twelve hour lactate was lower in survivors than nonsurvivors (5.45 vs. 9.04 mmol/L; p = 0.002), whereas prereperfusion lactate did not differ. In paired measurements (n = 38), mortality discrimination increased from an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.47 before reperfusion to 0.80 at 12 h. Each 5 mmol/L higher 12 h lactate was associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR] = 2.73), lower odds of ECMO weaning (OR = 0.44), and cerebral edema/hypoxic injury (OR = 2.07) after low-flow adjustment. Early metabolic response after extracorporeal reperfusion was associated with survival and both circulatory and cerebral recovery. Dynamic post-reperfusion physiology may provide complementary information beyond static pre-reperfusion assessment.

articles.title: Chlorhexidine within a standardized oral-care bundle for the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia: a pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover trial in six medical intensive care units.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover (AB/BA) trial in six adult medical ICUs of a single tertiary-care academic hospital in Bhubaneswar, India. ICUs were randomized as three ICUs of two Period of 9 months with the multicomponent oral-care bundle without chlorhexidine and three with the same bundle plus 0.12% chlorhexidine with a 1-month wash-in and re-training interval. Consecutive adults ventilated for ≥ 48 h were included. The primary outcome was VAP incidence density (Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) > 6) as per 1,000 ventilator-days. Secondary outcomes were 28-day all-cause mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, 28- day ventilator-free days, Beck Oral Assessment Scale (BOAS) and Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) scores. The primary model was a population-averaged Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) and adjustment for treatment, period, sequence, age, sex, APACHE II, and SOFA. RESULTS: A total of 1,035 patients (637 No CHX, 398 CHX) accrued 10,024 ventilator-days (5,918 vs. 4,106). Groups were well balanced at baseline (mean age ≈ 55 years; APACHE II ≈ 19.6; SOFA ≈ 13.4). VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics of oseltamivir and oseltamivir carboxylate in critically ill adults receiving veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation without renal replacement therapy - an ASAP ECMO study.
articles.abstract: To characterise the population pharmacokinetics of oseltamivir and oseltamivir carboxylate in critically ill adults receiving veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) without renal replacement therapy (RRT), and to compare oseltamivir carboxylate exposure with an exploratory exposure-response threshold and published pharmacokinetic data. This multinational ASAP ECMO analysis included 8 critically ill adults receiving oseltamivir 75 mg every 12 hours during VV-ECMO. Serial blood samples were collected over a dosing interval, and oseltamivir and oseltamivir carboxylate concentrations were measured using a validated assay. Population pharmacokinetic modelling was performed in Monolix using an integrated parent drug-metabolite model. Fifty-eight plasma concentration-time points were available for analysis. The cohort was relatively young and 63% had augmented renal clearance (ARC). A one-compartment model best described both oseltamivir and oseltamivir carboxylate, with a transit compartment required to account for delayed metabolite formation. Median oseltamivir carboxylate exposure was generally comparable to values reported in healthy adults and critically ill patients receiving standard dosing. Median oseltamivir carboxylate area under the concentration-time curve from 0-12 hours (AUC0-12) was lower in patients with ARC than in those without (1877.78 vs. 8253.39 ng·h/mL; p=0.07). Only 2 of 8 patients achieved the primary exploratory exposure-response threshold (AUC0-12 ≥7000 ng∙h/mL) and none of the 5 patients with ARC achieved this threshold. Marked variability and lower exposure were observed in adults receiving VV-ECMO without RRT, particularly ARC patients. Higher doses may be required in ARC patients, but the optimal dosing regimen remains undefined. Routine dose escalation is not supported by current evidence.

articles.title: Pre-ICU medication vulnerability and healthcare-access barriers associated with unplanned intensive care admission among cancer patients: A case-control study.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: BackgroundUnplanned intensive care unit (ICU) admission is a critical event in the cancer trajectory and is associated with substantial mortality. Medication-related vulnerabilities and healthcare-access barriers may contribute to acute deterioration but remain insufficiently studied together.ObjectiveTo identify medication-related and healthcare-access factors independently associated with unplanned ICU admission among adults with cancer.MethodsThis hospital-based case-control study was conducted at a tertiary oncology centre. Cases were adults with cancer with unplanned ICU admission (n = 150), and controls were adults with cancer admitted to wards or day-care units without ICU requirement (n = 150), frequency-matched by age group, sex, and cancer type. Medication vulnerabilities and healthcare-access barriers were assessed using medical records and structured interviews. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).ResultsCases had higher prevalence of polypharmacy (64.0% vs 38.7%), clinically significant drug-drug interactions (42.0% vs 20.7%), and medication non-adherence (51.3% vs 29.3%). Financial barriers (58.7% vs 34.7%) and delayed care-seeking (46.0% vs 24.0%) were also more frequent. After adjustment, financial barriers (aOR 2.31, 95% CI 1.34-3.99), drug-drug interactions (2.14, 1.19-3.85), delayed care-seeking (2.08, 1.16-3.72), polypharmacy (2.05, 1.21-3.47), and non-adherence (1.94, 1.12-3.36) remained independently associated with unplanned ICU admission. ICU mortality was 32.0%.ConclusionMedication vulnerabilities and healthcare-access barriers were associated with unplanned ICU admission. These findings identify potentially modifiable areas for further evaluation, but the case-control design does not establish that interventions targeting these factors would directly reduce ICU admissions.

articles.title: Portable ultra-low field MRI in neurocritical care and intensive care units: A systematic review of diagnostic performance and feasibility.
articles.abstract: To synthesise evidence on the diagnostic performance, safety, feasibility and clinical impact of ultra-low-field portable magnetic resonance imaging (pMRI) in adult neurocritical care and intensive care unit (ICU) populations. PubMed, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 6 February 2026 and supplemented by grey literature and citation searching. We included original English-language studies of adult ICU, neurocritical care or emergency department patients undergoing pMRI at ≤ 0.1 T. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias in diagnostic comparisons was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and feasibility and safety outcomes were appraised narratively. Because of heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. The review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261302014). Eleven studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included, comprising 694 patient participants and 715 patient examinations, plus 40 healthy controls. Cohorts overlapped substantially: six studies came wholly and one partly from a single institution, and one ECMO study was a subset of another. The number of unique patients is therefore estimated at 281 to 677. In the multicentre ECMO study, adverse events occurred in 3 of 50 patients (6%). One was serious: an intra-aortic balloon pump malfunction attributed to electrocardiographic artefact. No adverse events were reported in the other seven independent cohorts that reported safety outcomes, and two studies did not report safety outcomes. For ischaemic stroke, pMRI detected infarction in 45 of 50 patients (90%). By sequence, sensitivity was 100% for FLAIR, 98% for T2-weighted imaging and 86% for diffusion-weighted imaging. Visual DWI-FLAIR mismatch identified patients scanned within 4.5 h with 60% sensitivity, 82% specificity and a 93% negative predictive value. Sensitivity for intracerebral haemorrhage was 80.4% (specificity 96.6%) on initial blinded evaluation. It was 92.1% (specificity 99.3%) in a later cohort in which raters had clinical context and images used deep-learning reconstruction, with lower sensitivity for infratentorial haemorrhage (75.0%). Only one subdural haemorrhage and no extradural haemorrhages were reported. Midline-shift detection showed 93% sensitivity, 96% specificity and a kappa of 0.87. pMRI detected hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury in 12 of 12 affected post-cardiac-arrest patients. In ECMO patients, pMRI detected 8 of 8 ischaemic events, compared with 4 of 8 on head CT, but only 1 of 2 haemorrhages. Up to 28% of examinations were nondiagnostic, mainly because of motion. Ultra-low-field pMRI is a feasible bedside neuroimaging adjunct with a low but non-zero adverse-event rate. It is of particular value for ischaemic injury, midline shift and serial monitoring. Lower and variable sensitivity for haemorrhage, the nonspecificity of FLAIR hyperintensity, overlapping single-institution cohorts and small samples mean that larger multicentre validation studies are needed.

articles.title: Oral colonization patterns according to ventilatory support modality in critically ill patients.
articles.abstract: To evaluate oral colonization patterns according to ventilatory support modality in critically ill patients, with particular emphasis on colonization involving hospital-associated Gram-negative bacilli because of their relevance to healthcare-associated respiratory infections. A cross-sectional study included 120 adults admitted to two intensive care units in Brazil. Participants were equally allocated into three groups according to ventilatory support modality: no invasive ventilation, endotracheal tube, and tracheostomy. Oral samples collected from the dorsal surface of the tongue were analyzed using conventional culture methods. Oral colonization patterns differed significantly according to ventilatory support modality (p < 0.001). Colonization involving hospital-associated Gram-negative bacilli (isolated or mixed) increased progressively from 45.0% among patients without invasive ventilation to 62.5% among those with an endotracheal tube and 92.5% among tracheostomized patients. Conversely, conventional oral microbiota decreased from 40.0% to 25.0% and 5.0%, respectively. Salivary flow patterns also differed significantly among groups (p = 0.047). Increasing invasiveness of ventilatory support was associated with progressive oral colonization involving hospital-associated Gram-negative bacilli and a concomitant reduction in conventional oral microbiota. Although causality cannot be inferred because of the cross-sectional design, the findings support the concept that the oral cavity may serve as a reservoir of respiratory pathogens in critically ill patients. Characterizing oral colonization patterns according to ventilatory support modality may support infection prevention and control programmes by informing risk stratification and evidence-based oral care strategies in intensive care units.

articles.title: Impact of a Nurse-Led, Target-Directed Light Sedation Strategy on the Incidence of Delirium in Septic Patients in the Emergency Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the impact of a nurse-led, target-directed light sedation strategy on delirium incidence and short-term outcomes in septic patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation in the emergency intensive care unit (EICU).MethodsWe analyzed 221 consecutive septic patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation for more than 24 h at a single center (January 2022-May 2024). Based on a sedation protocol change, patients were assigned to conventional sedation group (control, n = 123) or nurse-led, target-directed light sedation group (exposed, n = 98). The primary outcome was delirium incidence. Secondary outcomes included delirium-free days (DFD-28), ventilator-free days (VFD-28), mechanical ventilation duration, EICU length of stay, and 28-day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression examined the independent association between the nurse-led strategy and delirium risk.ResultsDelirium occurred less frequently in the nurse-led sedation group than in the control group (20.4% vs 37.4%, P = .007). The exposed group had shorter mechanical ventilation duration and EICU length of stay (both P < .05), whereas VFD-28 did not differ significantly between groups. The two groups did not differ significantly in 28-day mortality (28.6% vs 26.0%, P = .671) or in the rate of airway-related adverse events. On multivariable analysis, the nurse-led strategy was independently associated with a lower risk of delirium (OR = 0.428, 95% CI: 0.215-0.854, P = .016). Subgroup analyses showed that this protective benefit was consistent across age strata, disease severity levels, and comorbidity burden.ConclusionIn septic patients undergoing mechanical ventilation, a nurse-led, target-directed light sedation strategy was associated with reduced delirium incidence, shorter mechanical ventilation duration, and decreased EICU length of stay, without increasing adverse events. However, no improvement in 28-day mortality was observed. Further validation through multicenter prospective randomized controlled trials is warranted to assess long-term efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Effect of remimazolam versus propofol anaesthesia on postoperative delirium in neurovascular surgery: a randomised noninferiority trial.
articles.abstract: Propofol-based total intravenous anaesthesia (TIVA) is commonly used in neurovascular surgery, in which intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring limits inhalation anaesthetic use. However, propofol causes hypotension, and prolonged infusions can delay emergence. Remimazolam, a benzodiazepine whose effects are reversible with flumazenil, has been associated with less intraoperative hypotension than propofol, but its use raises concerns about postoperative delirium (POD). We tested whether remimazolam-based TIVA is noninferior to propofol-based TIVA for POD. In this single-centre, double-blind, randomised noninferiority trial, adults undergoing elective intracranial aneurysm clipping, arteriovenous malformation resection, microvascular decompression, or superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery bypass received remimazolam-based TIVA with flumazenil reversal at emergence, or propofol-based TIVA, both with remifentanil. The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of POD within 5 days, assessed twice daily with the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-defined delirium (3D-CAM). The prespecified noninferiority margin was 10 percentage points. Among 686 patients in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, POD occurred in 44 of 344 (12.8%) with remimazolam and 37 of 342 (10.8%) with propofol (risk difference, 1.97 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.85 to 6.80; one-sided P<0.001 for noninferiority); per-protocol results were consistent. Hypotensive burden below a mean arterial pressure threshold of 65 mm Hg was lower in the remimazolam group (median, 0 vs 7.5 mm Hg min; P<0.001), and tracheal extubation in the operating room was more frequent (85.2% vs 67.3%). Remimazolam-based TIVA met the prespecified criterion for noninferiority to propofol-based TIVA with respect to postoperative delirium after elective neurovascular surgery. Interpretation should take into account that the observed incidence of postoperative delirium was lower than anticipated when the noninferiority margin was defined. NCT06115031 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

articles.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia after traumatic brain injury: a timing-sensitive ecological framework of neuroimmune-pulmonary vulnerability.
articles.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is frequent after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its biological meaning and outcome impact remain incompletely defined. Traditional models emphasise mechanical ventilation, aspiration, colonisation, endotracheal tube biofilm, and hospital pathogens. These mechanisms remain essential, but they do not fully explain the early clustering, heterogeneous susceptibility, changing bacteriology, and variable mortality effect observed after TBI. Severe brain injury creates an early vulnerable host state through impaired consciousness and airway protection, neuroimmune dysregulation, autonomic and endocrine activation, altered pulmonary immune surveillance, and, in many patients, extracranial trauma, shock, transfusion, or thoracic injury. These processes interact with ventilation, antibiotic pressure, and rapid respiratory microbiome disruption. Early VAP may reflect abrupt loss of control after injury and intubation, whereas late VAP may reflect persistent or secondary failure driven by biofilm maturation, antibiotic selection, multidrug-resistant pathogens, and intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired immune dysfunction. Clinically, VAP consistently prolongs ventilation, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and resource use, while its independent effect on mortality is phenotype- and context-dependent. This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. Future studies should distinguish isolated TBI from polytrauma, compare TBI with other acute brain injuries and non-neurological ventilated populations, and incorporate dynamic immune, microbial, and trajectory-based outcomes. VAP after TBI should be viewed as a timing-sensitive interaction between ventilator exposure and early host vulnerability, not as a distinct disease entity or as a pneumonia pathway unique to traumatic brain injury. The TBI-focused contribution lies in the early convergence of otherwise non-unique mechanisms: impaired airway control, aspiration risk, neuroimmune-endocrine activation, treatment exposure, dysbiosis, and extracranial injury burden, rather than in any single TBI-specific mechanism. Isolated TBI and TBI with polytrauma are biologically different phenotypes and should be separated in future studies. Early and late VAP may represent different phases of loss of pulmonary host-microbe containment; this distinction is probabilistic rather than TBI-specific in itself and requires validation in TBI-stratified cohorts. Mortality remains clinically relevant but context-dependent; VAP more consistently modifies recovery trajectory, ventilator dependence, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and possibly neurological recovery.

articles.title: Consensus-derived clinical sepsis profiles and mortality across six international cohorts.
articles.abstract: Clinical phenotyping may help characterize sepsis heterogeneity, but the applicability of derived profiles across healthcare settings remains uncertain. We evaluated consensus-derived clinical profiles and their associations with mortality across six international cohorts. We analyzed 62,458 adults from six critical care databases in four countries. In the MIMIC-IV discovery cohort (n = 28,733), six clustering algorithms were applied to 24 routinely available clinical variables to derive consensus profiles. The profiles were assigned in five external cohorts using fixed discovery-cohort templates. We examined clinical characteristics, mortality associations, and exploratory treatment-outcome associations. Three profiles were selected based on the Calinski-Harabasz peak and clinical interpretability. Profiles 1, 2, and 3 comprised 32.6%, 20.0%, and 47.4% of the discovery cohort, with in-hospital mortality of 30.3%, 13.8%, and 9.3%, respectively. Profile 1 showed greater multiorgan dysfunction, Profile 2 relatively preserved hemodynamics, and Profile 3 greater ventilatory support with less extrapulmonary dysfunction. Profile 1 had the highest mortality in all five external cohorts, with a decreasing mortality gradient across profiles in most cohorts. After adjustment for age and SOFA score, Profile 3 was associated with lower 1-year mortality than Profile 1 (hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.57-0.67). Treatment-outcome associations were exploratory. Consensus-derived profiles characterized clinically interpretable patterns of sepsis heterogeneity with mortality differences across the evaluated cohorts. These findings support further evaluation of clinical profiling for risk stratification and phenotype-informed research.

articles.title: Bacterial epidemiology and attributable mortality of Ventilator-associated pneumonia before and after COVID-19 pandemic (2018-2021).
articles.abstract: BackgroundVentilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in mechanically ventilated patients. The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly modified VAP epidemiology and microbial ecology.MethodsWe conducted a prospective multicenter cohort study within the REA-REZO network (≈20% of French ICU beds), 1 January 2018-31 December 2021. All adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation were included. VAP was defined according to ECDC criteria. Primary endpoints were VAP incidence density (per 1000 ventilation-days) and 30-day attributable mortality. Secondary endpoints included resistance patterns and pre-pandemic versus pandemic trends.ResultsAmong 98,047 patients, 12,251 patients developed VAP, with an incidence of 18.9/1000 ventilation-days. Peak incidence occurred at day 10 (29/1000 ventilation-days). Thirty-day attributable mortality was 4.9% [95% CI 3.7;6.2], rising to 7.2% [6.0;8.5] at 60 days. Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 78.0% of isolates, predominantly Enterobacterales (46%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (20%). Third-generation cephalosporin resistance reached 27% in Enterobacterales and 25% in P. aeruginosa. The COVID-19 patients had a higher VAP rate (19.5% vs 9.7%, p<0.001) and mortality (36.9% vs 31.0%, p<0.001).ConclusionsVAP remains highly prevalent in French ICUs with substantial attributable mortality. The COVID-19 pandemic nearly doubled VAP incidence and worsened resistance profiles. Intensified prevention bundles during the first 10 days of ventilation and reinforced antimicrobial stewardship are critical.

articles.title: Predictors of severe measles outcomes in hospitalized patients in Jerusalem, 2025.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract: Measles is a vaccine-preventable disease. Defining risk factors for poor outcomes in hospitalized patients can improve future measles outbreak preparedness. Data were collected on all confirmed measles cases that were evaluated at one of the emergency departments (ED) in the three main hospitals in Jerusalem from the first reported case of the current outbreak on April 10th to December 31st, 2025. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed using robust Poisson multivariable models to calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR) for hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and death. Among 786 individuals who visited the ED with confirmed measles, the rates of hospital admission (≥1 day), ICU, ECMO and death were 83.4%, 6.4%, 0.8%, and 1.4%, respectively. Complete data were available for 567 patients, of whom 303 (53.4%) were males. Median age was 2.1 years (IQR 1.2-3.8), and 474 (83.6%) were younger than 5 years. Most patients were unvaccinated (91.0%). Secondary infections were frequent, including lobar pneumonia (28.7%) and community-acquired bacteremia (3.5%). Respiratory support and severe dehydration were associated with hospital admission (IRR 1.4, 95% CI 1.3-1.5; p<0.001 and 9.5, 4.8-18.4; p<0.001, respectively) and ICU admission (IRR 1.3, 1.2-1.4; p<0.001 and 5.2, 2.1-12.4; p<0.001, respectively). Community-acquired bacteremia was associated with death or ECMO (IRR 44.5, 12.5-158.6; p<0.001). Despite high access to medical care in this urban setting, measles caused substantial morbidity and mortality. Respiratory compromise, severe dehydration, and bacteremia identified patients at increased risk of severe outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond 28-Day Mortality: The Unfinished Story of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Survivorship.
Impact of burst suppression duration on delirium and its diagnostic value in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) delirium affects up to 50% of mechanically ventilated patients. This condition is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Although bispectral index (BIS) monitoring is widely used for sedation assessment, its predictive value for delirium remains limited. Burst suppression (BS) is an electroencephalographic pattern reflecting profound cerebral dysfunction. BS has been proposed as a predictor of delirium. However, the quantitative role of burst suppression duration (BSD) in delirium risk stratification has not been established. This prospective observational study enrolled 300 mechanically ventilated adult ICU patients between April 2021 and October 2024 at Harrison International Peace Hospital. Continuous video-electroencephalogram (vEEG) monitoring was performed. BSD was quantified from the vEEG recordings. Delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU). Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of BSD. Among 300 patients, 130 (43.3%) developed delirium. The delirium group had significantly longer BSD than the control group (median 81.1 s, IQR 41.5-148.5 vs. 17.2 s, IQR 5.8-32.9; P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified BSD (adjusted OR = 1.018, 95% CI 1.012-1.023; P < 0.001), BIS (adjusted OR = 0.964, 95% CI 0.946-0.982; P < 0.001), age (adjusted OR = 1.024, 95% CI 1.002-1.047; P = 0.031), and hypertension (adjusted OR = 1.748, 95% CI 1.002-3.051; P = 0.049) as independent risk factors. ROC analysis demonstrated that BSD achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.871 (95% CI 0.829-0.913). The optimal cutoff of 41.5 s yielded a sensitivity of 80.8% and a specificity of 78.2%. The combination of BSD and BIS improved the AUC to 0.914 (95% CI 0.882-0.946). BSD is an independent risk factor for delirium in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. It demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy as a quantitative biomarker. The combination of BSD and BIS provides superior predictive performance. This combined approach offers a practical quantitative tool for early delirium risk stratification.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine versus propofol for the prevention of postoperative delirium in older adults undergoing regional anaesthesia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
articles.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common complication in older adults undergoing surgery and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. The choice of intraoperative sedative may influence its occurrence, particularly in the setting of regional anesthesia. A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing dexmedetomidine versus propofol in patients aged ≥60 years was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines, with protocol registration in PROSPERO. The primary outcome was the incidence of POD assessed using validated instruments (CAM or CAM-ICU). Five randomized controlled trials involving a total of 1,613 patients were included. The incidence of POD was 7.7% in the dexmedetomidine groups and 16.7% in the propofol groups. The meta-analysis showed a significant reduction in POD with dexmedetomidine (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.36-0.64; p < 0.001), with low heterogeneity (I² = 13.4%).
