Egger's test did not show significant evidence of publication bias, and trial sequential analysis suggested that the available evidence is sufficient. The certainty of evidence was rated as moderate according to the GRADE approach. In older adults undergoing surgery under regional anesthesia, intraoperative sedation with dexmedetomidine is associated with a lower incidence of POD compared with propofol.

articles.title: Dysnatremia in critically ill burn patients: incidence, timing and association with kidney outcomes.
articles.abstract: Dysnatremia is common in critically ill patients and has been linked to poor outcomes and renal prognosis. Burn patients are particularly vulnerable, but the prognostic significance of dysnatremia in this population remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 1,758 burn patients admitted to a French burn center between 2011 and 2023. Dysnatremia was defined as at least one episode of hyponatremia (<135 mmol/L) or hypernatremia (>145 mmol/L) during intensive care unit (ICU) stay. The primary endpoint was the incidence of dysnatremia; secondary endpoints included major adverse kidney events (MAKE) at ICU discharge and acute kidney injury (AKI) occurrence and severity. Dysnatremia occurred in 56.3% of patients (n = 990), with hyponatremia in 50.5% (n = 888) and hypernatremia in 23.8% (n = 418). MAKE at ICU discharge did not differ between hyponatremic and normonatremic patients (12.6% vs. 10.9%, p = 0.304) but was sixfold higher with hypernatremia (32.3% vs. 5.4%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and burned total body surface area, hypernatremia was independently associated with MAKE at ICU discharge (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 4.03; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.92-5.56; p < 0.001), whereas hyponatremia was not (aHR 1.15; 95% CI: 0.85-1.55; p = 0.377). Clustering analysis identified three phenotypes: Cluster B (severe burns, worst outcomes), Cluster A (older patients, mostly hyponatremic, intermediate outcomes), and Cluster C (younger patients, mild burns, best outcomes). Dysnatremia affects over half of burn patients. Sodium disturbances should be viewed as markers of systemic severity, warranting close monitoring and preventive strategies.

articles.title: Association between intracatheter Ca²(+) trajectory and extracorporeal circuit coagulation in unplanned early withdrawal among patients receiving CRRT: a retrospective cohort study.
Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID). SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles. In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

articles.title: SEPSIS-INDUCED COAGULOPATHY ATTENUATES THE PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF THE HEMOGLOBIN-ALBUMIN-LYMPHOCYTE-PLATELET (HALP) SCORE IN SEPSIS.
articles.abstract: The hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score predicts outcomes in sepsis, but its platelet denominator is also a core component of sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC), and may distort its prognostic meaning. We examined whether SIC modifies HALP's association with 28-day mortality. We analyzed 6,218 adults meeting Sepsis-3 criteria in MIMIC-IV. HALP was calculated from first ICU measurements; SIC was defined by the 2017 ISTH criteria (score ≥4). Analyses included multivariable regression, interaction testing, propensity-score methods, and platelet-independent coagulopathy definitions, and evaluation of modified HALP (m-HALP; platelets in the numerator). Twenty-eight-day mortality was 25.6%; SIC incidence was 26.1%. HALP showed a J-shaped association with mortality (P for nonlinearity <0.001). The lowest quartile independently predicted death (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.20-1.70; HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.10-1.39). This association persisted in non-SIC patients (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.28-1.79) but was attenuated and non-significant in SIC patients (OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.82-1.60; interaction P=0.006). Albumin carried HALP's discrimination in non-SIC patients, whereas platelets dominated in SIC (OR 0.51 per SD, P=0.001). When coagulopathy was redefined without platelets, the modification was no longer significant (P=0.295), indicating it partly reflects the shared platelet component. m-HALP was inversely associated with mortality in both strata (interaction P=0.691). Results were robust to weighting, 90-day mortality, and alternative Cox models. HALP is an independent prognostic marker mainly in septic patients without coagulopathy; once SIC develops, thrombocytopenia both raises mortality risk and arithmetically inflates HALP. Coagulation status should be assessed before HALP-based risk stratification; m-HALP may offer a platelet-consistent alternative.

articles.title: Quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly reveals a non-linear association with 30-day mortality in sepsis: a proof-of-concept pilot study.
articles.abstract: Direct, cell-resolved quantification of NLRP3 inflammasome activation in clinical patients has not been feasible. Previous studies have relied on indirect surrogates such as downstream cytokines, which are influenced by inflammasome-independent pathways and systemic clearance kinetics, potentially explaining the inconsistent prognostic findings reported in the literature. We applied a proximity ligation assay (PLA) to directly visualise NLRP3-caspase-1 complex formation in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of septic patients, providing a cell-specific, in situ readout of inflammasome assembly at the single-cell level. In this prospective, multicentre proof-of-concept pilot study, 78 patients fulfilling Sepsis-3 criteria were enrolled across three university hospitals. The PLA was validated in THP-1-derived macrophages against established readouts of canonical inflammasome activation prior to clinical application. Patients were stratified into low (n = 28), intermediate (n = 23), and high (n = 27) NLRP3 inflammasome activity groups. Median age was 64 years (IQR: 56-78), 63% were male, and median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score was 8 (IQR: 4-12). Baseline characteristics, disease severity scores, and routine inflammatory biomarkers did not differ across activity groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed a non-linear pattern of 30-day survival, with the most favourable outcomes in the intermediate activity group. Both low and high activity were associated with increased mortality (log-rank p = 0.003). In adjusted Cox regression, low inflammasome activity (HR 7.88, 95% CI 1.79-34.65; p = 0.006) and high inflammasome activity (HR 4.35, 95% CI 1.01-19.88; p = 0.048) remained associated with 30-day mortality. Modelling PLA activity as a continuous variable using restricted cubic splines confirmed a significant non-linear association with 30-day mortality, independent of the tertile-based categorisation (p for non-linearity = 0.015). This proof-of-concept pilot study demonstrates that direct in situ quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly is feasible in septic patients and reveals a non-linear association with 30-day survival. These findings indicate that PLA-based profiling captures immune heterogeneity beyond routine inflammatory biomarkers. Larger independent cohorts are needed to validate these findings before clinical application or patient stratification can be considered.

articles.title: Candida Septic Shock: If Every Hour Matters, Who Requires Empiric Therapy?

Data Stream and Hospital-Level Variation in Intensive Care Unit Vital-Sign Record Density Across Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV and eICU Collaborative Research Database: Retrospective Data Quality Study.
articles.abstract: Electronic health record-derived process measures such as vital-sign record density are used for quality monitoring, risk prediction, and cross-system benchmarking, but whether they retain consistent meaning across sites and data streams is rarely tested. This study aimed to determine whether vital-sign record density varies primarily by data stream, database, contributing site, or care unit, and what follows for comparative use. We retrospectively analyzed the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1 and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) version 2.0. Record density and timing metrics were computed for the first 24 intensive care unit hours from nurse-charted streams and, in eICU-CRD, from the monitor stream. Heart rate was primary; oxygen saturation and respiratory rate were replication variables. Variance was decomposed by database, hospital, and unit using η2 with hospital-clustered bootstrap inference and mixed-effects sensitivity analyses. A hospital-level plausibility floor of 12 nurse-charted heart rate observations per 24 hours was applied for the principal analysis; unrestricted and alternative-floor analyses are reported as sensitivities. A pooled-item MIMIC-IV heart rate count included alarm-limit documentation events, so label-based pooling mixes the two. In 117,572 eICU-CRD stays present in both streams, nurse- and monitor-derived counts were almost unrelated (Spearman ρ=0.024), with bottom-decile overlap at chance. Between-database η2 for record count was 0.960 against the eICU monitor stream and 0.026 against the nurse stream. Eight of 68 eICU-CRD hospitals fell below the plausibility floor and were excluded from principal estimates, a restriction introduced during review. Among the remaining 60 hospitals (88,560 stays), hospital η2 for record count was 0.354 (95% CI 0.259-0.450) against unit-within-hospital η2 of 0.043; for the interval-structure metrics, the hospital and unit components were not separable. For record count, the hospital component fell from 0.441 unrestricted to 0.321 at an hourly floor. A negative-binomial mixed model gave latent-scale hospital and unit variance-partition coefficients of 0.348 (95% CI 0.252-0.457) and 0.112 (0.078-0.163), equivalent to 0.318 and 0.110 observed. A pooled bottom-decile rule agreed with hospital-specific rules on 52.5% (4726/9006) of flagged stays, with 6 hospitals supplying half the pooled decile. The hospital component for record count replicated at 0.322 for oxygen saturation and 0.333 for respiratory rate. Within a multisite nurse-charted stream, vital-sign record volume varied more across contributing sites than across care units within hospitals; for the interval-structure metrics, the site and unit components were not separable at this cohort size. Apparent cross-database differences were reproduced by source-table choice, and site-level variation remained after excluding the most evident contribution-completeness outliers. Comparative use therefore requires specifying the generating stream, enforcing the analytic window, and explicitly modeling site-level variation; the residual site component should not be interpreted as documentation practice alone.

articles.title: 24-hour risk updating for major ICU complications after severe trauma: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Conventional trauma prognostic models rely primarily on admission data and cannot account for subsequent physiological response to treatment. We evaluated whether routinely collected physiological information available at 24 h provides incremental prognostic information for major intensive care unit (ICU) complications in severely injured patients. We conducted a prospective cohort of adults with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score [ISS] ≥ 15) admitted to the ICU between January 2024 and April 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of major respiratory, hemodynamic, renal, or septic complications during the ICU course. TRISS was compared with an admission ridge model incorporating ISS, Glasgow Coma Scale, hemoglobin, lactate, and international normalized ratio, and a 24-h updated ridge model additionally incorporating 24-h lactate and change in creatinine. Performance was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Among 109 patients, median ISS was 29 (IQR 20-38), and 73 (67.0%) developed major ICU complications. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 for TRISS, 0.873 for the admission model, and 0.887 for the 24-h updated model; Brier scores were 0.178, 0.140, and 0.131. Compared with the admission model, the 24-h updated model improved performance (ΔAUC 0.016, 95% bootstrap interval 0.004-0.030; ΔBrier - 0.010, - 0.017 to - 0.005). Twenty-four-hour lactate and creatinine change were the strongest contributors to the update. In severely injured ICU patients, incorporating physiological evolution during the first 24 h refined admission-based prognostic assessment. Lactate and creatinine trajectories provided incremental information for major ICU complications during the ICU course. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Attitudes, beliefs and perceptions of healthcare professionals regarding the role of physiotherapy in the management of critically ill patients in Intensive Care Units in Castilla-La Mancha.
Candidozyma auris in intensive care units: A point prevalence study and six-month colonization-infection surveillance.
articles.journal: International microbiology : the official journal of the Spanish Society for Microbiology
articles.abstract: Candidozyma auris has emerged as a globally significant nosocomial pathogen due to its multidrug antifungal resistance, environmental persistence, and high mortality rates. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of C. auris colonization through a point prevalence screening in the intensive care units (ICUs) of our hospital and to evaluate colonization and infection outcomes during a subsequent six-month follow-up period. The present study aimed to evaluate C. auris colonization rates through point prevalence screening in the ICUs of our hospital, to assess colonization and infection outcomes during a subsequent six-month follow-up period, and to establish a diagnostic algorithm for C. auris identification in our laboratory. Following the detection of an index C. auris case in our hospital in February 2025, a point prevalence study was conducted in all ICUs. Composite swab samples (bilateral axilla and groin) were obtained from hospitalized patients on the same day. In addition, urine and wound cultures were collected from eligible patients. Isolates were identified using chromogenic media, conventional microbiological methods, and MALDI-TOF MS. After the point prevalence study, surveillance for colonization and bloodstream infection was performed over a six-month period. C. auris colonization was detected in 7 of 70 ICU patients (10%) based on composite swab samples. During the six-month follow-up, colonization was identified in 15 patients, and C. auris fungemia developed in nine patients. All patients with positive blood cultures died. The most frequently identified risk factors were broad-spectrum antibiotic use, prolonged ICU stay, and the presence of urinary catheters. Our findings demonstrate that C. auris colonization can be detected at a high rate in ICUs and that severe invasive infections may develop following colonization. Early diagnosis, active screening strategies, and effective infection control measures are critical for reducing C. auris-associated morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Diagnosis: the forgotten ICU procedure.
Maternity versus non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: Substantial uncertainty exists regarding how healthcare system factors, especially care setting types, affect the uptake and implementation of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy screening in practice. Evidence suggests that the care environment may influence diagnostic processes. To assess the effectiveness of maternity and non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus or diabetes in pregnancy. We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL) for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) up to April 2026, and for controlled non-randomised studies of interventions (NRSIs) up to December 2025. We also searched CENTRAL to identify ongoing trials. We included RCTs and planned to include cluster-RCTs and NRSIs, but we did not find any. Eligible participants were pregnant women being screened for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) or diabetes in pregnancy. We defined maternity healthcare settings as those specialising in care for pregnant, birthing, and postpartum individuals, with appropriate screening protocols, and non-maternity healthcare settings as general medical environments lacking a focus on pregnancy and women's care. We considered any screening format (e.g. risk-factor-based screening) and any diagnostic test (e.g. one- and two-step oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT)). Critical health service outcomes were compliance with screening and follow-up guidelines, diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy, maternal emergency department visits during pregnancy, maternal antenatal hospitalisation, length of maternal hospitalisation, length of neonatal hospitalisation, and care accessibility. Critical maternal outcomes included hypertensive disorders, maternal death, intensive care admissions, hyperglycaemia requiring pharmacological treatment, infections, and postpartum glucose intolerance, including progression to diabetes, within 15 years after birth. Critical child-related outcomes encompassed perinatal death, neonatal intensive care admissions, preterm birth, neonatal hypoglycaemia, large-for-gestational-age, shoulder dystocia, and birth trauma. Further critical and important outcomes not included in the summary of findings tables can be found in the full text. We used the Cochrane RoB 2 tool to assess bias in the RCTs. We had planned to use ROBINS-I version 2 to assess bias in the NRSIs if we had identified any. We used standard Cochrane methodology. We planned to synthesise results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible (inverse-variance or Mantel-Haenszel approaches; fixed-effect model). We used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence for each outcome. We included one RCT with 781 participants: 390 were randomised to screening in a maternity healthcare setting and 391 were randomised to screening in a non-maternity healthcare setting. Except for screening compliance, trialists evaluated all outcomes using a per-protocol analysis instead of by original randomised groups. This approach created substantial disparities in sample sizes between settings and largely nullified the methodological protections typically provided by a randomised design. The trial evaluated screening for GDM only. We did not identify any ongoing studies or studies awaiting classification. Health service outcomes Screening in a maternity healthcare setting may increase compliance with screening and follow-up guidelines (risk ratio (RR) 1.69, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.53 to 1.87; 781 participants) and may improve care accessibility, assessed as time to access antenatal diabetes care, measured in days (mean difference (MD) -4.70, 95% CI -6.03 to -3.37; 690 participants), both with low-certainty evidence. We are very uncertain about the effect of screening in a maternity healthcare setting versus a non-maternity healthcare setting on diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy (RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.60 to 2.01; 690 participants; very low-certainty evidence) and length of neonatal hospitalisation (MD 0.04, 95% CI -0.57 to 0.65; 690 participants; very low-certainty evidence). No direct evidence was available on screening for diabetes in pregnancy as distinct from GDM. No data were reported on maternal emergency department visits, maternal antenatal hospitalisation, length of maternal hospitalisations, and costs. Maternal outcomes We are very uncertain about the effect of screening in a maternity healthcare setting versus a non-maternity healthcare setting on pre-eclampsia (RR 1.24, 95% CI 0.56 to 2.75; 690 participants; very low-certainty evidence). The following outcomes were not reported: eclampsia, HELLP syndrome, maternal death, admission to intensive care, hyperglycaemia requiring pharmacological treatment, infections, and postpartum glucose intolerance. Child-related outcomes We are very uncertain about the effect of screening in a maternity healthcare setting versus a non-maternity healthcare setting on: stillbirth or foetal death (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.08 to 9.93), admission to neonatal intensive care (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.59 to 1.71), preterm birth (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.41 to 2.71), neonatal hypoglycaemia (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.23 to 3.59), large-for-gestational-age (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.51 to 1.04), shoulder dystocia (RR 0.15, 95% CI 0.01 to 3.70), and birth trauma (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.08 to 9.93), all with 690 participants each and very low-certainty evidence. An effect estimate for neonatal death was not estimable (maternity setting: 0/475; non-maternity setting: 0/215). There is insufficient evidence to determine whether screening for gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy in maternity healthcare settings compared with non-maternity healthcare settings improves health service, maternal, or child-related outcomes. Low-certainty evidence from a single study indicates that screening in maternity healthcare settings may result in a reduction in time to access antenatal diabetes care and may increase compliance. The effects on other outcomes remain unknown. Conducting studies using intention-to-treat analyses could bridge existing research gaps, enhancing effect estimates and certainty. This Cochrane review was funded by the World Health Organization (WHO) and the UNDP-UNFPA-UNICEF-WHO-World Bank Special Programme of Research, Development and Research Training in Human Reproduction (HRP). Protocol available via PROSPERO: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251108692.

articles.title: Family suffering after critical illness: understanding buffers and stressors.
Traumatic Emergency Thoracotomy for Resuscitation in Shock (TETRiS): a national service evaluation of resuscitative thoracotomy practice outside the operating theatre.
articles.abstract: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse. Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings. Prospective 12-month observational study across 20 UK Helicopter Emergency Medical Services and 26 Major Trauma Centre Emergency Departments, using the PHOTON, TERN, and NaTRIC research networks. A total of 116 patients underwent RT, of which 82 (70.7%) were performed prehospital. Median age was 30 years, 97 patients (83.6%) were male, and 81 (69.8%) sustained penetrating injury. Suspected cardiac tamponade was the most common indication for RT (72/116 [62.1%]), although operative findings demonstrated exsanguinating haemorrhage in 82 patients (70.7%). Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest. In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

articles.title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation as rescue therapy for patients with suspected high-risk pulmonary embolism: A multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: For patients with suspected high-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) who cannot undergo computed tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) because of unstable hemodynamics, the optimal strategy, namely, prioritizing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or revascularization, remains unclear. This study investigated whether prioritizing ECMO is associated with increased survival rates. A total of 117 patients with suspected high-risk PE admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) at four ECMO centers were retrospectively enrolled (2013-2024). Among these patients, 79 received ECMO (ECMO group), whereas 38 underwent thrombolysis therapy (thrombolysis group). The baseline and preintervention management characteristics were comparable between the groups. In-hospital mortality was lower in the ECMO group than in the thrombolysis group (33/79, 41.8% vs 22/38, 57.9%), although the difference was not significant (P = 0.15). Multivariate Cox analysis revealed that treatment with ECMO was associated with a reduced risk of in-hospital mortality (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.45, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.79, P = 0.006). An elevated pretreatment Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score was identified as an independent risk factor for mortality (HR = 1.14, 95% CI 1.06-1.22, P < 0.001). Kaplan‒Meier curves and log-rank tests revealed better 28-day survival in the ECMO group than in the thrombolysis group (P = 0.041). Among the 79 patients who received ECMO, 63 had CTPA-verified high-risk PE, with 34 surviving to discharge (34/63, 54.0%). For hemodynamically unstable patients with suspected high-risk PE, prioritizing ECMO is a safe strategy that serves as an independent protective factor against in-hospital mortality, despite nonsignificant findings in unadjusted analyses. Larger studies are warranted to validate these results.

articles.title: Adjunctive therapeutic plasma exchange as rescue therapy in septic shock due to streptococcal infection: a multicentric retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Septic shock due to streptococcal infection (SRSS) carries a high mortality and is in part driven by toxin-mediated inflammation. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) may modulate the septic host responses by removing injurious mediators while replenishing protective plasma factors, but data specific to SRSS is lacking. We performed a retrospective, multicenter, cohort study of adults with SRSS between 2012-2024. Patients from three tertiary care ECMO centers in Germany and Switzerland were included requiring (i) streptococcal spp. detected in blood or primary focus and (ii) septic shock according to sepsis-3 definition. Adjunctive TPE with fresh frozen plasma at the intensivists` discretion was compared with standard of care (SOC). The primary outcome was 90-day-hospital mortality. Key exploratory outcomes included 24-h kinetics of vasoactive-inotropic score(VIS) and lactate, as well as SRSS-related complications. Results were validated in a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort. Of 149 patients, 31 (20.8%) received TPE and 118 (79.2%) SOC. TPE patients were more severely ill at baseline: SOFA 14 (IQR 13.5-15) vs 11 (IQR 8-14) (p<0.001); lactate 6.4 vs 2.8 mmol/L (p<0.001); Vasoactive-Inotropic-Score (VIS) 70.7 vs 23.3 (p<0.001); more frequent invasive ventilation (87% vs 65%), VV-ECMO (36% vs 19%), and renal replacement therapy (96.8% vs 52.5%). Overall, 90-day hospital mortality was 27.5% (TPE 29.0%, SOC 27.1%). Following SOFA-score adjustment, TPE was associated with lower mortality risk (aHR 0.67 [95% CI 0.5-0.9]; p=0.009). This was validated in the PSM cohort, with an aHR for TPE of 0.44 (95% CI 0.3-0.8); p=0.002. Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant VIS reduction only with TPE (fixed effect 24-h change, p=0.027) and improved lactate decrease versus SOC. In SRSS, adjunctive TPE was associated with rapid hemodynamic stabilization and improved lactate kinetics. Exploratory adjusted survival analyses support prospective evaluation of TPE in SRSS.

articles.title: Early echocardiographic hemodynamic phenotypes and clinical outcomes in congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
articles.abstract: Early postnatal hemodynamic adaptation may contribute to outcome heterogeneity in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). We evaluated whether echocardiography-defined hemodynamic phenotypes within 24 h of birth were associated with cardiorespiratory severity and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) or death. This retrospective cohort included infants with CDH admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit from 2021 to 2025 who underwent echocardiography within 24 h. Phenotypes were classified as no/mild pulmonary hypertension (PH), right ventricular (RV)-predominant PH, or left ventricular (LV)-involved PH based on ventricular function and ductal/atrial shunt direction. Associations with prenatal severity, respiratory indices, and ECMO or death were assessed. Among 66 infants, 21 had no/mild PH, 22 RV-predominant PH, and 23 LV-involved PH. ECMO or death occurred in 0%, 27.3%, and 65.2%, respectively (P < 0.001). Compared with RV-predominant PH, LV-involved PH was associated with greater respiratory severity and more frequent LV dysfunction; observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (O/E LHR) did not differ significantly between these two groups. Ordinal phenotype severity remained associated with ECMO or death after adjustment for O/E LHR (odds ratio (OR), 5.98; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.76-20.31; P = 0.004). However, the comparison between LV-involved and RV-predominant PH was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for O/E LHR (OR, 3.42; 95% CI, 0.87-15.10). Early hemodynamic phenotype was associated with cardiorespiratory severity and ECMO or death in CDH. LV-involved PH identified a high-risk phenotype and may complement prenatal anatomic risk stratification, although its independent prognostic value beyond prenatal lung size requires validation. • Prenatal lung size and liver herniation are established markers of disease severity and outcome in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). • Pulmonary hypertension and ventricular dysfunction contribute substantially to early cardiorespiratory instability and adverse outcomes in infants with CDH. • Early echocardiographic phenotypes were associated with cardiorespiratory severity and ECMO or death. • LV-involved PH identified a high-risk phenotype, although its prognostic value beyond prenatal severity remains uncertain.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of the Delta Neutrophil Index for Predicting 28-Day Mortality in Intensive Care Unit Patients with Candidemia.
articles.abstract: Candidemia is associated with substantial mortality in critically ill patients, and early identification of patients at increased risk of death remains challenging. The delta neutrophil index (DNI), an automated hematological parameter reflecting circulating immature granulocytes, has been proposed as a prognostic marker in sepsis, but its role in candidemia remains unclear. This retrospective study included adults who developed candidemia during intensive care unit hospitalization between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2023; patients with neutropenia, haematological malignancy receiving ongoing chemotherapy, or granulocyte colony-stimulating factor therapy were excluded. Patients were classified as survivors or non-survivors according to 28-day all-cause mortality after blood culture collection. DNI, leukocyte count, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin were evaluated 24 hours before, at the time of, and 24 hours after blood culture collection. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with mortality, and receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed the prognostic performance of DNI. Among 246 patients, 132 survived and 114 died. Non-survivors had higher APACHE II scores and more frequent acute kidney injury. DNI and procalcitonin levels were significantly higher in non-survivors at all three time points. In the primary multivariable model, acute kidney injury, DNI at blood culture collection, and procalcitonin at blood culture collection were independently associated with mortality; the association of DNI was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after further adjustment for Candida species and antifungal therapy. DNI showed limited discrimination, with area under the curve values ranging from 0.608 to 0.625; the highest value was observed at blood culture collection (0.625), with a cutoff of 2.4, 43.0% sensitivity, and 82.6% specificity. DNI may aid mortality risk stratification in candidemia but should not be used as a standalone prognostic marker.

articles.title: Resting Energy Expenditure in Mechanically Ventilated Surgical-Trauma Patients With and Without Acute Kidney Injury: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: To compare resting energy expenditure (REE) measured by indirect calorimetry (IC) in mechanically ventilated surgical-trauma critically ill patients with and without acute kidney injury (AKI); to evaluate differences in REE by sex, age, and body mass index (BMI); and to assess associations between REE, psoas muscle index (PMI) measured using computed tomography scans, and lean body mass (LBM) estimated by predictive equations. This single-center retrospective cohort study conducted at a tertiary academic medical center included mechanically ventilated critically ill adults admitted between 01/01/2012 and 12/31/2023. Exclusion criteria were pediatric, pregnant, or incarcerated patients; quadriplegia, paraplegia, cystic fibrosis; abnormal respiratory quotients; Medical ICU admission; major burns (≥20% TBSA); parenteral nutrition initiated on or after IC; tracheostomy on admission; discharge or death while ventilated; or absence of a nutrition prescription. Of 794 patients screened, 180 met inclusion criteria (AKI n=84; no AKI n=96). At baseline, patients with and without AKI differed significantly in age (59.9 vs 55 years; P = 0.046), BMI (32.2 vs 28.8 kg/m2; P = 0.046), CKD (23.8% vs 3.13%; P < 0.001), and serum creatinine (1.49 vs 0.84 mg/dL; P < 0.001). Of patients with AKI, 71.4% had stage I AKI and 20.2% required renal replacement therapy (RRT). No significant difference in mean REE was observed between patients with and without AKI (1,642 vs 1,665 kcal/day; P = 0.380) . REE was significantly higher in males compared with females (1,806 vs 1,425 kcal/day; P < 0.001), in patients aged 18-65 versus >65 years (1,768 vs 1,428 kcal/day; P = 0.002), and in obese versus non-obese patients (1,841 vs 1,500 kcal/day; P < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, higher BMI (P = 0.003) and male sex (P = 0.028) were independently associated with higher REE, while AKI was not. LBM estimated by predictive equations was more strongly correlated with REE than PMI (P < 0.001), and correlation strength did not differ by AKI status. Measured REE did not differ between ventilated surgical-trauma patients with and without AKI. REE differed by sex, age, and obesity status, and AKI was not associated with within-group differences. BMI and sex were identified as independent predictors of REE. Estimated LBM was strongly correlated with REE independent of AKI status. Given possible residual confounding, further investigation is needed.

articles.title: Computed tomography-derived nasojejunal tube tip-to-gastric antrum path length and short-term outcomes in severe acute pancreatitis.
articles.abstract: Nasojejunal (NJ) feeding is commonly used in severe acute pancreatitis (SAP), but whether deeper tube advancement improves clinical outcomes is uncertain. Computed tomography (CT)-based three-dimensional reconstruction can quantify the in-situ tube trajectory. To determine whether CT-derived NJ tube path length is associated with short-term outcomes in patients with confirmed SAP. This prospective single-center observational cohort included 63 patients with confirmed SAP. CT-based three-dimensional reconstruction measured the curved path length from the gastric antrum-pylorus junction to the tube tip. The primary outcome was intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation and Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II-adjusted median regression. Firth penalized logistic regression evaluated the exploratory composite outcome. Anatomical tube-tip position was independently classified on multiplanar CT. Median path length was 17.55 cm (interquartile range, 14.35-22.27 cm). Path length was not associated with ICU stay by Spearman analysis (rho = 0.055, P = 0.671) or adjusted median regression (difference per 5-cm increase = 0.192-day, 95% confidence interval: -0.922 to 1.305, P = 0.732). Post-CT ICU stay showed a similar null association. Anatomical position was duodenal in 28 patients, at the duodenojejunal flexure in 18, and jejunal in 17; path length correlated strongly with independently measured flexure-relative distance (rho = 0.997, P < 0.001). The exploratory composite outcome occurred in 17 patients, and path length remained non-significant in Firth regression. CT-derived NJ tube path length was not associated with ICU outcomes but closely reflected distal anatomical tube position. These findings do not establish an optimal advancement target.

articles.title: Same R0 , Different Risk: Colonization-Age Timing and Heterogeneity Drive ICU MRSA Establishment and Burden.
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) control of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) occurs over short horizons, whereas R 0  summarizes average transmission at the importation-free disease-free state without encoding timing. We couple within-host bacterial and immune dynamics to an ICU model structured by colonization age, generating transmission and progression kernels that vary with colonization age. A two-stage framework uses a branching process to quantify finite-threshold crossing and a deterministic ward model to quantify conditional burden after the threshold is reached. Calibration fixes η = 0.10  and distributes colonized admissions across pre-admission colonization ages. Of 1, 000, 000 parameter sets, 45, 250 satisfy cumulative  R 2 ≥ 0.90  . The representative calculation is subcritical, with  R 0 = 0.907957  ; across accepted sets, the median and 95% behavioral range are 0.917464 and [ 0.814593 ,  1.032975 ]  , with 92.460 %  below one. At  Z crit = 5  , exact threshold-reaching probabilities are 0.114659 for age-dependent transmission and 0.117074 for matched constant transmission. Their accepted-set difference range crosses zero, so this contrast has no robust direction. By contrast, age-dependent transmission reaches 50% of reproductive potential earlier in 98.378 %  of accepted sets. In 200-day conditional simulations, delaying τ crit  from 5 to 15 days increases the age-dependent peak total MRSA burden from 5.629 to 7.298 patients and cumulative total burden from 683.8 to 1398.0 patient-days. At the 9-day baseline and equal R 0  , age dependence gives a 7.372 %  higher peak but a 9.304 %  lower cumulative burden than constant transmission. Increasing κ max  from 0.6 to 1.4 times baseline reduces R 0  by 4.133 %  . Thus, matching R 0  does not preserve timing-sensitive outcomes, but their magnitude and direction depend on the endpoint; over the examined ranges, clearance timing has greater leverage than immune-strength intensification.

articles.title: The lived experience of critical care nurses caring for patients with intensive care unit-acquired weakness: a qualitative study.
articles.journal: Journal of research in nursing : JRN
articles.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired weakness (ICU-AW) is a prevalent neuromuscular complication with high morbidity. Understanding the nursing experience is crucial for improving patient outcomes. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences and challenges of critical care nurses caring for patients with ICU-AW. A descriptive qualitative design was employed. Semi-structured, face-to-face interviews were conducted with ten critical care nurses. Data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using content analysis. Analysis identified three core themes: (1) deficits in disease understanding, (2) challenges in patient nursing and (3) insufficiency of systemic support. The study highlights the complex realities of ICU-AW nursing, contributing a foundational narrative to nursing theory on the burdens of rehabilitation in critical care. It provides direct evidence for policy, recommending mandatory ICU-AW education in nursing curricula, the development of standardised interdisciplinary rehabilitation protocols and institutional support systems to mitigate nurse burnout and enhance collaborative practice.This study illuminates the critical nursing perspective on ICU-AW, advocating for the integration of structured rehabilitative nursing practices, supportive debriefing mechanisms and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration to improve both patient outcomes and nurse job satisfaction.

articles.title: What do the findings of compartmentalised sub-phenotypes in lungs of patients with pneumonia mean for critical care?
Assessment of healthcare professionals' perceptions regarding the implementation of a musical intervention in an intensive care unit.
Lactate-to-albumin ratio and 28-day mortality in older postoperative ICU patients: A prospective cohort study with MIMIC-IV replication.
articles.abstract: Older postoperative intensive care patients have heterogeneous mortality risk related to acute illness severity, frailty, and reduced physiological reserve. The lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) integrates routinely available markers of perioperative physiological stress, but its prognostic value remains uncertain. Patients aged ≥65 years admitted to a postoperative intensive care unit were prospectively enrolled. LAR was measured at ICU admission, whereas APACHE II used the worst values during the first 24 h. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality. LAR was compared with lactate, albumin, blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, Prognostic Nutritional Index, and Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet index. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, APACHE II score, Clinical Frailty Scale score, surgical urgency, and comorbidity burden. A harmonized replication analysis was conducted in the MIMIC-IV surgical ICU cohort. Internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resamples provided optimism-corrected estimates of discrimination, calibration, and overall model performance. Among 647 patients, 79 (12.2%) died within 28 days. LAR showed the highest discrimination (AUC, 0.803; 95% CI, 0.753-0.851) and was independently associated with mortality (adjusted OR per SD, 3.40; 95% CI, 2.33-4.96). LAR slightly outperformed lactate as a single marker (ΔAUC, 0.029; p = 0.002). Clinical models with LAR or lactate showed similar discrimination (optimism-corrected AUC, 0.885 vs 0.883; ΔAUC, 0.0014; 95% CI, -0.0071 to 0.0099; p = 0.750). In MIMIC-IV, LAR remained independently associated with 28-day mortality (OR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.28-1.94; AUC, 0.704). LAR was independently associated with 28-day mortality and performed similarly to lactate when added to the 24-h clinical model, supporting its role as a complementary biomarker. The association was reproduced in MIMIC-IV with attenuation.

articles.title: Practice Patterns and Staffing Models for Nonoperating Room Anesthesia in the Intensive Care Unit: An Exploratory Survey of the Membership of the American Society of Anesthesiologists Committee on Critical Care Medicine.
Beyond the stopwatch: the physiological cost of pulse checks during CPR.
Depressive and Anxiety symptoms associated with ICU admission in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Academy of Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly in Latin America. Depression and anxiety are frequent during pregnancy and may influence HDP severity, yet their impact on clinical outcomes remains unclear. To determine whether depressive and anxiety symptoms are associated with obstetric intensive care unit (ICU) admission and hospital length of stay among women with HDP. A prospective cohort study was conducted at a Colombian tertiary-care referral hospital (July 2024-January 2025). Women aged ≥16 years in their third trimester hospitalized for HDP completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7). Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression and Cox regression models assessed associations with ICU admission and length of stay RESULTS: Among 234 participants (median age 25 years), 61.1% required ICU care; only 14 of the 143 ICU patients (9.8%) were assessed before ICU transfer. An EPDS score ≥10 or a positive response to item 10 was independently associated with ICU admission (OR 4.83 , 95% CI 1.56 -14.94, p=0.006) and longer hospitalization (HR 0.69 , 95% CI 0.48 -1.00, p=0.048). In an exploratory finding, a GAD-7 score ≥10 showed an inverse association with ICU admission (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.09-0.88, p=0.029). Hemoglobin <11 g/dL and a post hoc mean arterial pressure threshold ≥102.5 mmHg were also significantly associated with ICU admission. Depressive symptoms were associated with obstetric ICU admission and prolonged hospitalization in patients admitted for HDP, whereas anxiety appeared protective, which seems counterintuitive and requires future research to confirm its association; however, because most assessments took place after ICU transfer, causality could not be established. Integrating mental health screening into HDP management may improve maternal outcomes.

articles.title: Observational study for perioperative intensive care unit (OPICU): Planned and unplanned ICU admissions, follow-up, discharge, and outcomes.
articles.abstract: Due to limited resources, identifying high-risk surgical patients who derive clinical benefit from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission is essential. Our primary aim was to characterize resource allocation and evaluate the true clinical benefit of ICU admissions using modified Wang criteria. Secondary aim is to identify independent risk factors for ICU admission; validate clinical scoring systems; and compare inter-group outcomes, including Clavien-Dindo complication rates, lengths of stay, and mortality. This multicenter, prospective, observational study was conducted across 75 ICUs. Adult inpatient surgery cases were categorized into four groups: planned admission (PAG), unplanned admission (UPAG), planned but not admitted (PBNAG), and emergent admission (EAG). Data included preoperative/intraoperative/postoperative(ICU) variables, modified Wang criteria, and mortality rates (ICU, hospital, 30/90-day). Of 55,963 preoperatively evaluated patients, 2764 (4.9%) were planned for ICU admission; 804/2764 patients could not be admitted because of limited ICU beds, remaining of 1960 patients with a planned ICU admission, 411/1960 did not require postoperative ICU care forming the PBNAG (14.8% of 2764). Overall, 1980 patients (3.09% of all cases) were admitted to the ICU (78.2% PAG, 12.5% EAG, 9.1% UPAG). POSSUM scores effectively differentiated PBNAG (lower) and EAG (higher) from PAG. ICU benefit indicators (e.g., vasopressor need, prolonged ventilation >12 h, arrest events) were significantly higher in UPAG and EAG versus PAG (p < 0.001). Emergency surgery (OR 12.4), intraoperative complications (OR 3.1), and ASA >2 (OR 2.7) independently increased UPAG risk, whereas minimally invasive surgery and regional anesthesia reduced ICU admissions. Overall ICU and 90-day mortality rates were 5.9% and 7.5%, respectively, peaking in the EAG group (18.1% and 18.9%). Integrating modified Wang criteria, POSSUM scores, intraoperative complications, emergency status, and ASA class >2 is effective in predicting the necessity of ICU admission.

articles.title: Dual Antiglutamate Therapy in Super-Refractory Status Epilepticus After Cardiac Arrest (SUPER-CAT Study).
articles.abstract: The SUPER-refractory status epilepticus (SE) after Cardiac Arrest Treatment (SUPER-CAT) study evaluated the efficacy and safety of dual antiglutamate therapy (combined AMPA and NMDA receptor blockade) in patients with super-refractory SE (SRSE) after cardiac arrest and without unfavorable prognostic indicators. Multicenter cohort study including patients with postanoxic SRSE meeting the following criteria: bilaterally preserved N20 cortical responses, intact pupillary reflexes, and absence of generalized periodic discharges. Patients treated with dual antiglutamate therapy (DUAL; ketamine 1.5-7.5 mg/kg/h for 3 days plus perampanel 6-12 mg/d for 5 days with tapering) were compared with patients receiving other combinations of antiseizure and anesthetic agents (OTHERS). The primary outcome was resolution of SE. Secondary outcomes included awakening to follow commands and good neurologic outcome at 6 months (modified Rankin Scale 0-3) in patients with fewer than 2 unfavorable multimodal prognostic indicators and 6-month mortality for the entire cohort. Safety analysis included in-hospital mortality and potentially treatment-related adverse events. Patients treated with single antiglutamate agents were described separately. Between May 2012 and May 2025, 95 of 1,352 consecutive post-cardiac arrest intensive care unit patients met inclusion criteria (mean age 66, interquartile range 55-73; 41% female; DUAL = 43; OTHERS = 41; single antiglutamate = 11). Compared with OTHERS, DUAL was associated with a higher rate of SE resolution (84% vs 49%; OR 5.4; 95% CI 1.9-14.9; p = 0.001), a greater likelihood of awakening before discharge (56% vs 32%; OR 2.7; 95% CI 1.0-7.3; p = 0.053) and lower 6-month mortality (52% vs 74%; OR 0.37; 95% CI 0.15-0.97; p = 0.043). A trend toward better 6-month neurologic outcome was observed in the DUAL group (39% vs 25%; OR 1.89; 95% CI 0.64-5.56; p = 0.245). Reversible cholestatic liver injury occurred more frequently in DUAL group, compared with OTHERS (77% vs 27%; OR 9.00; 95% CI 3.34-24.19; p < 0.001). In patients with postanoxic SRSE without unfavorable prognostic indicators, dual antiglutamate therapy was highly effective in resolving SE and was associated with improved short-term clinical outcomes. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05756621.

articles.title: DPP3 as a Biomarker in Patients with Cardiovascular Critical Illness.
articles.abstract: Dipeptidyl peptidase 3 (DPP3) exerts vasodilatory and myocardial depressant effects in preclinical models and is a potential therapeutic target in cardiogenic shock (CS). Patients admitted to the CICU at Brigham and Women's Hospital were enrolled in a biorepository with samples collected at CICU admission. Using samples from 2017-2023, DPP3 was measured using an immunoluminometric assay (4TEEN4). Shock, defined by hypotension and end-organ hypoperfusion, was adjudicated as CS (classic or vasodilatory) or distributive (DS). Controls were CICU patients without shock. Models were adjusted for age, sex, eGFR, and SOFA score. Of 1082 CICU patients, 381 (35.2%) had CS, 70 (6.5%) had DS, and 618 (57.2%) were non-shock controls. DPP3 values were higher in CS (median, 42.7 [Q1-Q3, 25.6-84.3] ng/mL) than in non-shock controls (31.8 [20.2-57.2] ng/mL; p<0.001) but, nevertheless, were elevated (>30 ng/mL) in 53.6% of non-shock controls. CICU patients with DPP3 >30 ng/mL had higher in-hospital mortality (19.9% vs. 8.4%; OR 2.7 [95% CI 1.8-4.0]; p<0.001), with a consistent pattern across CS, DS, and non-shock patients (p-interaction=0.72) and across CS etiologic subgroups (p-interaction=0.18). In adjusted analyses including both shock and non-shock patients, DPP3 showed a graded association with mortality across quartiles (adj-OR Q4 vs. Q1: 3.0 [1.6-6.1]; p<0.001), and at a 30 ng/mL threshold (adj-OR: 2.1 [1.4-3.4]; p=0.001). Among critically ill CICU patients, DPP3 was elevated in shock and non-shock states and was associated with in-hospital mortality. These findings support a potential role for DPP3 as a biomarker for risk stratification and a possible target for therapy.

articles.title: Closest to the patient, furthest from survival? Reframing the family witness for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in our aging world.
Recent advances in critical care nutrition: from dose escalation to phase-guided and response-guided care.
articles.abstract: To critically appraise recent advances that are shifting critical care nutrition from uniform nutrient targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided care, with particular emphasis on major studies published in 2025-2026. Recent large trials do not support routine early full-dose energy or high-dose protein delivery in unselected critically ill patients, and some higher dose strategies have generated safety signals. Indirect calorimetry improves measurement of energy expenditure, but measured expenditure is not synonymous with the dose that should be delivered. Emerging data suggest that dynamic responses, including early phosphate trajectories, may help identify metabolic readiness for feeding, although no validated bedside marker exists. Pharmacological intravenous vitamin C has shown no benefit and recurring harm signals in shocked patients, whereas micronutrient care should distinguish physiological requirements and deficiency correction from megadosing. After ICU discharge, intake frequently falls during the transition from enteral to oral nutrition, and intake-guided protocols have achieved high nutritional adequacy in proof-of-concept studies. Critical care nutrition is moving from universal targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided treatment. Acute-phase caution should not become prolonged underfeeding; repeated metabolic assessment, body composition, reliable intake monitoring and continuity through recovery are central priorities.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Based Mortality Prediction for Mechanically Ventilated Liver Failure Patients: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: To develop a mortality prediction model for patients with liver failure who require mechanical ventilation (MV) in ICU. This retrospective study utilized data from the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV (v3.0) databases. Variables included demographics, liver function markers, ventilator parameters, severity scores, comorbidities, use of vasoactive drugs and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) as well as length of ICU and hospital stay. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Five machine learning algorithms were applied: logistic regression, decision tree, Bagging, neural network, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). The dataset was randomly split into a training set (70%) and a test set (30%). Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and calibration plots. Predictive factors were ranked for the best-performing model by importance. A total of 2336 patients were identified from the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV databases. On the test set, the AUC values for each model were as follows: logistic regression (0.836), decision tree (0.768), neural network (0.774), Bagging (0.854), and XGBoost (0.875). Calibration curves showed good agreement for all models except the neural network. Among the 5 algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the highest predictive performance. The top 5 predictors identified were length of hospital stay, SAPS II score, use of vasoactive drugs, total bilirubin and length of ICU stay. Machine learning-based models can effectively predict in-hospital mortality in liver failure patients receiving mechanical ventilation. Among the 5 algorithms tested, the XGBoost model achieved the best overall performance.

articles.title: Which spontaneous breathing trial should be used to reproduce post-extubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related ARDS? A multicenter randomized crossover study.
articles.abstract: Spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) guide extubation decisions in intensive care unit (ICU), predicting the respiratory effort required by the patient after extubation. Different SBTs exist and should be adapted to critical illness. Viral pneumonias such as COVID-19 combine lung injury, sepsis-induced systemic inflammation, and encephalopathy, making classification challenging. The objective was to assess which SBT could be used to reproduce postextubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients. In this multicenter randomized crossover study, COVID-19-related ARDS patients mechanically ventilated at least 24 hours and ready for extubation underwent 3 different 15-minute SBT at random order: pressure support ventilation of 7-cmH2O with positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 0-cmH2O (PSV7PEEP0), PSV 0-cmH2O with PEEP 0-cmH2O (PSV0PEEP0) and T-piece trial. At baseline, end of each SBT, and 20 minutes after extubation, surrogates of respiratory effort were measured: esophageal pressure-time-product (PTPes), PTPes per minute (PTPes.min), swing esophageal pressure (SwingPes), and SwingPes per minute (SwingPes.min). Sixty measurements of respiratory effort from 12 patients were analyzed. Median PTPes.min increased from 193.8 [170.8-227.2] cmH2O.s/min at baseline to 236.6 [192.1-313.6] after extubation, with no significant differences between SBTs and postextubation. SwingPes and SwingPes.min were lower during PSV7-PEEP0 than after extubation, with median paired differences of 4.7 (95% CI 0.6-9.8) and 115.3 (95% CI 4.8-297.8), but these differences did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. No SBT modality differed significantly from post-extubation respiratory effort, suggesting that none could be excluded in COVID-19-related ARDS patients.

articles.title: Low-Use vs. High-Use Physical Restraint in Older Adults With Sepsis Receiving Mechanical Ventilation: A Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
articles.abstract: Physical restraints are commonly used in patients receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU), yet evidence regarding their effectiveness in older patients with sepsis is limited. This study evaluated whether a low-use physical restraint strategy improves outcomes in older patients with sepsis requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. This multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial was conducted in five ICUs in China from August 2023 to March 2026. Patients aged ≥ 65 years with invasive mechanical ventilation were randomly assigned (1:1) to a low-use restraint strategy (restraints applied only for severe agitation) or a high-use restraint strategy (routine restraint use until recovery of consciousness and liberation from mechanical ventilation). The primary outcome was days alive without delirium or coma within 7 days after randomization. Secondary outcomes included delirium incidence, ventilator-free days, coma-free days, sedative exposure, 28-day mortality, and safety events. Analyses were performed using intention-to-treat, per-protocol, and inverse probability weighting approaches. Among 485 randomized patients (median age, 74 years; 60.4% male), 244 received low-use and 241 high-use restraint. Delirium- and coma-free days did not differ between groups (adjusted mean difference, 0.17 days; 95% CI, -0.20 to 0.54; p = 0.37). Low-use restraint was associated with more ventilator-free days (0.69 days; 95% CI, 0.48-0.91; p < 0.001) and coma-free days (0.46 days; 95% CI, 0.19-0.74; p = 0.001). No significant between-group differences were observed in delirium incidence, sedative exposure, 28-day mortality, or safety outcomes. Among older mechanically ventilated patients with sepsis, a low-use physical restraint strategy did not improve days alive without delirium or coma but was associated with more ventilator-free and coma-free days. These findings suggest that reducing restraint use may facilitate short-term recovery, although the safety of restraint minimization requires further evaluation. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: ChiCTR1900025850.

articles.title: Significant hypercapnia as an initial manifestation of COVID-19 without typical symptoms in chronic cervical spinal cord injury: A case series.
articles.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
articles.abstract: Few reports have described how Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) presents in patients with long-standing high cervical spinal cord injury (SCI). This case series suggests that clinically significant hypercapnia may be an early manifestation of COVID-19 in this population, even without classic respiratory symptoms or marked oxygen desaturation, potentially delaying recognition of ventilatory failure. We describe two men with chronic C4 ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS) A. Case 1: A 76-year-old vaccinated man developed drowsiness, confusion, and headache without cough or fever. Room-air oxygen saturation was 90-95%, and inflammatory markers did not clearly indicate infection. Arterial blood gas (ABG) showed new-onset, clinically significant hypercapnia (pH 7.306, PaCO₂ 62.4 mmHg, PaO₂ 77.3 mmHg). He required endotracheal intubation and intensive care unit (ICU) care; COVID-19 was subsequently confirmed and remdesivir was administered. Tracheostomy was later performed after unsuccessful ventilator weaning. Case 2: A 70-year-old unvaccinated man reported chest discomfort without cough or fever, then developed confusion. Room-air oxygen saturation remained 94-95%. ABG showed respiratory acidosis with new-onset, clinically significant hypercapnia (pH 7.304, PaCO₂ 59.4 mmHg, PaO₂ 76.7 mmHg). He also required intubation, mechanical ventilation, ICU care, and tracheostomy after COVID-19 was confirmed; he was treated with remdesivir and corticosteroids. These cases suggest that hypercapnia may be an early and potentially critical manifestation of COVID-19 in chronic high cervical SCI, without typical respiratory symptoms or marked hypoxemia. Clinicians should assess CO₂ retention in this vulnerable population to avoid delayed diagnosis and deterioration.

articles.title: Molecular Subtypes in Acute Respiratory Illness and Sepsis.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Sepsis and acute respiratory illness are clinical syndromes that encompass profound biological heterogeneity. The resulting heterogeneity of treatment effect is now widely understood as the explanation to why immunomodulatory trials in critical care have not me their study endpoints, thereby misclassifying effective therapies as futile while concealing harm in biologically ineligible subgroups. High-dimensional molecular profiling offers a route to resolve this heterogeneity into tractable subgroups or subtypes. Here we review molecular subtypes across adult and paediatric sepsis, pneumonia, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), spanning transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic platforms. Blood transcriptomic frameworks derived independently in multiple countries, and subsequently harmonized by international consensus efforts, converge on recurring immune archetypes: a myeloid inflammatory state dominated by neutrophil activation; a mixed myeloid and lymphoid dysregulated state carrying the highest mortality; and a relatively immunocompetent state with preserved lymphocyte function and the most favourable clinical trajectory. Plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling recapitulate this architecture at orthogonal molecular layers, arguing that these archetypes are platform-independent rather than artefacts of any single technology. Cross-syndrome convergence is asymmetric, which plausibly reflects the methodological differences between top-down latent class analysis in ARDS and bottom-up unsupervised clustering in sepsis. Secondary analyses of randomized controlled trials consistently show subtype-dependent responses to treatment strategies, with a coherent directionality with potential benefit in hyperinflammatory states, and harm in immunosuppressed or adaptive immune-prevalent states. Subtype membership is not static; trajectory, not baseline assignment, most strongly encodes prognosis. Realising precision critical care now requires prospective, subtype-stratified trials of which none has yet been completed.

articles.title: Optimizing post-extubation respiratory support in high-risk patients.
ARDS at 60: beyond lung protection to lung repair.
Genomic Investigation of a Carbapenem-Resistant Chromobacterium haemolyticum Cluster Reveals Environmental Introduction and Nosocomial Transmission.
articles.abstract: To investigate the source and transmission dynamics of a cluster of four Chromobacterium haemolyticum infections in an intensive care unit (ICU) and to characterize their antimicrobial resistance profiles. An epidemiological investigation was conducted involving four ICU patients identified between July 2024 and August 2025. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on eight isolates, and core-genome single-nucleotide polymorphism (cgSNP) analysis was used to assess their genetic relatedness. Antimicrobial resistance genes were identified using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD), while resistance-associated point mutations were detected using AMRFinderPlus. A maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree was constructed based on 26 genomes to investigate the genomic relationships among the isolates. Two distinct epidemiological events were identified. Three patients harbored closely related isolates forming a clonal cluster with 0-10 SNP differences, linked to an index case with a history of near-drowning. In contrast, an isolate recovered from a patient with independent environmental exposure was genetically unrelated to the cluster, differing by >38,000 SNPs. All cluster isolates carried the chromosomal blaCRH-2 gene, encoding a class A carbapenemase related to Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC), and displayed carbapenem resistance, unlike previously reported carbapenem-susceptible C. haemolyticum strains. Transmission ceased during the winter, with Patient 2 serving as a potential long-term reservoir. This study provides the first genomic evidence supporting nosocomial transmission of C. haemolyticum. The concordant resistance profiles observed in the outbreak and unrelated isolates suggest that blaCRH-2 may be a key determinant of carbapenem resistance in C. haemolyticum, challenging the assumption that empirical carbapenem therapy is reliably effective against this pathogen.

articles.title: Serial bedside retinal optical coherence tomography angiography in sepsis associated circulatory dysfunction.
Environmental scan of Indigenous resources and culturally specific tools across intensive care units in Alberta, Canada.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract: Indigenous Peoples in Canada are disproportionately burdened with a spectrum of health issues and consistently report lower satisfaction with their health care; nevertheless, little is known about their experiences with critical care and the support received during critical illness. We aimed to describe the current scope of critical-care-specific resources available to Indigenous patients and their families across Alberta to identify gaps and opportunities to implement actionable change to realize more equitable and culturally safe care. We conducted a two-phase environmental scan. Phase 1 entailed searching websites for information to support Indigenous patients, their families, and health care workers. Phase 2 facilitated 21 interviews with intensive care unit (ICU) stakeholders from across Alberta to further describe site-specific resources, services, tools, or initiatives to support Indigenous Peoples. Indigenous partners were engaged through all aspects of the project. Our environmental scan identified a paucity of ICU-specific resources, programs, or policies to support Indigenous patients and families' navigation with critical care. We identified two national resources aimed at clinicians, rather than patients or families. Interviews with ICU stakeholders confirmed the paucity of Indigenous-specific resources. Stakeholders cited numerous barriers, including inadequate culture training, staff time constraints and burnout, physical space limits, and insufficient personnel, such as Indigenous liaisons and social workers. Multiple gaps exist in the availability of critical-care-focused resources and supports for Indigenous Peoples experiencing critical illness in Alberta, Canada. Addressing these care gaps may improve health equity, access, and the experience for Indigenous patients and families during critical illness and further build trust and strengthen relationships with health care workers.

articles.title: Associations of International Normalized Ratio and Hematocrit With Stroke Status and Machine Learning Mortality Prediction in Critical Care Databases.
articles.abstract: Stroke is a major cause of mortality and long-term disability. This retrospective cohort study evaluated associations of international normalized ratio (INR) and hematocrit (Hct) with stroke status in 29,831 adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Stroke status was identified using predefined International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and Tenth Revision codes. INR and Hct were defined using the first measurements within 24 h after ICU admission. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, quartile analyses, restricted cubic splines (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses. Primary analyses used complete-case cohorts, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. A post hoc exploratory secondary analysis among patients with stroke used Cox regression to identify six prognostic variables for machine learning-based prediction of ICU mortality. Stroke proportions decreased across increasing INR quartiles and increased across increasing Hct quartiles. After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in INR was associated with lower stroke odds, with odds ratios (ORs) of 0.105-0.395 across cohorts, whereas each 1-percentage-point increase in Hct was associated with higher stroke odds (ORs, 1.076-1.103). RCS analyses supported overall associations but not consistent nonlinearity after full adjustment. Multiple-imputation results were directionally consistent. The gradient boosting machine (GBM) model yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.717 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.669-0.766), 0.670 (95% CI, 0.603-0.737), and 0.630 (95% CI, 0.557-0.703) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. INR was inversely associated and Hct positively associated with stroke status. These observational associations require cautious interpretation; the exploratory ICU mortality analysis provides a complementary prognostic perspective among patients with stroke.

articles.title: Assessment of tools for the diagnosis of malnutrition and ICU outcomes in critically ill adults: A comparison study.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract: To evaluate the concurrent and predictive validity of the Academy of Nutrition & Dietetics/ASPEN Indicators for Malnutrition (AAIM) in critically ill patients compared with the SGA, considering disease etiology and fluid accumulation. This was a comparison study. Malnutrition was assessed within 24 h of ICU admission using the Subjective Global Assessment (SGA) and the AAIM consensus. The AAIM approach was applied assuming all patients had acute disease (AAIM I) or differentiating acute versus chronic disease-related malnutrition (AAIM II). Two variations were tested based on fluid accumulation: including (AAIM a) or excluding (AAIM b) this component. Concurrent validity was evaluated against SGA using diagnostic accuracy metrics, and predictive validity was assessed using hospital and ICU length of stay and mortality. Among 450 critically ill patients [median age 64 (54-71) years; 53.1% male; APACHE II score 18 (11-23)], 46.3% were malnourished by SGA, whereas AAIM prevalence ranged from 70.9% to 75.5%. AAIM showed moderate sensitivity (75.1%-78.9%) but low specificity (28.6%-32.4%) and poor agreement with SGA (κ = 0.066-0.073). AAIM-defined malnutrition was not associated with outcomes, while SGA-defined malnutrition predicted prolonged hospital stay (OR 1.48; 95% CI 1.00-2.20) and ICU mortality (HR 2.26; 95% CI 1.42-3.49). In critically ill patients, AAIM overestimated malnutrition prevalence and lacked concurrent and predictive validity, whereas SGA showed prognostic value.

articles.title: Associations between Global Immune-Nutrition-Inflammation Index and Risk of Mortality in Intensive Care Unit Patients.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract: This retrospective study aimed to evaluate the association between the newly developed Global Immune-Nutrition-Inflammation (GINI) index and the risk of all-cause mortality among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV version 3.0 (MIMIC-IV-3.0) database. Associations between the GINI index and all-cause mortality were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves and multivariate weighted Cox regression models. Additionally, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were performed to explore potential non-linear relationships between the GINI index and hazard ratios (HRs). Subgroup analyses were conducted to evaluate possible interactions between the GINI index and selected clinical features. A total of 970 patients were included, of whom 11.75% (N = 114) experienced all-cause mortality. A significant association was observed between a higher GINI index and increased risk of all-cause mortality. This association remained consistent when the GINI index was treated as a continuous variable (HR = 1.12; P = 0.03) and when categorized into groups (Group 2 vs. Group 1: HR = 1.97; P = 0.02; Group 3 vs. Group 1: HR = 2.17; P = 0.01). The RCS analysis supported a linear, rather than a non-linear, relationship between the GINI index and all-cause mortality (P > 0.05 for non-linearity). The GINI index is associated with elevated all-cause mortality risk among ICU patients and may serve as a promising candidate for mortality risk stratification, which highlights the potential benefit of timely targeted intervention.

articles.title: Wearable Sweat Biosystem with Dual Diffusion-Limiting Interface for Dynamic Hyperlactatemia Management in Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Hyperlactatemia is a critical indicator of tissue hypoperfusion, metabolic dysfunction, and an adverse prognosis in critically ill patients. Yet conventional monitoring depends entirely on intermittent, invasive blood sampling, which cannot capture the dynamic metabolic fluctuations required to guide timely clinical interventions. Herein, we report a wearable sweat-sensing device built on a dual-diffusion-limiting architecture for the continuous and accurate assessment of clinical hyperlactatemia. This system synergistically modulates lactate diffusion in sweat through a silane-network-encapsulated lactate oxidase layer coupled to a polyvinyl chloride layer. This design effectively delays enzyme saturation, extending the linear detection range for sweat lactate to 0-60 mM and thereby fulfilling the stringent requirements of critical care monitoring. The device also integrates real-time pH and temperature calibration to safeguard measurement accuracy in complex physiological environments. Moreover, linear mixed-effects analysis of 82 paired samples from 33 critically ill patients demonstrated a strong association between sweat and blood lactate levels, with a marginal R2 of 0.840. Sweat lactate effectively identified hyperlactatemia and predicted in-hospital mortality, yielding areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.943 and 0.785, respectively. The integrated iontophoresis-microfluidics module further ensures high consistency with bedside arterial blood gas analysis, as validated by a marginal R2 of 0.811. Together, these results establish sweat biosensors as a promising platform for continuous metabolic monitoring, resuscitation assessment, and objective prognostic stratification in critical care settings.
