Therapeutic drug monitoring can help guide dose adjustment when validated targets are available, while model-informed precision dosing may provide additional support in selected patients. The review also proposes an eight-step practical framework based on residual kidney function, the actual delivered CRRT prescription, drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, therapeutic monitoring, and repeated reassessment. Future approaches may combine real-time CRRT data with pharmacokinetic models to support more individualized dosing.

articles.title: Complications and Hospital Resource Utilization Associated with ECMO in COVID-19 ARDS with Acute Kidney Injury: Insights from United States National Inpatient Sample, 2020-2022.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication of COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), yet the impact of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) on outcomes in this high-risk population remains unclear. We performed a retrospective, survey-weighted study using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database from 2020-2022 to compare outcomes among adults hospitalized with COVID-19-associated ARDS and AKI managed with invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) alone versus IMV and ECMO. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, while secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT), complications, hospital length of stay (LOS), and healthcare utilization. Among 198,395 hospitalizations with COVID-19 ARDS complicated by AKI, 4730 received IMV and ECMO. ECMO use was not associated with statistically significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.81-1.12). However, ECMO was associated with greater odds of RRT, intracranial hemorrhage, disseminated intravascular coagulation, cardiogenic shock, vasopressor use, tracheostomy, acute liver failure, deep vein thrombosis, ischemic stroke and ICU-acquired weakness. ECMO was also associated with longer LOS and higher hospitalization charges. Among hospitalizations with COVID-19-associated ARDS and AKI, ECMO was not associated with statistically significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality but was associated with markedly higher complication burden, longer hospitalization, and substantially greater healthcare resource utilization.

articles.title: Mechanical ventilation-associated AKI: toward a multimodal and kidney-protective ventilatory framework.
articles.abstract: Mechanical ventilation-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a complex manifestation of lung-kidney cross-talk driven by hemodynamic alterations, neurohumoral activation, systemic inflammation and disturbances in gas exchange and acid-base homeostasis. Beyond static ventilatory settings, increasing evidence suggests that dynamic fluctuations in airway and perfusion parameters, including static driving pressure (ΔP), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), mean airway pressure (Pmean), and effective renal perfusion pressure (eRPP) may substantially influence renal vulnerability during mechanical ventilation. This comprehensive narrative review synthesizes current mechanistic and clinical evidence on the relationship between mechanical ventilation and AKI and proposes an integrated framework for future research on the interplay between ventilatory stress, venous congestion, renal perfusion, and inflammatory injury. Emerging bedside tools such as renal Doppler indices, venous excess ultrasound score (VExUS), and kidney injury biomarkers are discussed as components of an integrated physiologic approach for early recognition and risk stratification of ventilator-associated AKI. We further propose a multimodal conceptual framework integrating respiratory mechanics, congestion assessment, perfusion monitoring, and biomarkers to support individualized kidney-protective ventilation strategies. Future research should prioritize standardized physiologic monitoring, time-varying exposure analyses, causal mediation approaches, and prospective multicenter studies to better define renal-protective ventilatory targets and advance precision critical care.

articles.title: oXiris-Based Blood Purification Efficacy in Adults with Septic Shock and Acute Kidney Injury: The PURE Multicenter Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Randomized evidence for the oXiris adsorptive membrane in septic shock remains limited. We estimated its effect on 28-day mortality and explored short-term physiologic outcomes in adults with septic shock and acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy. Methods: PURE was a multicenter, single-blind, parallel-group pilot randomized trial in Saudi Arabia. Participants were randomized 1:1 to oXiris-based or conventional continuous venovenous hemodialysis. The primary comparison used unadjusted mortality risk estimates. Secondary observations were summarized descriptively; adjusted and post-hoc Bayesian sensitivity analyses are reported in the main text and supplement. Results: Of 204 randomized participants, 202 were analyzed (oXiris, 100; control, 102). Twenty-eight-day mortality was 39.0% (39/100) versus 47.1% (48/102), respectively (risk ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.60-1.14; risk difference, -8.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -21.7 to 5.6; p = 0.247). Reported 72 h norepinephrine dose, lactate, C-reactive protein, and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score were lower with oXiris; reported intensive care unit (ICU) stay was also shorter. Secondary descriptive observations are limited by unverifiable time-specific denominators and handling of intercurrent events. Premature filter clotting was reported in 8/100 versus 7/102 participants; no device-related adverse events were reported, but safety ascertainment was limited. Conclusions: This pilot trial did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in 28-day mortality, although mortality was numerically lower in the oXiris group. Consistent protocol implementation and encouraging, hypothesis-generating physiologic observations provide a foundation for a definitive trial with complete longitudinal ascertainment.

articles.title: Electrolyte disturbance phenotypes and adverse outcomes in the intensive care unit: The role of magnesium and potassium abnormalities.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Magnesium and potassium disturbances are common in critically ill patients, but the prognostic value of their co-occurrence is poorly defined. To evaluate the association of combined magnesium-potassium phenotypes at intensive care unit (ICU) admission with 30-day in-hospital mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), and invasive mechanical ventilation. This retrospective cohort included 9462 adults admitted to the ICU of a tertiary hospital in Jordan (2012-2022) with admission magnesium and potassium, classified into nine phenotypes. Mortality was analyzed by Cox regression, censoring patients discharged alive at discharge, and AKI and ventilation by logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, and modified APACHE II score. Thirty-day mortality was 30.6%, ranging from 25.0% with normal magnesium and potassium to 63.6% with combined hypermagnesemia-hyperkalemia. The combined phenotype had the highest adjusted hazard of death (HR 3.01, 95% CI 2.60-3.49), with positive additive interaction (relative excess risk due to interaction 0.76, 95% CI 0.29-1.23). Isolated hyperkalemia (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.46-1.82) and isolated hypermagnesemia (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.42-1.86) were also associated with mortality. The combined phenotype was associated with AKI (aOR 2.66, 95% CI 2.09-3.38) and ventilation (aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.17-1.94). Modeled continuously, potassium showed a U-shaped and magnesium a J-shaped association with mortality. Co-occurring hypermagnesemia and hyperkalemia at ICU admission identify a high-risk phenotype. Because both are measured routinely, this combination may serve as a simple marker for early risk stratification.

articles.title: Utilities of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor in the Intensive Care Units.
articles.abstract: Background Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have become foundational therapies for heart failure and chronic kidney disease and are increasingly used in critically ill patients. Their established benefits for kidney and heart health, along with emerging evidence from acute-care settings, indicate growing interest in their potential role in intensive care medicine. However, whether these benefits can be translated to critically ill populations remains uncertain, and concerns regarding safety continue to influence clinical practice. Summary Clinical evidence supporting the use of SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) during acute illness is expanding. Benefits have been most consistently observed in acute heart failure, perioperative care, and renal outcomes, where randomized and observational studies suggest improved decongestion, reduced acute kidney injury, and favorable cardiorenal outcomes. These observations are supported by several biological effects of SGLT2i that extend beyond glucose lowering, including modulation of fluid balance, renal hemodynamics, metabolic adaptation, inflammation, and endothelial function-pathways that are central to the development of organ dysfunction during critical illness. However, important uncertainties remain regarding which critically ill patients are most likely to benefit, whether chronic therapy should be continued during acute illness, and how potential benefits should be balanced against safety concerns in the ICU. This review integrates current mechanistic and clinical evidence, examines the balance between potential benefits and risks, discusses practical management considerations, and highlights key research priorities to better define the role of SGLT2i in critical care medicine.   Key Messages - SGLT2 inhibitors show promise in critical care but are not established therapies. - Cardiorenal benefits must be balanced against metabolic and hemodynamic risks. - Future research should define the right patient, the right timing, and the right treatment strategy.

articles.title: Clinical prediction models in cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is a frequent postoperative complication associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Clinical prediction models (CPM) may identify high-risk patients enabling targeted preventive interventions and improved outcomes. The objective of the study was to identify available CPMs for the risk of developing CSA-AKI and summarize their performance. A systematic search of studies published in Pubmed, Scopus, the Chocrane Library and Web of Science was conducted, including studies that developed or validated CPMs for CSA-AKI in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. Data were extracted by two independent reviewers. Summary measures of diagnostic performance were calculated when feasible using random-effects models. Calibration and sensitivity analyses were also performed. The pooled incidence of CSA-AKI was 26.3% (95% CI, 26.0-26.4), whereas CSA-AKI requiring renal replacement therapy (CSA-AKI RRT) occurred in 2.2% of patients (95% CI, 2.1-2.2). Among validated CPMs, Thakar 2005 demonstrated the best predictive performance for CSA-AKI RRT: pooled AUC 0.80 (95% CI, 0.77-0.82), sensitivity of 0.87, and a specificity of 0.49 at a threshold of ≥ 3 points. Calibration analyses indicated underestimation of risk. The Mehta 2006 and Wijeysundera 2007 models also demonstrated good discrimination. Discrimination for the prediction of milder stages of CSA-AKI was poorer, but newer models such as the Demirjian 2022 model showed promising performance. Accurate and well-validated CPMs can facilitate risk stratification for CSA-AKI which can influence clinical practice and research. Thakar 2005 demonstrated very good discrimination for predicting CSA-AKI RRT, whereas more validation studies for the prediction of milder stages of CSA-AKI are warranted.

articles.title: Association of Oliguria With Acute Kidney Injury, Chronic Kidney Disease, and Mortality: Determining the Optimal Threshold in Critically Ill Patients.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Oliguria is a key prognostic indicator of acute kidney injury (AKI), yet the consensus definition (< 0.5 mL/kg/hr) is increasingly questioned. We aimed to determine thresholds of lowest mean diuresis (LMD) associated with AKI, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and mortality. DESIGN: Retrospective observational study. SETTING: Uppsala University Hospital ICU, Sweden. PATIENTS: A total of 4999 adults (≥ 18 yr) without preexisting CKD admitted to the ICU between 2017 and 2024. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: LMD was calculated over 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours (LMD3h-LMD24h). Generalized additive models were used, adjusting for Simplified Acute Physiology Score 3 estimated mortality ratio and gender. Outcomes were AKI within 7 days of LMD (Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes creatinine criteria), incident CKD after ICU discharge, and 90-day mortality. All LMD time frames were significantly associated with AKI, CKD, and death (p < 0.0001). Thresholds for AKI were 0.43, 0.41, 0.42, and 0.53 mL/kg/hr; for CKD, 0.21, 0.21, 0.31, and 0.43 mL/kg/hr; and for mortality 0.16, 0.18, 0.24, and 0.39 across LMD3h-LMD24h. CONCLUSIONS: The risk of mortality or persistent kidney injury, reflected by incident CKD, increases at a lower urine output threshold than the current AKI definition. These findings support the idea of filtration deficit, urine output, and tissue injury as different dimensions of AKI and should influence future AKI definitions.

articles.title: Fluid Therapy in Mechanically Ventilated Critically Ill Adult Patients.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Fluid therapy is ubiquitous in the intensive care unit (ICU) but carries risks, especially in mechanically ventilated patients. Contemporary global practice across dose, indication, and type is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To characterize ICU fluid practices in mechanically ventilated adults. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: International prospective observational cohort study between April 2024 and July 2025, across 206 ICUs in 41 countries on 6 continents. Consecutive adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation within 3 days of ICU admission and ventilated 24 hours or more. Exclusion criteria were age younger than 16 years and transfer under mechanical ventilation from another ICU. EXPOSURES: Fluid volume, indication, and type after intubation. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Key measures included (1) total infused volume and daily fluid balance over 7 days after intubation; (2) the indication for fluid therapy over the first 3 days after intubation; (3) the proportion of total administered fluid volume attributable to each fluid type over the first 3 days after intubation. RESULTS: Among 2454 patients analyzed (median age, 63 years [IQR, 49-73 years]; 63.6% [1560] male), median daily fluid input peaked on day 1 at 3.0 L (IQR, 2.2-4.0 L) and declined to 2.6 L (IQR, 1.8-3.5 L) through day 6. Daily fluid balance (median, 0.9 L; IQR, 0.1-1.9 L on day 1) decreased to less than 0.3 L (IQR, -0.5 to 1.2 L) by day 3 and remained near-neutral through day 6. Maintenance and replacement fluids (to meet daily requirements and to correct ongoing losses; 31.9%) and creep fluids (to deliver medications and maintain catheter patency; 30.9%) were the primary indications, whereas resuscitation (to restore circulating blood volume; 16.0%) accounted for a smaller proportion. Isotonic balanced crystalloids (48.9%) and isotonic saline (0.9% sodium chloride) (27.0%) were common; colloids were rare (1.3%). Substantial between-site variation persisted after adjustment for case-mix. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this prospective international cohort study, fluid therapy varied widely among mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, with maintenance and creep fluids-rather than resuscitation fluids-accounting for most total volume.

articles.title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Amikacin and Monte Carlo Simulation Study in Critically Ill Septic Patients Undergoing Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy with CytoSorb(®) or oXiris(®).
articles.abstract: Background: Adsorptive devices, including CytoSorb® and oXiris®, are increasingly added to continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in septic patients, but their effect on amikacin clearance and exposure is unknown. We characterized amikacin pharmacokinetics (PK) during adsorptive CRRT and derived dosing implications. Methods: A population PK model was developed in 24 critically ill septic patients (using NONMEM ver. 7.5.0), separating intrinsic clearance (CL_int) from filter-specific extracorporeal clearance (CL_CRRT). Sparse pre-filter sampling was handled using informative priors for distribution parameters. Robustness was assessed by sampling-importance-resampling (SIR) and prediction-corrected visual predictive checks (pcVPC). Monte Carlo simulations (9000 subjects) evaluated probability of target attainment (PTA; Cmax/MIC ≥ 8, AUC24/MIC ≥ 75) and cumulative fraction of response (CFR) against four Gram-negative pathogens across three regimens (500 mg q8h, 500 mg q24h, 1500 mg q24h), two filters, and three connection times. Results: While connected, the CytoSorb® and oXiris® CRRT configurations increased amikacin clearance by 61% and 93%, respectively, accounting for 38-48% of total clearance (CL_TOT). Because these devices were only applied for 10-14 h per 24 h interval in simulated scenarios, there were only minor differences in target attainment. Hence, dosing regimen, not device type or connection timing, dominated. Only amikacin at 1500 mg once daily achieved CFR ≥ 90%, and only for susceptible Enterobacterales. Conclusions: Adsorptive CRRT configurations substantially increase extracorporeal amikacin clearance. These exploratory findings support high-dose, once-daily, concentration-guided amikacin dosing during adsorptive CRRT, although this dose may be insufficient against pathogens with elevated MICs.

articles.title: Evaluation of Chromium Picolinate Supplementation and Insulin Requirements in Critically Ill Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.journal: The Journal of pharmacy technology : jPT : official publication of the Association of Pharmacy Technicians
articles.abstract: Chromium picolinate has been studied as an adjunct to improve glycemic indices in ambulatory type 2 diabetes mellitus, but its role in critically ill patients is unknown. To evaluate whether chromium picolinate supplementation was associated with reduced insulin requirements without worsening glycemic control in critically ill adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. We conducted a single-center retrospective pre-post cohort study of adult intensive care unit patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus or hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5% who received insulin and at least 4 consecutive chromium picolinate doses between July 2022 and January 2023. Patients served as their own controls during 24-hour pre- and post-chromium periods. The primary outcome was change in total daily insulin dose. Secondary outcomes included proportion of measured glucose values within 140 to 180 mg/dL, acute kidney injury, hypoglycemia, and exploratory Sequential Organ Failure Assessment-2 change. Among 91 screened patients, 45 met the inclusion criteria. Median total daily insulin dose decreased from 76.3 U/d (interquartile range [IQR], 40.1-96.9) before chromium to 40.0 U/d (IQR, 20.5-65.6) after chromium; the Hodges-Lehmann paired difference was -23.0 U/d (95% CI, -33.25 to -14.25; P < .0001). Proportion of measured glucose values within target did not differ significantly. No post-intervention hypoglycemia was observed, and 2 patients met the study-defined acute kidney injury criterion. Interpretation is limited by the retrospective design and absence of a concurrent control group. Chromium picolinate supplementation was associated with lower insulin requirements without worsening glycemic control. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in prospective controlled studies.

articles.title: Dynamic course and outcomes of acute-on-chronic liver failure in the intensive care unit : Insights from a real-world cohort.
articles.abstract: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) frequently requires intensive care unit (ICU) management, yet real-world data on dynamic disease course, organ support and mortality predictors in critically ill ACLF patients remain scarce. All ACLF patients admitted to a tertiary care hepatology ICU between 2013 and 2023 were analyzed in this retrospective single-center study for ACLF grade trajectories, organ support, and independent predictors of 90-day mortality. Among 209 patients (228 admissions), 54.4% had ACLF grade 3 at ICU admission (median CLIF‑C ACLF 56). Most patients required vasopressors (86.8%), invasive mechanical ventilation (59.6%), and renal replacement therapy (53.5%). The ICU and 90-day survival were 56.1% and 34.2%, respectively. One third of the patients (33.3%) showed improvement in ACLF grade during the ICU stay, including grade 3 patients, indicating meaningful reversibility under comprehensive organ support. The CLIF‑C ACLF score (OR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.03-1.11, p < 0.001) and the peak noradrenaline dose (OR: 13.5, 95% CI: 3.18-69.7, p < 0.001) were identified as independent predictors of 90-day mortality. Critically ill ACLF patients retain potential for partial recovery under full organ support, justifying ICU escalation even in grade 3 disease. Peak noradrenaline dose, alongside the established prognostic scores, provides a readily available parameter to guide individualized decision-making regarding full organ support or timely de-escalation.

articles.title: Associations of base excess and alactic base excess with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 acute kidney injury in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: To identify the associations of base excess (BE) and alactic base excess (aBE) with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 acute kidney injury (AKI) in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). In this cohort study, 1,377 adult patients with AIS were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. A univariable logistic regression model was used to explore the associations of all variables with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI during the ICU stay of patients. Confounding factors were screened using bidirectional stepwise regression. Subgroup analysis was stratified based on age, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA), and comorbidities. Forest plot was plotted to identify the associations of BE and aBE with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI in AIS patients in different subgroups. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) was plotted. A total of 1,377 participants were included, of whom 680 developed KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI during their ICU stay. After adjusting for covariates including SOFA, sodium, anticoagulants, furosemide, and aspirin, we found that the association between BE < -5.124 mmol/L and KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI was significant (OR = 1.51, 95% CI: 1.05 - 2.16). As for aBE, we observed that aBE < -3.444 mmol/L might be related to KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI (OR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.12 - 2.20). In the adjusted model, aBE < -3.444 mmol/L was associated with elevated OR of KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI in AIS patients (OR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.00 - 2.04). RCS revealed the non-liner associations of BE and aBE with KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI in AIS patients. Low BE or aBE were associated with an increased risk of KDIGO stage 2 - 3 AKI in patients with AIS.

articles.title: Opsonic Peptide MOP3 Attenuates Ischemic Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: Renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) induced acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common and serious condition characterized by renal dysfunction, inflammation, tubular injury, and cell death. Extracellular cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (eCIRP) is a damage-associated molecular pattern that contributes to inflammation and tissue injury. MFG-E8-derived oligopeptide 3 (MOP3) is an opsonic peptide that binds eCIRP and promotes its phagocytic clearance. Here, we investigated the therapeutic effects of MOP3 in a murine model of renal I/R-induced AKI. Mice were subjected to 30 minutes of bilateral renal ischemia and treated with MOP3 or vehicle at the onset of reperfusion. Blood and kidney tissues were collected 20 h later. Renal inflammation, kidney function, tubular injury markers, histological damage, and cell death were assessed by RT-qPCR, biochemical assays, Western blotting, hematoxylin and eosin staining, and TUNEL staining. MOP3 treatment reduced circulating eCIRP by 40% and renal IL-6, IL-1β, MIP-2, and KC mRNA expression by 43%, 84%, 73%, and 69%, respectively, compared with vehicle treatment. Serum urea nitrogen, creatinine, and NGAL levels were reduced by 56%, 63%, and 44%, respectively, after MOP3 treatment. MOP3 also decreased renal KIM-1 and NGAL mRNA expression by 88% and 44% and reduced their protein levels by 29% and 45%, respectively. Furthermore, MOP3 attenuated renal tubular injury and decreased TUNEL-positive cells. These findings demonstrate that MOP3 attenuates inflammation, renal dysfunction, tubular injury, and cell death following renal I/R, suggesting that MOP3 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic AKI.

articles.title: The Easiest Decision in the Room: Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in Cirrhosis.
Intradialytic Hemodynamic Instability and Delirium in Critically Ill Patients Receiving Renal Replacement Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT) is common in critically ill patients and is frequently accompanied by delirium. Intradialytic hemodynamic instability, particularly hypotension, may impair cerebral perfusion; however, its quantitative relationship with delirium remains unclear. This study investigated the association between intradialytic hemodynamic instability and Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU)-defined delirium in critically ill patients receiving RRT. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 87 adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients undergoing RRT between September 2025 and May 2026. Delirium was assessed using the CAM-ICU. Intradialytic hemodynamic burden was quantified by the cumulative duration of mean arterial pressure (MAP) < 65 mmHg and the number of hypotensive episodes during RRT. Multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, and admission SOFA score were performed to evaluate the associations between hemodynamic parameters and delirium, while receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were used to assess their discriminative ability. Results: Of 87 patients, 46 (52.9%) were classified as CAM-ICU-positive for delirium. Patients with delirium had a longer cumulative duration of MAP < 65 mmHg (median, 36.0 vs. 5.0 min; p = 0.048) and more hypotensive episodes (median, 3.0 vs. 1.0; p = 0.032). These differences were no longer significant after normalization to the number of RRT sessions (p = 0.153 and p = 0.249). In addition, neither parameter showed a statistically significant association with delirium after adjustment for age, sex, and admission SOFA score. ROC analysis demonstrated limited discriminative ability (AUC, 0.62 and 0.63, respectively). Mechanical ventilation duration, ICU length of stay or ICU mortality did not show a statistically significant association with CAM-ICU positivity in the adjusted models. Sensitivity analyses using alternative functional forms for cumulative MAP < 65 mmHg duration, including log-transformed, categorical, and natural cubic spline models, did not show statistically significant associations with CAM-ICU positivity. Conclusions: Critically ill patients with delirium had greater cumulative intradialytic hypotensive burden; however, these differences were attenuated after accounting for the number of RRT sessions, and the hemodynamic parameters did not show statistically significant associations with delirium in the adjusted regression models. These findings suggest a potential relationship between intradialytic hemodynamic burden and delirium but do not establish an independent or causal association.

articles.title: Improving delivery and quality of renal replacement therapy in the ICU.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects more than half of critically ill patients, and 10-15% require acute renal replacement therapy (RRT). Despite comparable outcomes among appropriately delivered RRT modalities, substantial practice variation persists due to differences in organizational structures, resources availability, and implementation of evidence-bases care. This review summarizes recent advances in quality improvement for acute RRT, including quality frameworks, key performance indicators (KPIs), and implementation science. The Acute Disease Quality Initiative (ADQI) established a framework for evaluating acute RRT quality across structure, process, and outcome domains and developed consensus-based KPIs for continuous RRT (CRRT). Key CRRT quality measures include program leadership, education and training, filter life, treatment downtime, access alarms, dose-intensity, ultrafiltration, adverse events, RRT discontinuation, and ICU mortality. Institutional QI initiatives demonstrate that multidisciplinary collaboration, standardized protocols, electronic medical record integration, and continuous audit and feedback can improve treatment delivery, adherence to evidence-based practices, and resource utilization. Contemporary registries are generating data to validate KPIs, characterize practice variation, and establish performance benchmarks. Quality improvement is essential for optimizing acute RRT delivery. Integrating standardized quality measurement with implementation science provides a practical framework to reduce practice variation, improve RRT delivery, and enhance patient outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical Significance of Klotho, Fibroblast Growth Factor 23, and Their Ratio for Acute Kidney Injury in Sepsis Patients.
articles.journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
articles.abstract: The sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is common in patients with sepsis and associated with poor outcomes, yet serum creatinine and urine output have limited value for early assessment. We examined whether admission Klotho, fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), and the Klotho/FGF23 ratio were associated with SA-AKI and short-term outcomes and compared their discriminative performance. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 320 patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with Sepsis-3-defined sepsis. SA-AKI (n = 112) was retrospectively identified according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Klotho and FGF23 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in stored serum samples collected within 24 h of ICU admission. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis, and adjusted associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Patients with SA-AKI had lower Klotho, higher FGF23, and a reduced Klotho/FGF23 ratio at admission (all p < 0.001). The ratio showed the highest area under the curve biomarkers for SA-AKI (0.84; 95% confidence interval 0.79-0.88) and remained associated with SA-AKI after multivariable adjustment (odds ratio 2.25; 95% confidence interval 1.46-3.53). The ratio decreased with increasing KDIGO stage. Among patients with SA-AKI, a low ratio remained associated with lower 3-month renal recovery, longer ICU and hospital stays, higher in-hospital mortality, and greater 3-month chronic kidney disease progression after adjustment. The admission Klotho/FGF23 ratio was associated with SA-AKI, higher KDIGO stage, and short-term outcomes and showed the highest observed discrimination among the three biomarkers.

articles.title: Association between invasive mechanical ventilation and acute kidney injury in critically ill patients: a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) may contribute to the development and progression of acute kidney injury (AKI) in critically ill patients. Given the expanding evidence-base and the immense variation in the association described, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic era, a rigorous synthesis is warranted. This systematic review and meta-analysis will evaluate this association and identify potential risk-mitigation strategies. We will conduct a comprehensive search of databases, including Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection and the Cochrane Library, using keywords to capture relevant literature on IMV and AKI. The search will include studies published from database inception through March 2026. Two reviewers will independently screen, select and extract studies using the web-based platform Covidence. Eligible studies will include randomised controlled trials reporting the occurrence of new-onset or worsening AKI following initiation of IMV in adult patients admitted to intensive care units. Studies in which IMV was initiated after the onset of AKI will be excluded. Study quality and risk of bias will be assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 Tool. The primary outcome will be the proportion of critically ill patients who develop new-onset or worsening AKI after initiation of IMV. Secondary outcomes will include AKI trajectory, use of organ support and length of stay. Ethics approval is not required, as this study will synthesise data from previously published studies and will not involve direct contact with human participants. The findings will be disseminated through presentations at academic conferences and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. CRD420261303862.

articles.title: Development and validation of a cefepime population pharmacokinetic model to guide treatment for patients with hospital-acquired pneumonia requiring renal replacement.
articles.abstract: Cefepime is used in critically ill pneumonia patients, but dosing in renal replacement therapy (RRT) is complicated by altered renal function, extracorporeal removal, and variability in pulmonary epithelial lining fluid (ELF) exposure. We sought to develop an integrated model linking systemic, extracorporeal, and pulmonary cefepime pharmacokinetics in RRT. Pharmacokinetic (PK) data from critically ill adults receiving cefepime and requiring RRT were included. In a dedicated continuous RRT (CRRT) cohort (n = 8), pre- and post-filter plasma and effluent PK data were collected. Additional patients (n = 43) requiring RRT also contributed plasma and ELF samples. A non-parametric population PK model was developed using an 80/20 subject-level development-validation split. Covariate models assessed the impact of residual renal function, effluent flow rate, body size, and fixed intradialytic hemodialysis (HD) clearance. Monte Carlo simulations evaluated plasma and ELF target attainment across dosing strategies, weight strata, and minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). The final model jointly described systemic, extracorporeal, and pulmonary cefepime disposition using piecewise central volume, native clearance, linear effluent-flow-dependent CRRT clearance, fixed HD clearance, and ELF distribution. Simulations showed adequate plasma target attainment, whereas ELF attainment was sensitive to MIC, target, regimen, and body weight. Continuous infusions of 4 g/day provided adequate ELF attainment at MICs ≤4 mg/L. Plasma-based cefepime target attainment may overestimate pulmonary exposure during RRT, particularly at higher MICs, body weights, and fT>MIC targets. External validation and prospective studies are needed to refine pulmonary target estimates and determine whether plasma-guided Bayesian dosing can reliably ensure site-of-infection exposure.

articles.title: Cerebral microembolic load during continuous versus intermittent renal replacement therapy in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (COMET-AKI).
articles.abstract: Microemboli generated during kidney replacement therapy (KRT) may contribute to cerebro-vascular injury in patients with acute kidney injury. Whether different KRT modalities influence cerebral microembolic burden remains uncertain. In this single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial, intensive care unit patients with dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) were randomized to continue CRRT or convert to intermittent therapy (IRRT). Doppler assessments were performed during baseline CRRT and after randomization during CRRT or during the first IRRT session after a KRT-free interval. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in total cerebral microemboli count between baseline and the post-randomization assessment. Secondary outcomes included cerebral microemboli type and rates, extracorporeal venous microbubble counts and rates, 30-day mortality, and intensive care unit length of stay. The study was terminated early for technical reasons. Thirty-eight patients were analyzed (CRRT, n = 24; IRRT, n = 14). The median between-group difference in total cerebral microemboli count from baseline to post-randomization assessment was -216 events over 30 minutes (95% Confidence Interval (CI) -919 to 246; P = .79). Venous microbubble counts increased during CRRT but decreased during IRRT, with a between-group difference of -36 975 events (95% CI -63 621 to -15 899; P < .001). No significant differences were detected in 30-day mortality or intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay. This exploratory study did not detect a statistically significant difference in cerebral microembolic burden between modalities. Larger studies are needed to clarify the clinical and neurological relevance of microembolization during kidney replacement therapy.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury at a tertiary nephrology referral center: predictors of renal recovery and in-hospital mortality.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a global health problem associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in prevention and management, in-hospital mortality remains high, particularly among critically ill patients. To determine incidence, risk factors of AKI among patients admitted to Mansoura Nephrology and Dialysis Unit (MNDU), a tertiary nephrology referral center in Dakahlia governorate, Egypt, over one year, and to identify predictors of renal recovery at discharge and in-hospital mortality. This prospective observational study was conducted from June 2022 to May 2023 and included adult patients admitted with various kidney disorders. Patients were classified into AKI and non-AKI groups according to KDIGO 2012 criteria. Clinical, laboratory, and outcome data were analyzed, and multivariable regression analyses were used to identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality and renal recovery after AKI. A total of 839 patients were enrolled, including 330 (39.3%) with AKI and 509 (60.7%) without AKI. The most common pathophysiological causes of AKI were pre-renal (54.2%) followed by intrinsic renal (38.5%) one. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher in AKI than non-AKI group (17.3% vs. 3.8%), with septic shock being the leading cause of death (84.2%). Among patients with AKI, 45.2% achieved complete renal recovery, 21.8% had partial recovery, and 33.0% had no recovery at discharge. On multivariable logistic regression analyses, KDIGO Stage 3 AKI (adjusted OR 0.277, P = 0.046), kidney replacement therapy (adjusted OR 0.409, P = 0.004), and requirement of vasopressor therapy (adjusted OR 0.041, P < 0.001) were independently associated with lower odds of renal recovery, whereas necessity of vasopressor therapy emerged as the only independent predictor of in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 420.511, 95% CI 97.451-1814.543; P < 0.001). AKI was common among hospitalized patients and was associated with substantially increased in-hospital mortality. Vasopressor requirement was the strongest independent predictor of mortality, emphasizing the prognostic impact of hemodynamic instability and critical illness severity. Severe AKI (KDIGO Stage 3), kidney replacement therapy, and vasopressor necessity were independently associated with reduced renal recovery at discharge. These readily available clinical indicators may support early risk stratification and guide closer monitoring of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Optimization and Therapeutic Drug Monitoring of Beta-Lactam Antibiotics in Abdominal Sepsis: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Clinical Perspectives-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Background: Abdominal sepsis is associated with profound pharmacokinetic (PK) alterations that make standard beta-lactam dosing regimens potentially inadequate in critically ill patients. Increased volume of distribution, hypoalbuminemia, augmented renal clearance (ARC), acute kidney injury (AKI) and the PK complexity of the peritoneal compartment collectively impair the ability of conventional dosing to achieve pharmacodynamic (PD) targets. These PK derangements are clinically relevant but incompletely characterized in intra-abdominal infections (IAI)- specific cohorts, as most available data derive from broader critically ill populations. Beta-lactam antibiotics, the cornerstone therapy in IAIs, are particularly susceptible to these alterations, especially in the context of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens. Methods: We conducted a structured narrative review of the literature published between 2010 and 2026, searching PubMed and Embase using terms related to pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, therapeutic drug monitoring, beta-lactam antibiotics, abdominal sepsis, and intra-abdominal infection in critically ill patients. Additional references were identified through manual bibliography screening, including seminal studies predating the search window. No formal systematic review methodology was applied. Results: PK/PD optimization in abdominal sepsis can be organized around four proposed domains: extended or continuous infusion of beta-lactams to maximize the time above the minimum inhibitory concentration; therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) to guide individualized dose adjustment in the presence of ARC, AKI, or continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT); tailored dose optimization during CRRT; and target attainment analysis against MDR organisms. Extended and continuous infusions improve PD target attainment and are associated with improved outcomes in some observational studies, although prospective IAI-specific evidence is lacking and the evidence supporting these strategies derives largely from broader intensive care unit populations. Conclusions: In abdominal sepsis, integrating PK/PD principles and TDM-guided dosing represents a pharmacologically rational strategy to optimize beta-lactam exposure and improve target attainment against MDR pathogens. Rigorous IAI-specific prospective studies are needed to establish definitive TDM-guided dosing protocols and translate these pharmacological strategies in this high-acuity setting.

articles.title: Age-Based Preoperative Transthoracic Echocardiography, Intraoperative Hypotension, and Postoperative Outcomes in Older Adults Undergoing Noncardiac Surgery: A Regression Discontinuity Analysis.
articles.abstract: The clinical value of routine preoperative transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) in older adults remains controversial. Existing evidence is largely observational and vulnerable to confounding by indication, limiting causal interpretation of whether preoperative TTE improves intraoperative management and perioperative outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the local effect of routine age-based preoperative TTE using a quasi-experimental design. This single-center retrospective cohort study used a fuzzy regression discontinuity design based on an institutional policy of routine preoperative TTE in patients aged ≥75 years. Eligible patients were aged 60 to 89 years and underwent elective noncardiac surgery under general anesthesia from July 2017 to August 2024. To minimize confounding by indication, patients with guideline-based indications or other clinical conditions likely to prompt preoperative TTE independent of age were excluded. The primary outcome was intraoperative hypotension (IOH), defined as the duration of mean arterial pressure <65 mm Hg. Exploratory secondary outcomes included 30- and 90-day mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), planned and unplanned intensive care unit (ICU) or cardiac care unit (CCU) admission, and postoperative length of hospital stay. Continuity of baseline characteristics and density of the running variable were assessed. Among 7270 patients, the probability of undergoing preoperative TTE increased by 43.1 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], 33.3-52.9) at the 75-year-old cutoff, confirming a strong first-stage discontinuity. The estimated local effect of preoperative TTE on IOH was a 24.8-minute reduction (95% CI, -71.1 to 21.5). Sensitivity analyses using alternative bandwidths and covariate adjustment yielded similar findings. Point estimates for 30-day mortality (-2.1%; 95% CI, -6.0 to 1.8), 90-day mortality (-3.2%; 95% CI, -10.4 to 3.9), and AKI (-3.6%; 95% CI, -15.9 to 8.6) were below zero but imprecise. Point estimates were also below zero for unplanned ICU or CCU admission (-6.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -12.2 to 0.2) and postoperative length of hospital stay (-7.0 days; 95% CI, -14.6 to 0.5). Baseline characteristics and the density of the running variable (age) showed no clear discontinuity at the cutoff. Using a quasi-experimental design that reduces susceptibility to confounding by indication, we found no clear evidence that routine age-based preoperative TTE reduced IOH or improved postoperative outcomes near the threshold. The estimates were imprecise, and clinically meaningful benefit or harm could not be excluded. These findings suggest that age alone may be insufficient to justify routine preoperative TTE and support further evaluation of selective risk-based strategies.

articles.title: Fulminant multi-organ failure associated with cereulide-producing Bacillus cereus after consumption of improperly stored rice.
articles.abstract: A male in his 20s with no medical history was found with generalised seizures and profound hypoglycaemia after consuming improperly stored, reheated rice.Initial laboratory tests showed acute liver failure with hyperammonaemia, acute kidney injury and lactic acidosis, which rapidly progressed to multi-organ failure requiring urgent liver transplantation evaluation.With maximal supportive therapy, including glucose, ammonia and glutamine scavengers, renal replacement therapy, haemodynamic and respiratory support, he gradually improved, avoiding transplantation and achieving full neurological recovery. Toxicological analysis of the rice and serum revealed high concentrations of cereulide, a toxin produced by Bacillus cereus This case illustrates that cereulide intoxication can be associated with potentially fatal multi-organ failure, particularly after ingestion of improperly stored starchy foods.Early recognition through targeted dietary history, focused laboratory evaluation and prompt supportive therapy are essential. Increasing awareness among healthcare professionals and safe food storage practices are key preventive measures.

articles.title: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects of Renal Replacement Therapy in Critically Ill Patients: A Multicenter Observational Study Using a Japanese ICU Registry.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Randomized trials evaluating the timing of renal replacement therapy (RRT) have informed current practice toward more conservative initiation strategies because of the lack of mortality benefit from early initiation. However, the optimal indications for RRT to offer lifesaving benefits remain uncertain. We aimed to estimate heterogeneous treatment effect of RRT and to identify patient groups associated with benefit or harm. DESIGN: Multicenter observational study. SETTING: A nationwide intensive care registry in Japan, Japanese Intensive Care Patient Database. PATIENTS: Adult patients who were admitted to the ICUs from 2018 through 2023 were included, excluding those with end-stage kidney disease, early death, readmission, or normal renal function. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Exposure was RRT during the ICU stay. Hospital mortality was the primary outcome. After 1:1 propensity score matching to adjust for confounding, 18,794 patients (9,397 per group) were analyzed. On average, RRT was associated with higher hospital mortality (risk difference, 6.1% points [95% CI, 3.4-8.7]). However, our machine learning-based causal forest algorithm showed substantial heterogeneity of treatment effects heterogeneity of treatment effects (HTEs) (rank-weighted average treatment effect, -8.2 percentage points [95% CI, -9.7 to -6.7]). Patients characterized by elevated serum creatinine, reduced urine output, and elevated blood urea nitrogen levels showed potential mortality benefit from RRT, whereas relatively preserved renal function was more likely to be associated with harm. CONCLUSIONS: Although RRT was associated with an increased risk of hospital mortality overall, HTEs were identified in selected subgroups that may benefit from RRT. These findings support a data-driven approach to defining clinically applicable optimal RRT indications to guide more judicious use of RRT.
articles.ai_key_stats: n=18,794, risk difference 6.1% points (95% CI 3.4-8.7), HTEs rank-weighted average treatment effect -8.2 percentage points (95% CI -9.7 to -6.7)
articles.ai_summary: This study used a large Japanese ICU registry to investigate the effects of renal replacement therapy (RRT) on hospital mortality. While RRT was associated with higher hospital mortality overall, the study found that certain subgroups of patients may benefit from RRT, such as those with elevated serum creatinine, reduced urine output, and elevated blood urea nitrogen levels.
articles.ai_significance: These findings suggest that RRT may not be beneficial for all critically ill patients, and that a more nuanced approach to its use is needed, taking into account individual patient characteristics.

articles.title: Net Ultrafiltration Rate and Mortality in Critically Ill Patients: A Multicenter Cohort Study With Analysis of Fluid Balance Changes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between net ultrafiltration (NUF) rate and fluid balance changes with 28-day mortality in critically ill patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). DESIGN: Multicenter retrospective observational study. SETTING: Data from two European mixed medical-surgical ICUs: University Hospital Bern, Switzerland, and Amsterdam University Medical Center, the Netherlands. PATIENTS: Adult critically ill patients receiving CRRT for at least 24 hours. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We studied 973 critically ill adults undergoing a total of 6914 days of CRRT. NUF rates and fluid balance changes were calculated from hourly data and categorized into four predefined groups. NUF rates were classified as no NUF, low (< 1.01 mL/kg/h), moderate (1.01-1.75 mL/kg/h), or high (> 1.75 mL/kg/h). Fluid balance change was stratified as negative (< -1.5 L/day), moderate negative (-1.5 to -0.5 L/day), neutral (-0.5 to 0.5 L/day), or positive (> 0.5 L/day). Using multivariable regression, random forest modeling, and mediation analysis, we observed no independent association between NUF rate and 28-day mortality after accounting for fluid balance. Mediation analysis suggested that the apparent survival advantage observed among patients with higher NUF rates was largely mediated through achievement of a more negative fluid balance, rather than a direct effect of NUF rate itself. In contrast, more positive fluid balance changes were linked to adverse clinical outcomes including 28-day mortality. CONCLUSIONS: In this two-center cohort of CRRT patients, NUF rate was not independently associated with mortality. Instead, the key determinant of outcome was fluid balance change. These findings suggest clinicians should not make NUF decisions in isolation, but rather should be using NUF as a means to achieve patient-specific fluid balance targets.
articles.ai_key_stats: n=973, no independent association between NUF rate and 28-day mortality, fluid balance change linked to adverse outcomes including 28-day mortality
articles.ai_summary: This study investigated the relationship between net ultrafiltration rate and fluid balance changes in critically ill patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy. The results showed that fluid balance change, not net ultrafiltration rate, was the key determinant of outcome. The study found that more positive fluid balance changes were linked to adverse clinical outcomes.
articles.ai_significance: These findings suggest that clinicians should prioritize achieving patient-specific fluid balance targets over focusing solely on net ultrafiltration rate in critically ill patients receiving CRRT.

articles.title: Decades of intensive care medicine trials: what randomised evidence has changed, corrected, and still questions to resolve.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) have reshaped intensive care medicine (ICM), a discipline defined by acute, interacting organ failures, time-sensitive decisions, biological uncertainty, and heterogeneous recovery trajectories. Many interventions supported by strong physiological rationale failed to improve patient-centred outcomes, whereas durable advances often emerged from optimisation of supportive care, avoidance of iatrogenic harm, and reassessment of established practices. METHODS: We conducted an interpretive historical review of landmark multicentre RCTs in adult ICM from the early 1990s onwards. PubMed searches, reference lists from major trials and reviews, and international guidelines were used to identify trials with conceptual influence on practice, guidelines, physiological reasoning, therapeutic strategy, research priorities, de-implementation, or outcome framing. Evidence was organised into overlapping paradigms rather than rigid chronological periods. FINDINGS: Across haemodynamic support, mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, antimicrobial treatment, nutrition, glucose control, transfusion, and sedation, landmark RCTs describe more than therapeutic expansion. Early biological and haemodynamic trials exposed the limits of reductionist strategies in syndromic critical illness. Protocol-driven approaches improved timeliness and consistency, but later pragmatic trials showed that rigid targets and invasive algorithms often added little once high-quality usual care was established. More recent trials challenge the assumption that greater intervention intensity improves outcomes, emphasising timing, disease phase, baseline risk, heterogeneity, patient selection, and treatment-related harm. Modern ICM RCTs have clarified not only what works, but what can be reduced, delayed, avoided, or applied selectively. Future progress requires biologically informed, context-sensitive trials focussed on meaningful survival, recovery, and long-term function.

articles.title: Associations between advanced lung cancer inflammation index score and kidney outcomes in intensive care unit patients with diabetes: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.abstract: ObjectiveAcute kidney injury is commonly observed in critically ill patients with diabetes and is associated with adverse outcomes. The advanced lung cancer inflammation index score, which reflects nutritional and inflammatory status, has not been well studied in relation to acute kidney injury and subsequent kidney events in this population.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. Adult intensive care unit patients with diabetes were included. Associations of log-transformed advanced lung cancer inflammation index scores with acute kidney injury and major adverse kidney events within 30 days were assessed using logistic regression and Cox models, respectively. Restricted cubic spline analyses, eXtreme gradient boosting with SHapley Additive exPlanations interpretation, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate model-based contribution, effect modification, and robustness.ResultsIn total, 2337 critically ill patients with diabetes were included in the acute kidney injury occurrence analysis, of whom 1624 developed acute kidney injury. Each 1-SD increase in log-transformed advanced lung cancer inflammation scores was associated with lower odds of acute kidney injury (odds ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.81-0.99). Among the 1624 patients with acute kidney injury, 750 developed major adverse kidney events within 30 days. Higher log-transformed advanced lung cancer inflammation index scores were associated with a lower hazard of major adverse kidney events within 30 days (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.82-0.96). Dose-response analyses revealed a consistent inverse association between the advanced lung cancer inflammation index score and adverse kidney outcomes, particularly major adverse kidney events within 30 days. Machine-learning interpretation supported the contribution of the advanced lung cancer inflammation index score to model output for kidney outcomes, and sensitivity analyses yielded similar results.ConclusionsAmong intensive care unit patients with diabetes, higher advanced lung cancer inflammation index scores were associated with lower odds of acute kidney injury and a lower hazard of major adverse kidney events within 30 days after acute kidney injury. The advanced lung cancer inflammation index score may serve as a simple marker for inflammation and nutritional status associated with short-term kidney outcomes; however, its clinical utility requires validation in independent cohorts.

articles.title: Management of renal failure in earthquake-related crush syndrome: Multicenter intensive care outcomes.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: Crush syndrome (CS) is a clinical condition associated with multisystem organ dysfunction that develops after traumatic rhabdomyolysis and primarily affects the kidneys. The aim of this study was to characterize the incidence, risk factors, and treatment patterns of acute kidney injury (AKI) in earthquake victims with CS, with a particular focus on renal replacement therapy (RRT) use and clinical outcomes. In this retrospective multicenter study, 247 adult patients with earthquake-related CS who were admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) in 22 hospitals after the Kahramanmaraş 2023 earthquakes were analyzed. Demographic data, injury patterns, laboratory parameters, treatment protocols, and outcomes were evaluated during the first 15 days following ICU admission. AKI developed in 78.5% (n=194) of patients, and RRT was required in 62.4% (n=121) of those with AKI. Multiple logistic regression analysis demonstrated that myoglobin and creatinine levels were associated with an elevated risk of developing AKI (odds ratio [OR]: 1.001; 95% confidence interval CI: 1.000-1.001 and OR: 1.735; 95% CI: 1.151-2.615, respectively). Similarly, creatinine level and reasons for ICU admission were identified as factors influencing RRT administration. (OR: 1.7; 95% CI: 1.28-2.15 and OR: 2.9; 95% CI: 1.26-6.90, respectively). The 30-day mortality rate was higher in patients with AKI than in those without AKI. Mortality rates were similar between patients with AKI who received RRT and those who did not. This study demonstrates the high incidence of AKI in earthquake-related CS, underscores the need for improved disaster preparedness with adequate dialysis capacity and early risk stratification using serum myoglobin and creatinine levels for optimal management.

articles.title: Retrospective Cohort Study on the Association Between a Laboratory Test-Derived Frailty Index and Mortality in Elderly Critically Ill Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a growing worldwide health concern. There is a need for easily obtainable markers that can improve risk evaluation in affected patients. Here, we investigated whether a laboratory-derived frailty index (FI-Lab) carries prognostic information for older CKD individuals admitted to intensive care. A retrospective cohort design was adopted, drawing on the MIMIC-IV repository. Records of elderly ICU patients with diagnosed CKD were retrieved. The endpoints of interest were all-cause death within 30 and 90 days. Cox proportional hazards regression with incremental covariate adjustment and propensity score matching were employed to quantify the independent contribution of FI-Lab to survival. The analytic sample consisted of 5013 hospitalized CKD patients (mean age 77.9 ± 7.6 years; 61.4% male). Following full adjustment, a 0.1-unit rise in FI-Lab corresponded to a 94% higher mortality risk at 30 days (HR 1.94; 95% CI 1.57-2.40) and a 65% higher risk at 90 days (HR 1.65; 95% CI 1.43-1.91; both p < 0.001). Propensity-matched analyses yielded comparable estimates. No meaningful association emerged between FI-Lab and ICU or hospital length of stay. Conversely, higher FI-Lab values were accompanied by greater odds of acute kidney injury and continuous renal replacement therapy utilization. An elevated FI-Lab score at ICU entry is independently tied to elevated short- and intermediate-term mortality in older critically ill patients with CKD. Confirmatory prospective work is needed to establish its clinical role in this population.

articles.title: Ethylene Glycol Poisoning Without Fomepizole in a Regional Australian Intensive Care Unit: The Lactate Gap as the Diagnostic Key and the Consequences of Nasogastric Ethanol Therapy.
articles.abstract: A 62-year-old man presented comatose with pH 6.88 and no ingestion history. A point-of-care lactate above 31 mmol/L with a laboratory lactate of 0.8 mmol/L revealed a lactate gap, diagnosing ethylene glycol poisoning despite a near-normal osmolar gap. High-dose continuous renal replacement therapy corrected the acidosis; he survived.

articles.title: Characterization of an Unusual Severe Yellow Fever Outbreak in the Colombian Andean Region.
articles.abstract: Yellow fever (YF) reemerged in Colombia's Andean region during 2024-2025, outside the country's historically recognized endemic areas. We characterized critically ill adults admitted during this outbreak and described clinical features, organ dysfunction, supportive care, and in-hospital outcomes. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of consecutive adults with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)-confirmed YF admitted to the national referral intensive care unit in Ibagué, Tolima, Colombia, from March through September 2025. Clinical, laboratory, complication, intervention, and outcome data were prospectively captured using a standardized case report form. Sixty-one patients were analyzed; 22 died (36.1%). Non-survivors had lower platelet counts and fibrinogen and higher INR, aminotransferases, lactate dehydrogenase, and creatinine at ICU admission. Shock, acute kidney injury, acute respiratory distress syndrome, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and severe bleeding were more frequent among non-survivors. Prior YF vaccination was self-reported by 10 patients (16.4%). Severe YF in this Andean outbreak was characterized by hepatic-coagulation abnormalities and multisystem organ dysfunction. The occurrence of critical illness outside historically recognized endemic areas supports surveillance and vaccination strategies that can adapt to changing epidemiological risk.

articles.title: Circulating NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation Is Associated With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury and Disease Severity: A Prospective Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is a severe and prevalent complication in critically ill patients, characterized by high mortality and a lack of reliable biomarkers that reflect inflammatory pathway activation and disease severity. Although the NLRP3 inflammasome is known to mediate inflammatory responses, pyroptosis, and renal injury, its clinical relevance in human SA-AKI remains poorly defined. This study aimed to characterize the expression profiles, dynamic trajectories, and clinical associations of circulating NLRP3 inflammasome components in patients with SA-AKI. Thirty adult patients with sepsis (13 with SA-AKI and 17 without AKI) were prospectively and consecutively enrolled. Sepsis was defined according to the Sepsis-3 consensus criteria, whereas AKI was diagnosed and staged exclusively using the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Serum protein levels of NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, cleaved caspase-1, IL-1β, and IL-18, and transcript levels of NLRP3, ASC, and caspase-1, were determined on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 after enrollment using ELISA and quantitative real-time PCR. Statistical analyses included group comparisons, Spearman rank correlations, linear mixed-effects models, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses to assess concurrent group discrimination. Because samples were collected post-classification, these analyses describe post-diagnostic expression kinetics rather than prediction of future AKI onset. The expression of NLRP3 inflammasome-related molecules was significantly upregulated in the SA-AKI group and correlated with renal dysfunction and elevated illness-severity scores (SOFA and APACHE II). Exploratory ROC analyses suggested strong discrimination of concurrent AKI status for ASC, caspase-1, and NLRP3 transcript levels, with the strongest overall performance observed on day 3. These estimates are hypothesis-generating because of the small sample size and post-classification sampling. The NLRP3 inflammasome pathway is prominently activated in patients with SA-AKI and is closely associated with renal dysfunction and systemic illness severity. Circulating components of this pathway are candidate biomarkers of concurrent SA-AKI, but their ability to predict AKI onset or prognosis requires validation in larger prospective cohorts sampled before AKI develops.

articles.title: When Hydronephrosis Was Not Physiological: A Case of Septic Shock Secondary to Obstructive Uropathy in Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Urosepsis in pregnancy is a life-threatening condition requiring early recognition, rapid multidisciplinary escalation and timely source control. Physiological hydronephrosis is common during pregnancy and may obscure clinically significant urinary tract obstruction. We report a 26-year-old gravida 5 para 3 woman at 30 weeks' gestation who presented with severe right-sided loin pain. Initial ultrasound demonstrated moderate right hydronephrosis without a visible calculus. Within hours, she deteriorated with pyrexia, acute kidney injury, lactic acidosis and septic shock. Computed tomography demonstrated high-grade obstruction of the right renal collecting system secondary to a ureteropelvic junction calculus with associated inflammatory change. Following maternal deterioration and evidence of foetal compromise, an urgent multidisciplinary decision was made to proceed with category 1 caesarean delivery followed by cystoscopy and right ureteric stent insertion. Cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae. The patient subsequently required intensive care support including invasive ventilation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy and treatment for disseminated intravascular coagulation. Both maternal and neonatal outcomes were favourable. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing physiological hydronephrosis from pathological obstruction in pregnancy and emphasises the importance of source control in infected obstructive uropathy.

articles.title: Early postoperative galectin-3 for risk stratification of delayed graft function after kidney transplantation.
articles.abstract: Delayed graft function (DGF) is a major early complication after kidney transplantation. Galectin-3 (Gal3), a mediator of inflammation and fibrosis, is associated with renal injury, but its role in predicting DGF remains unclear. This study evaluated whether early postoperative Gal3 levels predict DGF and clinical outcomes. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult kidney transplant recipients from deceased donors (January 2021-December 2022). Gal3 was measured preoperatively, at intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and at ICU discharge. The primary outcome was DGF, defined as renal replacement therapy within 7 days. A base clinical model (age, cold ischemia time, creatinine at ICU admission) was compared with a Gal3-extended model, assessed by area under the curve (AUC), Brier score, calibration, bootstrap optimism correction, and categorical net reclassification improvement. Among 182 patients, 35 (19.2%) developed DGF. Gal3 at ICU admission was significantly higher in DGF patients (52.3 vs. 40.0 ng/ml, P < .001) and was independently associated with DGF (odds ratio per 5-ng/ml increase: 1.19; 95% confidence interval: 1.05-1.35; P = .008). Adding Gal3 modestly improved the AUC from 0.705 to 0.744 and the Brier score from 0.144 to 0.139. The Gal3-extended model retained superior discrimination after bootstrap correction. An exploratory prediction score demonstrated increasing DGF risk across score categories. Gal3 measured at ICU admission was independently associated with DGF and provided modest incremental risk-stratification value. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury with Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) Scoring Versus Renal Resistive Index (RRI) in Patients Undergoing On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: The diagnosis of acute kidney injury (AKI) using conventional markers such as serum creatinine and urine output is often delayed, prompting interest in bedside ultrasound-based predictors. This study compared renal resistive index (RRI) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) scoring for early prediction of AKI after on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). In this prospective observational study, 180 adult patients were enrolled. RRI and VExUS assessments were performed preoperatively and within 3 hours of cardiothoracic ICU admission. AKI was diagnosed within 48 hours postoperatively using kidney disease: improving global outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed for RRI and VExUS parameters, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using area under ROC curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity. AKI occurred in 48 patients (26.7%). Postoperative RRI showed excellent discrimination for AKI (AUROC 0.854; cut-off ≥0.68: sensitivity 75%, specificity 86%, negative predictive value [NPV] 90.5%), outperforming preoperative RRI (AUROC 0.681). VExUS showed limited predictive performance (preoperative AUROC 0.588; postoperative AUROC 0.623). The baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in the AKI group was significantly lower than in the patients who did not develop AKI [70.3 ml/min/1.73 m2 vs 79.4 ml/min/1.73 m2]. Diabetes mellitus was more common in the AKI group (62.5% vs 35.6%, P = 0.002). Postoperative urine output remained significantly lower in AKI patients on day 1 and day 2 (P < 0.001). Postoperative RRI ≥ 0.68 demonstrated the best predictive performance for early AKI in our cohort, outperforming preoperative RRI, ΔRRI or change in RRI, and VExUS scores, supporting the predominant role of intrarenal arterial hemodynamic alterations in early postoperative renal injury.

articles.title: Incidence and Predictors of Acute Kidney Injury Among Postoperative Cardiac Surgery Patients in Tanzania.
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is a severe postoperative complication linked to increased morbidity and mortality. Data on the incidence and predictors of CSA-AKI in sub-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania, are limited. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of AKI in patients who underwent cardiac surgery at Tanzania's National Cardiac Institute. This prospective study included 177 patients. AKI was defined using the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria based on serum creatinine (SCr) changes at 24, 48, and 72 h postoperatively. The patients' clinical profiles were collected and analyzed using SPSS version 27.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Chi-square tests and modified Poisson regression were used to identify associated factors at 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with P < 0.05. The prevalence of postoperative AKI was 53%, with the majority of patients presenting with AKI stage I (72.9%). In the multivariable analysis, diabetes mellitus (Adjusted Prevalence Ratio (aPR )1.32, 95% CI 1.02-1.70; P = 0.038), American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) IV status (aPR 1.39, 95% CI 1.10-1.76; P = 0.007), blood transfusion (transfusion: aPR 3.63, 95% CI 1.15-11.41; P = 0.027), triple components (aPR 3.41, 95% CI 1.08-10.78; P = 0.037), and prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time of 181-240 min (aPR 3.53, 95% CI 1.51-8.25; P = 0.004) and > 240 min (aPR 3.80, 95% CI 1.57-9.18; P = 0.003) were independent predictors of AKI. Female sex was independently associated with a lower prevalence of AKI (aPR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.88; P = 0.004). Patients who developed AKI had significantly longer stays in the intensive care unit (ICU) (aPR 2.39, 95% CI 1.39-4.12; P = 0.002). The prevalence of CSA-AKI is remarkably high in this setting, posing a significant clinical burden. Key preoperative and intraoperative predictors were also identified. These results reinforce the importance of perioperative patient optimization, strategies to minimize CPB exposure, transfusion practice optimization, and surveillance of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Three-Point Bedside Congestion Score (IJV Collapsibility + IVC Collapsibility + Central Venous Pressure) in Elective Mitral Valve Surgery: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Systemic venous congestion and right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction are key drivers of postoperative hemodynamic instability, prolonged ventilation, and acute kidney injury (AKI) after mitral valve surgery. Comprehensive echocardiography is informative but may be impractical in high-throughput pre-anesthesia workflows. We evaluated a pragmatic three-point bedside congestion score combining internal jugular vein (IJV) collapsibility, inferior vena cava (IVC) collapsibility, and invasively measured central venous pressure (CVP) for preoperative risk stratification. In this prospective, observational, single-center study, 100 consecutive adults (>18 years) undergoing elective mitral valve surgery for mitral stenosis were enrolled. A bedside ultrasound was performed in the preoperative area with patients in a 45° head-elevated position during quiet, spontaneous respiration. One point was assigned for each abnormal component (IJV collapsibility <18%, IVC collapsibility <25%, and CVP >12 mmHg), yielding a total score of 0 to 3. Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) was dichotomized at 17 mm. Outcomes included vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay, AKI, and in-hospital mortality. Discrimination for AKI and mortality was evaluated using a 5-fold cross-validated receiver operating characteristic (ROC) area under the curve (AUC) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Calibration was assessed using recalibration intercept and slope, and decision curve analysis was used to explore clinical net benefit across threshold probabilities. The observed score distribution concentrated at 0 to 2 and 3; therefore, patients were analyzed as low score (0 to 2; n = 50) versus high score (3; n = 50). Compared with low-score patients, high-score patients had higher postoperative VIS (median 18.0 vs 10.0), longer ventilation (31.5 vs 22.0 hours), longer ICU stay (10.0 vs 5.5 days), and longer hospital stay (23.0 vs 12.5 days). AKI occurred in 40% versus 20%, and mortality in 10% versus 2% in high- versus low-score groups. In the combined 2 × 2 stratification, low score with normal TAPSE had no AKI or mortality, whereas high score with abnormal TAPSE had AKI in 55.6% and mortality in 14.8%. The combined score + TAPSE model showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.77 for AKI; AUC 0.782 for mortality) with near-ideal calibration in this dataset. Decision curve analysis suggested a higher net benefit for the combined model than single-predictor models across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.05 to 0.30. A simple three-point bedside congestion score stratifies postoperative risk after elective mitral valve surgery. Incorporating TAPSE into preoperative assessment provided a rapid and reliable means of excluding significant RV dysfunction, thereby reinforcing the validity of the threepoint scoring system. Multicenter external validation and evaluation of score-guided perioperative protocols are warranted.

articles.title: From manual to digital: prospective ICU evaluation of the FIZE kUO(®) for continuous urine output measurement.
articles.abstract: ICU nurses manage complex, time-sensitive care while also performing frequent manual tasks. Manual urine output (UO) measurement is one such task that remains labor-intensive, interruptive to workflow, and prone to delays - despite the need for timely and accurate recording. Automation may reduce this burden and improve consistency of monitoring. The FIZE kUO® is an electronic urinometer designed to provide continuous, real-time UO data without requiring manual handling. We conducted a prospective, single-center pilot study to evaluate the usability, workflow impact, and safety of the FIZE kUO® device in 10 critically ill patients. Nurses completed staged questionnaires before, during, and after use to assess perceptions of manual monitoring versus automated monitoring. Device performance and adverse events were documented throughout monitoring. Nursing staff reported positive perceptions regarding ease of setup (84-87%), time saving (74%), and improved recognition of changes in UO (87%). At treatment completion, 88.9% of nurses indicated the system prevented missing data, and 78% reported it facilitated earlier identification of situations requiring intervention. The device provided continuous monitoring for a total of 1,263 patient-hours, with no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events observed.
