Automating urine output monitoring was perceived by nurses as beneficial for workflow efficiency, data reliability, and clinical awareness. Nurses perceived the FIZE kUO® to reduce repetitive manual tasks and support timely decision-making. These findings support the potential of automated UO monitoring to alleviate components of ICU nursing workload.

articles.title: Transaxillary access for ascending aortic and root surgery: a single-center comparison with full and partial sternotomy.
articles.abstract: Minimally invasive approaches for ascending aortic and root surgery remain controversial regarding operative complexity and safety. The transaxillary (TAX) approach avoids sternotomy entirely but has not been compared with both full sternotomy (FS) and partial upper sternotomy [minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MIC)]. This study evaluates perioperative outcomes across these three access strategies. Between January 2022 and December 2025, 194 consecutive patients undergoing elective isolated ascending aortic or root surgery were retrospectively analyzed. Surgical access was FS (n=52), MIC (n=106), or TAX (n=36). TAX suitability was assessed by team consensus on electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated computed tomography (CT). Primary endpoints were in-hospital mortality, major complications [Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) composite], and hospital length of stay. TAX was compared with MIC after 1:2 propensity score matching. FS served as descriptive reference. FS patients had higher EuroSCORE II (median 2.7 vs. MIC 2.2 vs. TAX 2.3%, P=0.006). Cardiopulmonary bypass time was longer in TAX {196 [interquartile range (IQR): 175-239] vs. MIC 160 [138-192] vs. FS 172 [140-198] min, P<0.001}, while cross-clamp time did not differ (P=0.34). In-hospital mortality was 3.8% (FS), 0% (MIC), and 0% (TAX). Major complications occurred in 26.9%, 12.3%, and 8.3% (P=0.02), and acute kidney injury (AKI) in 28.8%, 8.5%, and 2.8% (P<0.001). One stroke occurred in the FS group. In the matched cohort (34 TAX vs. 68 MIC), bypass time remained longer in TAX {196 [175-240] vs. 160 [139-190] min, P<0.001}, whereas cross-clamp time, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital stay, major complications (5.9% vs. 11.8%), AKI (2.9% vs. 10.3%), atrial fibrillation, and wound complications did not differ significantly. TAX ascending aortic and root surgery was feasible in carefully selected patients, with no in-hospital mortality, no stroke, and no wound complications. In a propensity-matched comparison with partial upper sternotomy, early outcomes did not differ significantly despite longer bypass time. TAX extends the sternal-sparing concept to the aortic root and ascending aorta and warrants prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Survival outcomes after liver transplantation in acute-on-chronic liver failure: A prospective study.
authors: Investigators of the CHANCE study group
articles.abstract: The impact of liver transplantation (LT) on mortality among patients with advanced cirrhosis who have two organ failures (acute-on-chronic liver failure-2 [ACLF-2]) or ≥ three organ failures (ACLF-3) is unclear. Adults with decompensated cirrhosis with or without ACLF (grades 1-3), undergoing LT at 63 liver transplant centers worldwide were prospectively enrolled between 2021 and 2023 and followed for one year. Patients with ACLF-2 or ACLF-3 who were declined for LT were also prospectively followed for one year. Among the 144 patients declined for LT, 73% of those included with ACLF-2 and 88% of those with ACLF-3 died within 1 year. Of the 612 transplanted patients, 2% were re-transplanted and 12% died during the year. According to ACLF status at LT, the case-fatality rate without re-transplantation was 21% with ACLF-3 (42% when patients had five or six organ failures), 10.5% with ACLF-2, 10% with ACLF-1 (one organ failure), and 9% without ACLF. During the post-LT period, ACLF-3 patients experienced longer intensive care stay but similar ward stay, readmission rate and requirement for long-term renal replacement therapy. In time-to-event multivariable analyses, variables that were associated with higher post-LT mortality were being transplanted in Asia (vs. Europe or North America) or having ACLF-3 at LT (vs. no ACLF). The risk of dying after LT was similar in Asia vs. Latin America or with ACLF-2 vs. no ACLF. Patients with severe ACLF who underwent LT showed markedly better survival outcomes than those who were declined. Patients with five or six organ failures had high risk of post-LT death cautioning against routine LT in this population. ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04613921.

articles.title: Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia: The Role of Kidney-Lung Crosstalk and Renal Replacement Therapy, a Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) results from dynamic inter-organ interactions rather than isolated organ failures. Among these, kidney-lung crosstalk is a key determinant of outcomes in critically ill patients. Acute kidney injury (AKI) promotes pulmonary dysfunction through hemodynamic, inflammatory, endothelial, and metabolic mechanisms, while acute respiratory failure and mechanical ventilation may aggravate renal injury. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) may represent a clinical consequence of these interactions, although causality remains uncertain. Renal replacement therapy (RRT) may further influence kidney-lung crosstalk through several physiological mechanisms. To summarize current evidence on kidney-lung crosstalk, evaluate its potential contribution to VAP susceptibility, and examine the role of RRT in modulating these interactions. Methods: Narrative review of experimental, translational, and clinical studies investigating bidirectional kidney-lung interactions in critical illness. Results: Kidney-to-lung crosstalk involves fluid overload, venous congestion, immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, and metabolic disturbances. Lung-to-kidney signaling is driven by mechanical ventilation, ventilator-induced lung injury, hypoxemia, and hypercapnia. Clinical evidence is strongest for fluid overload, venous congestion, and mechanical ventilation, whereas endothelial dysfunction and uremic toxins remain supported mainly by experimental data. AKI-associated immune dysfunction and prolonged mechanical ventilation provide biologically plausible mechanisms linking AKI to VAP, but definitive causal evidence is lacking because of methodological limitations. RRT may influence these interactions through optimized fluid balance, correction of acid-base disorders, improved antimicrobial pharmacokinetics, and potentially extracorporeal immunomodulation. However, no randomized trial has demonstrated a direct reduction in VAP incidence attributable to RRT. Conclusions: Kidney-lung crosstalk is a major driver of organ dysfunction in critical illness, yet translation into targeted therapies remains limited. Current evidence supports integrated organ-protective strategies-including lung-protective ventilation, individualized fluid management, VAP prevention, and optimized antimicrobial therapy-while future advances will rely on biological phenotyping, biomarker-guided risk stratification, and robust causal inference approaches.

articles.title: JICS Education: Continuous renal replacement therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
articles.abstract: Delivering continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is an integral mode of organ support provided on intensive care units (ICU). This article provides readers with a comprehensive understanding of CRRT, covering indications for therapy and when and how to start it. Supporting this information are practical tips to help improve therapy efficacy and a summary of the current evidence which should underpin clinical decision making.

articles.title: Mechanical Power and Acute Kidney Injury in Mechanically Ventilated Critically Ill Patients: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is highly prevalent among critically ill patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) and is associated with adverse outcomes. Mechanical power (MP) reflects the total energy delivered to the respiratory system, but its association with AKI in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients remains incompletely understood. Few studies have examined the relationship between MP and AKI development. Materials and Methods: Adult patients with MP data available for each of the first five consecutive days of IMV constituted the study population. MP and ventilatory parameters were recorded during this period. Factors independently associated with AKI were identified using multivariable logistic regression. The discriminative performance of MP for AKI and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) use was evaluated. Results: Among 924 patients, 605 (65.5%) developed AKI. MP was consistently higher in patients who developed AKI during the first five days of IMV (11.45 ± 2.88 vs. 9.48 ± 2.50 J/min; p < 0.001). Although PEEP, peak inspiratory pressure, driving pressure, respiratory rate, and FiO2 were higher in the AKI group, tidal volume and respiratory system compliance did not differ significantly. In multivariable analysis, higher mean MP (OR = 1.330, 95% CI 1.235-1.432; p < 0.001), greater mean fluid balance (OR = 1.477, 95% CI 1.225-1.780; p < 0.001), older age, and trauma were independently associated with AKI. MP showed moderate discrimination for AKI (AUC = 0.681), with an optimal cutoff of 10.38 J/min. For CRRT use, MP showed significant but limited discrimination (AUC = 0.624; 95% CI, 0.584-0.664; p < 0.001). Conclusions: In critically ill patients receiving IMV, higher MP remained associated with AKI after adjustment for measured covariates. The 10.38 J/min threshold is hypothesis-generating and requires external validation.

articles.title: Systematic Review of Vancomycin Population Pharmacokinetic Models in Critically Ill Patients: A Focus on Model Characteristics and External Predictive Performance.
articles.abstract: Objective: Several population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) studies of vancomycin in intensive care unit (ICU) patients have been reported. However, substantial heterogeneity exists across these studies, and their predictive performance remains uncertain owing to a lack of external validation. This study systematically reviews published PopPK models of vancomycin in critically ill patients and externally validated selected models using real-world data, with the aim of clarifying factors contributing to variability in vancomycin pharmacokinetic parameters and identifying knowledge gaps that require further investigation. Methods: Databases such as PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies on vancomycin PopPK models in critically ill patients constructed using nonlinear mixed-effects methods. External validation of selected models was performed using the NONMEM software with external datasets. Results: A total of 16 PopPK studies of vancomycin in ICU patients were included. Factors such as renal function indicators, concomitant renal replacement therapy (RRT), and demographic characteristics significantly influenced vancomycin PopPK parameters in ICU patients. Serum creatinine levels and concomitant RRT significantly affected vancomycin clearance, with clearance increasing with higher creatinine clearance or the presence of RRT, whereas body weight significantly influenced the apparent volume of distribution, which increased with increasing body weight. External validation was performed for three of these models, but all models showed unsatisfactory external validation results, with poor predictive capability for the external validation datasets. Conclusions: The reported studies show variations in vancomycin PopPK parameters among ICU patients, with significant inter-individual variability. Clinical dosing should be adjusted based on patients' concomitant therapies, renal function, and body weight. Existing published models lack external validation, and the results of external validation have not been satisfactory. It is recommended that PopPK models undergo external validation to assess their predictive performance before application. Additionally, future research should place greater emphasis on external validation to thoroughly evaluate model performance.

articles.title: Vancomycin dosing in critically ill patients receiving renal replacement therapy: a critical appraisal of the toxicity threshold and external validation.
Epidemiology of Critically Ill Patients With Cirrhosis Undergoing Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Contemporaneous Parallel Analysis of the HRS-HARMONY and CRRTnet Registries.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Describe the epidemiology of patients with cirrhosis/acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) pertaining to process factors including renal replacement dose, modality, and circuit anticoagulation. SETTING: Academic tertiary care hospitals in the United States and Canada. DESIGN AND PATIENTS: We performed a parallel study of contemporaneous data from the HARMONY and CRRT network (CRRTnet) databases to describe the epidemiology and process of CRRT care of cirrhosis/ACLF patients receiving CRRT in the ICU. We evaluated clinical and CRRT process factors (dialysis dose, anticoagulation) with the primary outcome of in-hospital mortality. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The HARMONY cohort (n = 245; median age, 57 yr; 41% female) and CRRTnet cohort (n = 206; 58 yr; 39% female) demonstrated similar overall survival to hospital discharge (HARMONY, 34%; CRRTnet, 30%). In HARMONY, the two most common causes of acute kidney injury (AKI) requiring CRRT were acute tubular necrosis (73%) and hepatorenal syndrome-AKI (13%), with no significant difference between survivors and nonsurvivors (p = 0.24). In HARMONY, higher chronic liver failure-C ACLF scores (hazard ratio, 1.03 [95% CI, 1.01-1.05]; p < 0.001) were independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality. In CRRTnet, the most common CRRT modality was continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration (83.8%), and the most common anticoagulation strategy was regional citrate anticoagulation (58.0%) or no anticoagulation (35.8%). CRRT prescribed dose greater than 30 mL/kg/hr was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (multivariable regression; odds ratio, 2.69; 95% CI, 1.3-5.64; p = 0.01). Of survivors in CRRTnet, 64% were transitioned to intermittent hemodialysis (IHD) before hospital discharge. CONCLUSIONS: Critically ill cirrhosis/ACLF patients initiated on CRRT in the absence of liver transplantation had high in-hospital mortality. These patients were prescribed higher initial CRRT doses (median total effluent > 30 mL/kg/hr), with higher CRRT dose independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality. Of ICU survivors, 64% were transitioned to IHD at ICU discharge. Despite concerns for citrate toxicity, citrate regional anticoagulation was commonly employed in these patients.

articles.title: Landscape of Biomarker Use in Critically Ill Patients: Systematic Evidence Map of Acute Kidney Injury and Implications for Practice.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Create systematic evidence maps of novel biomarkers of kidney injury from a mapping review to guide future implementation in patient care. DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase. STUDY SELECTION: Systematic evidence maps included clinical trials and observational studies in critically ill patients, investigating novel kidney biomarkers for acute kidney injury (AKI). DATA EXTRACTION: Six thousand eight hundred five records were screened, and 1116 studies were included that related to one or more novel biomarkers and AKI. DATA SYNTHESIS: Adult populations accounted for 78.6% of the studies, and 93.3% used a cohort design to investigate AKI biomarkers. Mixed critically ill populations, cardiac surgery, and sepsis were identified as the most frequently studied clinical contexts in 69.5% of the studies. Systematic evidence maps were synthesized for biomarker studies to predict AKI (n = 944), prognosticate clinical outcomes (n = 647), diagnose AKI etiology (n = 109), enrich clinical trials (n = 6), and manage AKI (n = 12). Implementation strategies for patient care included surveilling patients at risk of AKI, including patients undergoing surgery and those exposed to multiple nephrotoxic drugs. CONCLUSIONS: Substantial clinical evidence assessing the accuracy of biomarkers compared with diagnosis of AKI exists, with fewer practical trials in clinical use. Still, guidance on implementation approaches can be gleaned from evaluations using biomarkers for the management of critically ill patients, particularly in surgical and nephrotoxin-exposed populations where evidence is available. This review identifies the landscape of current evidence and highlights priorities for future management and enrichment trials needed to bridge the gap between predictive accuracy and clinical decision-making.

articles.title: [Development and validation of a predictive model for high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy failure in patients with type I respiratory failure].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
articles.abstract: To explore the independent risk factors for failure of high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy (HFNC) in patients with type I respiratory failure, and to establish and validate an effective risk prediction model. A retrospective observational study was conducted, Patients with type I respiratory failure who received HFNC treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University from January 2019 to December 2024 were selected as the research subjects. Clinical data within 24 hours after admission to the ICU were collected, including demographic information and general conditions, underlying diseases, early acute organ dysfunction, vital signs, laboratory examinations, disease severity scores, and treatment measures. Patients were divided into the HFNC success group and the HFNC failure group based on whether HFNC failure (endotracheal intubation and/or death during treatment) occurred. The overall cohort was randomly divided at a ratio of 7 : 3 into a training set and a validation set. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to screen independent predictors of HFNC failure, and a nomogram prediction model was constructed accordingly. The receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve), Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to evaluate the model's discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. A total of 700 patients with type I respiratory failure were included, of whom 601 experienced HFNC success and 99 experienced HFNC failure, with a failure rate of 14.1%. Compared with the HFNC success group, patients in the HFNC failure group had lower height, proportion of coronary heart disease, serum sodium, oxygenation index, Glasgow Coma Score (GCS), and proportion of patients receiving human albumin, while exhibiting significantly higher incidence of acute kidney injury (AKI), heart rate, respiratory rate, blood urea nitrogen level, serum creatinine level, blood lactate level, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, and Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II(APACHE II) score, as well as longer prothrombin time (all P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that the presence of AKI [odds ratio (OR)=2.113, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.159-3.854, P=0.015] and elevated blood lactate level (OR=1.148, 95%CI was 1.027-1.283, P=0.015) were independent risk factors for HFNC failure, while elevated oxygenation index (OR=0.973, 95%CI was 0.963-0.983, P<0.001) and higher GCS score (OR=0.815, 95%CI was 0.760-0.874, P<0.001) were independent protective factors. Based on these four independent predictors, a nomogram prediction model was established. The ROC curves showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of the training set and validation set were 0.844 (95%CI was 0.794-0.895) and 0.794 (95%CI was 0.706-0.881), respectively. At a cutoff value of 0.160, the sensitivities were 73.9% and 60.0%, the specificities were 81.0% and 82.8%, and the accuracies were 80.0% and 79.5% in the training set and validation set, respectively. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test showed good fit for the model in both the training set (χ 2=8.636, P=0.374) and validation set (χ 2=6.652, P=0.575). The calibration curves indicated good agreement between the model predicted probabilities and the actual observations. DCA demonstrated that the model exhibited good clinical net benefit over a wide range of threshold probabilities. The nomogram model constructed based on AKI, blood lactate level, oxygenation index, and GCS score has good predictive performance for the risk of HFNC failure in patients with type I respiratory failure, providing a reference for early identification of high-risk patients and optimization of clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Association of Iron Deficiency Anemia with Outcomes in Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Analysis.
articles.abstract: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently have iron deficiency anemia (IDA), but the mechanism by which this condition affects clinical outcomes is not well understood. The purpose of this study was to assess whether IDA is associated with mortality in patients with AF. Data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) for 2021-2022 examined IDA and inpatient outcomes in a nationally representative cohort of hospitalized adults diagnosed with AF. Patients were categorized by IDA status. The factors assessed were mortality, hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, thromboembolic and cardiovascular complications, and overall hospital expenses. Hospital, clinical, and demographic factors were included in multivariable logistic and linear regression models. Of the 8.35 million AF hospitalizations, 7.1% had associated IDA. IDA was linked to multiple comorbidities along with increased risk of hypotension (OR: 1.15, 95% CI 1.12-1.17, P<0.001), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.25, 95% CI 1.23-1.27, P<0.001), and heart failure (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR]: 1.29, 95% CI 1.27-1.31, P<0.001). Ironically, IDA was linked independently to decreased risks of cardiac arrest (AOR: 0.70, 95% CI 0.66-0.73, P<0.001), transient ischemic attack (AOR: 0.58, 95% CI 0.53-0.63, P<0.001), stroke (OR: 0.49,95% CI 0.47-0.51, P<0.001), and in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.66, 95% CI 0.64-0.68, P<0.001). IDA was also associated with increased hospital expenses and increased LOS (P<0.001). IDA was linked to higher morbidity and healthcare use in those with AF admitted to the hospital, but there was a decrease in mortality and thromboembolic events. These results suggest the possibility of tailored iron therapy and imply a complex interaction between IDA and AF-related outcomes.

articles.title: Ischemic Colitis in the Setting of Tirzepatide Use: A Potentially Underrecognized Adverse Effect.
articles.abstract: Ischemic colitis is an uncommon but serious cause of acute abdominal pain that may result in bowel necrosis and may require surgical intervention. We report the case of a 63-year-old female patient with multiple comorbidities and a history of ischemic colitis, who developed sudden-onset severe cramping and abdominal pain, together with hypotension and diaphoresis, shortly after receiving her weekly tirzepatide injection. The patient reported suffering from chronic constipation with increased frequency of laxative use after beginning tirzepatide (Mounjaro). Laboratory evaluation demonstrated leukocytosis and lactic acidosis, while computed tomography (CT) findings were consistent with ischemic colitis. Her condition rapidly progressed to hypovolemic shock and acute kidney injury (AKI), requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission and segmental bowel resection with colostomy creation. Surgical pathology report confirmed patchy mucosal necrosis consistent with ischemic colitis. This case raises concern for a potential association between tirzepatide use and ischemic colitis in a patient with preexisting risk factors. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for ischemic colitis in patients receiving tirzepatide who present with severe abdominal pain, particularly in the setting of worsening constipation or a prior history of ischemic colitis. This case raises the question of whether a history of ischemic colitis and/or chronic constipation may warrant clinical caution and pharmacovigilance before starting these medications.

articles.title: Severe Rhabdomyolysis and Acute Kidney Injury Following Rosuvastatin Reinitiation During Ticagrelor Therapy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Rhabdomyolysis is a potentially life-threatening condition characterized by skeletal muscle injury, marked elevation of creatine kinase (CK), and potential development of acute kidney injury (AKI). Statins are a well-recognized cause of rhabdomyolysis, although the risk may be influenced by concomitant medications and patient-related factors. We present a case of severe rhabdomyolysis and AKI following initiation of high-intensity rosuvastatin therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention. A 66-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted with acute coronary syndrome. Coronary angiography revealed a critical lesion in the left anterior descending artery, and a drug-eluting stent was implanted. Her low-density lipoprotein cholesterol was 184 mg/dL, and her triglycerides were 356 mg/dL. She was discharged on rosuvastatin 40 mg once daily, ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily, aspirin 75 mg once daily, perindopril, and amlodipine. One month later, she developed generalized weakness, fatigue, and severe myalgia. Initial laboratory investigations demonstrated elevated serum creatinine, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase. Two days later, she developed anuria, severe muscle pain, and dark-red urine. On admission, CK and serum creatinine were markedly elevated. She denied other medication use, toxic exposure, or recent muscle trauma. Rhabdomyolysis with severe AKI was suspected, and she was admitted to the intensive care unit. Rosuvastatin was immediately discontinued, and ticagrelor was replaced with clopidogrel. Despite intravenous hydration and supportive treatment, metabolic acidosis and renal dysfunction worsened, with a serum creatinine level of 6.3 mg/dL, BUN of 82 mg/dL, and bicarbonate of 15 mmol/L. Hemodialysis was initiated. On the fourth day, she developed severe dyspnea and hypoxemia associated with pulmonary congestion, requiring additional consecutive hemodialysis sessions. Cardiac causes of pulmonary edema were excluded by electrocardiography and echocardiography. Her clinical condition subsequently stabilized, and CK and creatinine levels progressively decreased. She was discharged with continued renal monitoring, and serum creatinine decreased to 1.3 mg/dL by the third week after discharge. This case highlights the potential for severe rhabdomyolysis and AKI following high-intensity rosuvastatin therapy, particularly in patients with multiple comorbidities. Early recognition of myalgia, dark urine, oliguria, and markedly elevated CK levels is essential. Prompt discontinuation of the suspected medication, aggressive supportive management, and timely initiation of renal replacement therapy can be crucial in preventing further complications and facilitating recovery.

articles.title: What place for pragmatic RCTs in intensive care?
articles.abstract: Pragmatic trials test the effectiveness of an intervention within real-life clinical practice, prioritising applicability and generalisability. By contrast, explanatory trials evaluate the efficacy of an intervention under optimal conditions and in well-defined populations, aiming to minimise bias and confounding and to maximise the treatment effect. The majority of large-scale, multicentre academic ICU studies are overall pragmatic in nature but have repeatedly failed to demonstrate outcome differences against control populations. This relates in part to the marked heterogeneity of ICU populations, often with enrolment based on syndromic categories such as sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, shock and acute kidney injury with significant inter-individual biological variability. Any beneficial treatment effects in specific, often unidentified, subsets are diluted or cancelled out by no effect or even harm in others. A second important factor underlying the lack of intervention effect is suboptimal performance of the trials, particularly poor protocol adherence, which undermines the likelihood of showing benefit, particularly when reliant on intention-to-treat analyses. In this article we discuss these issues and provide some suggestions for improvement.
articles.ai_summary: This article discusses the limitations of pragmatic randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in intensive care units (ICUs). Pragmatic RCTs often fail to demonstrate outcome differences due to heterogeneity of ICU populations and suboptimal trial performance. Suggestions for improvement are provided.
articles.ai_significance: Understanding the limitations of pragmatic RCTs in ICUs is crucial for developing effective treatment strategies and improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: Vancomycin optimised dosing regimens for critically ill patients receiving renal replacement therapy.
authors: European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (ESCMID) Study Groups for Infections in Critically Ill Patients (ESGCIP) and the ESCMID PK/PD of Anti-Infectives Study Group (EPASG)
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal dosing of vancomycin in critically ill patients receiving renal replacement therapy (RRT) is uncertain due to high pharmacokinetic variability. We aimed to develop individualised vancomycin dosing recommendations that optimise efficacy while minimising toxicity. METHODS: Prospective, international, pharmacokinetic study enrolling critically ill patients treated with vancomycin and various RRT modalities. A population pharmacokinetic model was developed, externally validated and applied to perform Monte Carlo dosing simulations. We calculated the probability of each dosing regimen to achieve the efficacy target against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (ratio of the area under the concentration-time curve to the minimum inhibitory concentration (AUC0-24 h/MIC) ≥ 400) without exceeding the toxicity threshold (AUC0-24 h ≥ 700 mg.h/L). RESULTS: We enrolled 65 critically ill patients from 6 countries receiving continuous RRT (50.8%) or sustained low-efficiency dialysis (49.2%). The model was developed using 1318 pre- and post-filter plasma and effluent concentrations and validated with a new dataset (19 critically ill patients, 124 pre-filter plasma concentrations), with 47.4% patients concomitantly treated with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Predictive performance was high (median prediction error =-13.4%). Simulations showed that dosing requirements were dependent on actual body weight and RRT intensity and duration (p < 0.05). An optimised dosing nomogram was subsequently developed considering these clinical characteristics. CONCLUSIONS: Actual body weight and RRT intensity and duration are the main determinants of vancomycin dosing requirements in critically ill patients treated with RRT. Efficacious, non-toxic dosing may be guided by the optimised nomogram.

articles.title: Determinants of Delayed Recovery of Consciousness After Analgosedation Discontinuation in the ICU: Insights From Patients With COVID-19 Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Prolonged disorders of consciousness are common in critically ill patients receiving mechanical ventilation and are often attributed to prolonged sedative exposure in the setting of decreased drug clearance and/or reduced metabolism. Here, in a large sample of critically ill COVID patients obtained over a short period, we tested the assumption that prolonged unconsciousness following benzodiazepine and/or propofol sedation can be attributed to residual exposure. Further, we examine associations between clinical variables on time to recovery of consciousness (RoC) as a framework for the broader critically ill population. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Massachusetts General Hospital, Weill Cornell Medicine, Columbia University Irving Medical Center. PATIENTS: Seven hundred eighty-four patients with COVID-19 critical illness in Spring-Summer 2020. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We estimated the latest expected RoC (LERoC) using models of sedation exposure that account for sedative-specific pharmacokinetics and critical illness. Our primary exposure variable was a time-weighted dose of analgosedative agents at benzodiazepine and/or propofol cessation; our primary outcome was time to RoC. We estimated relative risks for late RoC (i.e., after LERoC) via multinomial logistic regression. Among individuals with late RoC, we fit a multivariate subdistribution hazard model for time to RoC. Seventy-three percent of patients had RoC before hospital discharge, yet 34% of patients achieving RoC did not do so within pharmacologically plausible sedative elimination times. Patients with late RoC were older and exhibited hypoxemia and acute kidney injury. Patients with dexmedetomidine as an adjunct sedative had a disproportionately larger incidence of early recovery. Patients with early vs. late RoC did not have significantly different discharge dispositions. CONCLUSIONS: In our cohort, the time to RoC was commonly prolonged beyond that expected from sedation exposures alone. These data may aid clinicians and families with expectations of RoC and warrant investigation of alternative determinants of delayed RoC in this population.

articles.title: Sodium bicarbonate therapy in severe metabolic acidemia: an individual patient data meta-analysis of the BICAR-ICU and BICAR-ICU2 trials.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Two randomized trials (BICAR-ICU and BICAR-ICU2) evaluated intravenous sodium bicarbonate therapy in patients with severe metabolic acidemia but yielded inconclusive results. We performed an individual patient data meta-analysis to assess its effects on 90-day mortality and renal replacement therapy (RRT) use, and search for heterogeneity of treatment effects across prespecified subgroups. METHODS: We performed an individual patient data meta-analysis of the BICAR-ICU and BICAR-ICU2 trials, including adults with severe metabolic acidemia (pH ≤ 7.20). Patients were randomized to receive intravenous sodium bicarbonate titrated to a pH ≥ 7.30 or no sodium bicarbonate. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included RRT initiation and dialysis-free days. Prespecified subgroup analyses explored treatment-effect heterogeneity by acidemia depth (pH ≤ 7.10 vs. > 7.10), severe acute kidney injury (AKI) status, and serum lactate (< 2mmol/L vs. ≥2mmol/L). RESULTS: A total of 1,016 patients was included (509 sodium bicarbonate, 507 control). Sodium bicarbonate therapy did not significantly reduce 90-day mortality compared to control (58.3% vs. 60.6%; risk ratio [RR], 0.96; 95%CI, 0.86-1.07; p = 0.51). However, it significantly reduced RRT initiation (34.8% vs. 50.7%; RR, 0.69; 95%CI, 0.60-0.79; p < 0.001, number needed to treat: 6.3) and increased dialysis-free days (incidence rate ratio, 1.10; 95%CI, 1.06-1.14; p < 0.001). A significant interaction was observed with acidemia depth (p-for-interaction = 0.006): in patients with pH ≤ 7.10, sodium bicarbonate reduced 90-day mortality (RR, 0.80; 95%CI, 0.68-0.93; p = 0.004); no benefit was seen with pH > 7.10 (RR, 1.05; 95%CI, 0.92-1.21; p = 0.47). No significant interactions were observed for severe AKI status (p-for-interaction = 0.11) nor serum lactate (p-for-interaction = 0.22). CONCLUSIONS: Sodium bicarbonate therapy did not reduce overall 90-day mortality but decreased RRT use and suggested a mortality benefit in patients with the most profound acidemia (pH ≤ 7.10). These findings invite a reconsideration of current paradigms, suggesting timely correction of severe metabolic acidemia to avoid RRT in some patients.
articles.ai_summary: This study combined data from two previous trials to assess the effect of sodium bicarbonate therapy on patients with severe metabolic acidemia. It found that while sodium bicarbonate did not reduce overall mortality, it did decrease the need for renal replacement therapy and may benefit patients with the most severe acidemia.
articles.ai_significance: These findings suggest that timely correction of severe metabolic acidemia may help avoid the need for renal replacement therapy in some patients, and may change current clinical practice paradigms.

articles.title: Nutrition Therapy in Critically Ill Adults.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract: In the acute phase of critical illness, adults have severe catabolism, inflammation, muscle loss, and gut dysfunction, all of which shape nutritional requirements. Early enteral nutrition supports gut integrity and microbiome health, but trials have shown that early short-term parenteral nutrition is a safe alternative when enteral feeding is not possible. Large trials have shown that early full-dose energy delivery offers no benefit over restrictive dosing and may increase gastrointestinal and metabolic complications, findings that support a restrictive nutrition strategy, especially in patients who have circulatory shock or are at risk for refeeding syndrome. Similarly, large trials have shown no advantage of high-dose over standard-dose protein and suggest harm in patients with acute kidney injury. Because adverse events are common with enteral nutrition, safe nutrition delivery requires gradual advancement, strategies for prevention of refeeding syndrome, glycemic control, and avoidance of routine gastric residual volume monitoring. Patient heterogeneity underscores the need for precise, biomarker-guided, phase-specific nutrition to preserve lean muscle mass and improve recovery.

articles.title: Genomic dynamics of antimicrobial resistance transmission between bacteria from intensive care unit surfaces and from critically ill patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Intensive Care Unit (ICU) is an environment where multiple factors that predispose to the transmission of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) coexist. Genomic sequencing is a technology that enables a better understanding of how AMR genes are transmitted within the ICU environment. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the genomic dynamics of the transmission of antimicrobial resistance genes between bacteria from ICU surfaces and bacteria from critically ill patients. METHODS: A cross-sectional analytical study. Surface swab samples were collected from the ICU, including suction units, infusion pumps, stethoscopes, dialysis machines, monitors, ventilators and gas valves, as well as samples from critically ill patients with infections. Species were identified using microbiological microplate panels; antibiotic susceptibility testing was carried out to assess AMR; and whole-genome sequencing was performed on isolates that were multidrug-resistant (MDR). The sequencing was carried out using a nanopore long-read sequencer and the results were analysed using specialised bioinformatics tools. RESULTS: A total of 130 positive isolates were identified, of which 96 (73.85%) were from environmental samples and 34 (26.15%) from patient samples. Forty (30.76%) MDR species were identified. The most common MDR species were Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii. The most frequently detected AMR genes were blaNDM-5 and blaOXA-23. The most common plasmids were IncFIB(K)_1_Kpn3, Col440I and IncL/M(pMU407)_1_pMU407. A clonal outbreak of Acinetobacter baumannii ST 2 was detected on the dialysis machine, stethoscopes and patient samples. Evidence of horizontal transfer of resistance genes via plasmids conjugation was found in samples taken from suction units, oxygen valves and tracheal secretion in three cases. CONCLUSION: The findings of this research show that antimicrobial resistance genes are transferred between bacteria on surfaces and bacteria in critically ill patients, and that this transfer occurs in both directions.

articles.title: Interpreting protein dose trials in critical illness: a guide for the bedside clinician.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Critical illness induces a catabolic state, associated with profound muscle wasting and functional disability in survivors. Based on evidence at the time of development, international critical care nutrition guidelines recommend providing higher protein doses than in healthy populations. MAIN BODY: Three recent international multi-centre randomised trials (total n = 5633 patients) have compared higher protein doses to usual protein doses in critically ill patients. Based on the primary outcomes, these trials concluded that higher protein doses did not improve time-to-discharge alive or number of days free of the index hospital and alive at day 90, with worse functional recovery using the EQ-5D-5L health utility score over 180 days. Supported by evidence from recent trials, it appears preferable to commence protein delivery at low doses once patients are haemodynamically stable and increase progressively over the first 5 days to deliver a maximum of 1.2 g/kg/day. Based on current trial data, this upper limit may represent a safer alternative to doses >1.2 g/kg/day, acknowledging that the optimal dose may be lower. Subgroup analyses suggest that patients with an acute kidney injury may be particularly vulnerable to higher protein. There are no data to indicate the minimum protein dose that can be safely delivered to critically ill patients over their entire ICU stay. While existing trials included patients with a prolonged ICU stay, no trial identifying this cohort pre-randomisation has been conducted. It cannot be excluded that higher protein doses may provide benefit later in recovery, when the anabolic resistance to dietary protein observed early in the ICU admission has subsided. Evidence is also lacking on optimal protein targets for patients after ICU discharge. CONCLUSION: In critically ill adults, we suggest that protein doses be commenced at a low dose and increased progressively to a maximum of 1.2 g/kg/day based on recent randomised trials.
articles.ai_summary: Three large international trials compared high protein doses to usual doses in critically ill patients. The results showed no benefit to high protein doses, and instead suggest starting with low doses and increasing over time. This may be especially important for patients with acute kidney injury.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings have significant implications for ICU nutrition practice, suggesting a shift away from high protein doses and towards a more gradual and individualized approach to protein delivery.

articles.title: Implementation of the kidney protection strategy in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury - a multi-center prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The international Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines recommend the implementation of a kidney protection strategy (KPS) in patients at high risk of and with Acute Kidney Injury (AKI). However, real-world implementation of this strategy in critically ill patients with AKI is unclear. We quantified timely and sustained adherence to KPS in critically ill adults with moderate-to-severe (KDIGO stage 2 or 3) AKI and explored associations with clinical outcomes. METHODS: This was a multicenter, prospective cohort study enrolling adult patients with moderate or severe AKI requiring vasopressors and/or mechanical ventilation across five centers in Europe. The primary endpoint was adherence to the KPS, which included hemodynamic monitoring, sustained optimization of mean arterial pressure (MAP) > 65 mmHg, monitoring of serum creatinine and urine output, and avoidance of hyperglycemia, radiocontrast agents and nephrotoxins when possible, within 12 h after AKI diagnosis for 48 h or until ICU discharge. Exploratory analyses examined associations between adherence and renal outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 258 patients were enrolled (median age 69 years [IQR 62-75]; 65% male; median SOFA 10 [IQR 8-13]). The complete KPS was implemented in 80 patients (31%; 95% CI, 25.5-37.2%). Adherence to individual components of the KPS varied widely with optimization of MAP showing the lowest implementation rate (33%). In exploratory analyses accounting for death as a competing risk, KPS adherence was associated with a lower incidence of AKD beyond day 7 (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.64; 95% CI, 0.41-0.99; p = 0.046), a higher incidence of renal recovery at hospital discharge (SHR 6.02; 95% CI, 4.00-9.05; p < 0.0001), and a lower incidence of RRT within 30 days (SHR 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.91; p = 0.04). After multivariable adjustment, the association with renal recovery remained robust (adjusted SHR 6.29; 95% CI, 3.08-12.85; p < 0.0001). A clear dose-response relationship was observed between the number of implemented KPS components and renal outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: In critically ill patients with moderate-to-severe AKI, the complete KDIGO-recommended kidney protection strategy was implemented in approximately one-third of patients, and full KPS adherence was associated with a higher rate of renal recovery at hospital discharge.
articles.ai_summary: This study looked at how well a kidney protection strategy was implemented in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. They found that about a third of patients received the full strategy, and those who did had a higher rate of kidney recovery. The study also found a link between the number of strategy components implemented and better kidney outcomes.
articles.ai_significance: This study is important for ICU clinicians because it highlights the need to implement a kidney protection strategy in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury to improve kidney recovery rates.

articles.title: The role of hemoadsorption in septic shock: toward a personalized approach.
articles.abstract: A dysregulated host response to infection is central to the pathophysiology of sepsis and may culminate in life-threatening organ dysfunction. Given that this process is largely characterized by concurrent pro- and anti-inflammatory activation, immunomodulatory strategies have long been explored in sepsis research. Among these, extracorporeal removal of circulating cytokines, inflammatory mediators and other soluble factors through non-specific hemoadsorption with macroporous styrene-divinylbenzene sorbents has been proposed as a potential therapeutic approach. Its adoption into clinical practice has largely been based on pathophysiological considerations rather than on evidence from large, well-designed randomized clinical trials. Over the past 15 years, most of the available evidence has been predominantly derived from small, single-center cohorts, reports from registries and heterogeneous prospective studies with substantial variability in patients' selection, timing, and treatment intensity. In addition, the precise mechanisms of action of hemoadsorption remain incompletely understood. Although several meta-analyses have attempted to synthesize the existing data, the overall quality and heterogeneity of the included studies limit the strength and reliability of their conclusions. As a result, current guideline recommendations are largely based on expert opinions rather than high-certainty evidence. This position statement aimed to provide a concise overview of the biological rationale, current evidence, and contemporary clinical practice related to hemoadsorption in critically ill patients.
articles.ai_summary: Researchers reviewed the evidence on hemoadsorption in septic shock, finding that current guidelines are based on expert opinions rather than high-certainty evidence. Hemoadsorption involves removing inflammatory mediators from the blood, but its effectiveness and mechanisms of action are not well understood. More research is needed to determine its role in treating septic shock.
articles.ai_significance: This study highlights the need for more robust clinical trials to establish the effectiveness of hemoadsorption in septic shock, which could lead to more personalized and effective treatment approaches in the ICU.

articles.title: Sodium Bicarbonate for Critically Ill Adults with Metabolic Acidosis and Shock.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
authors: SODa-BIC Investigators and the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Clinical Trials Group
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic acidosis is common in critically ill patients and is associated with organ dysfunction and death. Sodium bicarbonate is used to correct acidemia, but its benefit in patients with metabolic acidosis who are receiving vasopressors remains uncertain. METHODS: In this pragmatic, adaptive, double-blind, randomized trial, we assigned adults with metabolic acidosis (pH, <7.30; base excess, no more than -4 mmol per liter; and partial pressure of arterial carbon dioxide, ≤45 mm Hg without intubation or ≤50 mm Hg with intubation) who were receiving vasopressors in the intensive care unit (ICU) to receive either sodium bicarbonate or placebo (5% dextrose). Sodium bicarbonate or placebo was infused for up to 5 hours, with the infusion rate adjusted for a target pH of at least 7.30 and base excess of at least 0 mmol per liter. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event, defined as death, use of renal-replacement therapy, or persistent renal dysfunction, within 30 days. RESULTS: A total of 500 patients were enrolled in 55 ICUs across seven countries; 245 patients were assigned to receive sodium bicarbonate and 255 to receive placebo. A major adverse kidney event within 30 days occurred in 98 of 244 patients (40.2%) in the sodium bicarbonate group and in 100 of 254 patients (39.4%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, 1.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -7.1 to 9.4; P = 0.78). Renal-replacement therapy was used within 30 days in 16.8% of the patients in the sodium bicarbonate group and in 20.9% of those in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -3.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.6 to 2.7). In-hospital mortality by day 30 was 25.4% in the sodium bicarbonate group and 24.0% in the placebo group (adjusted difference, 1.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.6 to 9.2). Four patients (1.6%) in the sodium bicarbonate group had an adverse effect, as compared with none in the placebo group (P = 0.06). CONCLUSIONS: The use of sodium bicarbonate in critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis receiving vasopressors did not lead to a lower risk of major adverse kidney events within 30 days than placebo. (Funded by the National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia; SODa-BIC ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05697770.).
articles.ai_summary: Researchers conducted a randomized trial of 500 critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis and shock to see if sodium bicarbonate reduced kidney damage. The results showed no difference in kidney damage or mortality between patients who received sodium bicarbonate and those who received a placebo. The study found that sodium bicarbonate did not provide a benefit in reducing kidney damage or improving outcomes in critically ill patients.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings are significant for ICU clinical practice as they suggest that sodium bicarbonate may not be beneficial in reducing kidney damage or improving outcomes in critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis and shock. Clinicians may need to reconsider using sodium bicarbonate in these patients.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of prediction models for ICU-level intervention and 14-day mortality at Medical Emergency Team activation: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Medical Emergency Team (MET) activation represents acute clinical deterioration requiring rapid decisions regarding escalation of care. Previous post-MET prediction studies have evaluated outcomes including unplanned intensive care unit (ICU) admission and mortality; however, ICU admission is a location-based outcome that may be influenced by institutional factors. Prediction based on treatment intensity rather than location of care has received less attention. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of adult patients undergoing MET activation on general wards at a tertiary-care hospital in Japan between May 2021 and December 2025. Two outcomes were evaluated: initiation of ICU-level interventions within 24 hours and all-cause 14-day mortality. ICU-level interventions were defined as the initiation of mechanical ventilation, vasopressor or inotropic infusion, renal replacement therapy, or polymyxin B hemoperfusion (PMX). Multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were developed using variables available at the time of MET activation. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination (C-index), calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap-based internal validation. Among 533 patients, 303 (56.8%) required ICU-level interventions and 147 (27.6%) died within 14 days. Lower albumin levels and higher blood urea nitrogen, potassium, and white blood cell count were associated with both outcomes, whereas higher heart rate was associated with 14-day mortality. The model demonstrated moderate discrimination for ICU-level intervention (C-index 0.721, 95% CI 0.660-0.745) and good discrimination for 14-day mortality (C-index 0.784, 95% CI 0.720-0.814). Calibration analyses indicated modest overfitting but generally good agreement between predicted and observed risks. Decision curve analysis demonstrated clinical net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. In this single-center cohort, treatment escalation and short-term mortality represented related but distinct dimensions of clinical risk. Defining intensive care need based on treatment intensity rather than ICU admission may provide an operational framework for risk stratification at MET activation. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting early acute kidney injury and altered consciousness in cardiac surgery patients admitted to the intensive care unit: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and altered consciousness are common and serious complications following cardiac surgery, both associated with increased morbidity and mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU). Early prediction of these complications is essential for timely intervention. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting early AKI and altered consciousness risk in this population. We retrospectively extracted data from the MIMIC-IV database. Adult patients who underwent cardiac surgery within 24 h before ICU admission were included. The primary outcome was early AKI defined by KDIGO criteria within 48 h after ICU admission. The secondary outcome was altered consciousness within 24 h after ICU admission, defined as a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score ≤12. A comprehensive set of candidate variables was screened using four feature selection methods (LassoCV, mRMR, mutual information, and F-test) with a voting strategy. Eight machine learning models were developed and compared. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were used to interpret the best-performing model. External validation was performed using data from cardiac surgery patients at Wuxi No.2 People's Hospital between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2025. A total of 5,288 patients were included, with an AKI incidence of 76.2% (4,031/5,288) and an altered consciousness incidence of 22.8% (1,206/5,288). For the primary outcome of AKI, the XGBoost model achieved a training AUC of 0.787 (95% CI: 0.770-0.804) and an internal test AUC of 0.659 (95% CI: 0.629-0.688). For the secondary outcome of altered consciousness, the XGBoost model achieved an internal test AUC of 0.951 (95% CI: 0.936-0.963). Calibration curve and decision curve analysis confirmed good calibration and clinical utility for both models. SHAP analysis identified SpO2, age, APSIII score, creatinine, and white blood cell count as the top 5 most important predictors for AKI. External validation was performed in an independent cohort of 395 cardiac surgery ICU patients from Wuxi No.2 People's Hospital, in whom the incidence of AKI and altered consciousness was 28.1% and 67.3%, respectively. The models retained acceptable discrimination in this external cohort (AKI: AUC 0.764, 95% CI: 0.711-0.818; altered consciousness: AUC 0.679, 95% CI: 0.615-0.737). We developed interpretable XGBoost-based prediction models for both early AKI and altered consciousness risk in cardiac surgery patients admitted to the ICU. The models exhibited excellent discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, which may facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and guide personalized interventions.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury in critically ill older adults: clinical severity and nursing workload.
articles.abstract: To determine the incidence and association of acute kidney injury, clinical severity, and nursing workload with prognostic outcomes in older patients admitted to an Intensive Care Unit. A retrospective cohort study conducted between January and December 2023 in an Intensive Care Unit. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire applied to medical records. Two-sided p-values <0.05 were considered statistically significant. Among the 81 older patients analyzed, 32% developed acute kidney injury. Of these, 22.2% had moderate to severe impairment of renal function. The use of norepinephrine (p=0.019) and the need for mechanical ventilation (p<0.001) were significantly associated with the occurrence of acute kidney injury. In addition, nursing workload was significantly higher in the group with renal impairment (p=0.006). A relevant incidence of acute kidney injury of moderate to high severity was observed among older patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit. Patients with acute kidney injury had a higher nursing workload, as evidenced by higher Nursing Activities Score values. In addition, acute kidney injury was associated with unfavorable prognostic outcomes, including prolonged length of stay and a greater need for advanced support.

articles.title: Effects of higher versus lower protein intake in critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: The optimal protein dose for critically ill patients remains uncertain, and emerging evidence suggests that the effects of higher protein intake may differ across clinically relevant subgroups. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating protein delivery in critical illness adults (up to July 2026). Higher and lower protein groups were defined according to each trial's original allocation. Primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included mechanical ventilation (MV) duration, Intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS), muscle outcomes, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), biochemical outcomes, and adverse events. Results were reported as risk ratios (RRs) or mean difference (MD) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Trial Sequential Analysis (TSA) was performed to control for random error, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE framework. Thirty three RCTs involving 11,622 participants were included. No significant differences were observed between higher and lower protein groups for all-cause mortality (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.08), MV duration (MD -0.48, 95% CI -1.08 to 0.13), or ICU LOS (MD -0.18, 95% CI -0.86 to 0.51), with TSA confirming these null findings. Some muscle metrics favored the higher protein group; however, there was a trend towards poorer HRQoL (SMD -0.12, 95% CI -0.24 to 0.00). The higher protein group showed improved nitrogen balance (MD 5.58, 95% CI 2.89 to 8.27) and higher serum albumin levels (SMD 0.18, 95% CI 0.07 to 0.29), but increased urea (MD 2.06, 95% CI 1.49 to 2.64) and blood urea nitrogen concentrations (MD 2.94, 95% CI 1.32 to 4.56). Sensitivity analyses restricted to 27 isocaloric-design trials yielded consistent results. Subgroup analyses revealed that higher protein intake was linked to increased mortality in patients with acute kidney injury (RR 1.46, 95% CI 1.14 to 1.87); however, higher protein intake combined with rehabilitation interventions was associated with reduced mortality (RR 0.68, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.93), shorter MV duration (MD -1.45, 95% CI -2.61 to -0.29), and beneficial muscle effects. Higher protein intake was not associated with better clinical outcomes. While it may increase mortality in patients with AKI, combining it with physical rehabilitation yields survival and clinical benefits, warranting confirmation in future factorial RCTs. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251109618, identifier [CRD420251109618].

articles.title: Development and multi-database validation of machine learning models for 28-day mortality prediction in ICU patients with COPD and pulmonary hypertension.
articles.abstract: Early mortality prediction in critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) coexisting pulmonary hypertension (PH) remains challenging, particularly because prediction models developed in intensive care unit (ICU) database may not perform consistently across other healthcare systems. This retrospective multicenter study employed two large-scale databases to establish and validate ML models for predicting early mortality in ICU patients with COPD and PH. The MIMIC-IV database served as the model-development cohort (2555 patients), with external validation conducted on eICU CRD (292 patients) database. Six ML algorithms were adopted: Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Logistic Regression (LR), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN).The baseline variables were screened to identify potential predictors via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (Lasso) regression. Model interpretability was evaluated via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. The overall cohort consisted of 2,847 ICU patients with COPD and PH. Twelve consistently crucial clinical features were identified, including acute kidney injury, pneumonia, age, weight, heart rate, red blood cell distribution width (RDW), white blood cell (WBC), anion gap, chloride, creatinine, base excess, potential of hydrogen (pH). The Random Forest algorithm achieved the optimal performance, with a training Area Under Curve (AUC) of 0.938, internal validation AUC of 0.748, and eICU CRD external validation AUC of 0.800. SHAP analysis indicated that acute kidney injury was the most influential predictor, followed by base excess and RDW. Additionally, a web tool was developed in this study to facilitate the application of early death risk prediction in clinical practice. This study is the multi-database validation of ML models for early mortality prediction in ICU patients with COPD and PH. The Random Forest model integrated with SHAP interpretability offers a reliable tool for clinical decision-making support, with consistent validity verified across two databases, including our internal validation cohort. This work provides a decision support tool to assist in identifying high-risk individuals within this complex comorbid population, and establishes a foundation for future studies with a more dynamic and personalized prognostic approach.

articles.title: Association of red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.
articles.abstract: Critically ill patients with aortic dissection remain at high risk of adverse ICU outcomes, including ICU mortality. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection. Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. ICU mortality was defined as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and renal replacement therapy (RRT) use. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the discriminative performance of RAR for ICU mortality. The optimal RAR cutoff was determined using Youden's index and was considered exploratory. Calibration plots and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. RAR showed modest discrimination for ICU mortality (AUC: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.552-0.765). The exploratory cutoff value of RAR was 5.182. Compared with the low-RAR group, the high-RAR group had higher ICU mortality (21.8% vs. 6.7%; P < 0.001), a higher prevalence of sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay (82.8% vs. 61.1%; P < 0.001), and more frequent RRT use (33.3% vs. 9.4%; P < 0.001). The AUC increased from 0.706 for SOFA alone to 0.731 for SOFA plus RAR, indicating only limited incremental discrimination. Higher early-ICU RAR was associated with ICU mortality and other adverse ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection, but its discrimination was modest, its incremental value beyond SOFA was limited, and external validation is required.

articles.title: Editorial: Extracorporeal organ support: innovations and challenges in critical care.
Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI. In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort (n = 409) and a validation cohort (n = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS). The standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832-0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = -0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs (AUC = 0.652), and OASIS (AUC = 0.647). The logistic regression-based nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.838, providing a user-friendly bedside tool for clinicians. The machine learning-based XGBoost model, incorporating ten readily available clinical variables, demonstrated excellent predictive performance for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with VTE and AKI. This model offers a practical and interpretable tool for early risk stratification and may guide proactive nutritional and therapeutic interventions in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Nursing Activities Score in critically ill patients on invasive mechanical ventilation.
articles.abstract: to assess the association between invasive mechanical ventilation duration, classified as prolonged and non-prolonged, and nursing workload in critically ill patients. a prospective cohort study with adult patients on mechanical ventilation for up to 21 days or more. Nursing workload was measured using the Nursing Activities Score (NAS). Clinical data were collected using a structured questionnaire. A significance level of 5% was adopted. considering 61 patients, there was no significant difference in nursing workload between prolonged and non-prolonged mechanical ventilation according to NAS [111.2 (105.118) vs. 111.8 (107.119); p=0.880], nor was there an association between mechanical ventilation time and this score (AUC=0.512). Prolonged mechanical ventilation was associated with vasoactive drugs (96%; p=0.007) and greater severity of acute kidney injury (KDIGO=3.78%; p=0.009). mechanical ventilation duration was not associated with changes in nursing workload, which remained high regardless of the ventilatory support duration.

articles.title: OmniTFT: an EHR-driven multi-target forecasting model for ICU clinical decision support systems.
articles.abstract: Accurate multivariate time-series forecasting of vital signs and laboratory results is crucial for electronic health record (EHR)-driven clinical decision support systems in intensive care units (ICUs). However, vital signs are susceptible to noise and exhibit rapid fluctuations, while laboratory results are characterized by missing values and measurement lags, making it challenging to forecast heterogeneous ICU variables within a common framework. We introduce OmniTFT, a Temporal Fusion Transformer-based multi-target forecasting model for ICU EHR time series. OmniTFT combines state-balanced sliding-window sampling with three training regularizers: frequency-aware embedding shrinkage, historical group-entropy regularization, and shock-alignment regularization. A shared backbone with target-specific heads enables multiple forecasting tasks within a common training and inference framework while preserving target-specific temporal resolutions and forecast horizons. OmniTFT was trained on MIMIC-IV (n = 13,277) and independently validated on two cohorts: the MIMIC-III CareVue cohort (n = 4,188) and the eICU cohort (n = 23,238). Component ablation and sampling sensitivity analyses were conducted using a fixed patient partition and ten different training seeds. On the MIMIC-IV test set, OmniTFT achieved the lowest MAE for five of eight targets, ranked second for creatinine and respiratory rate, and ranked third for temperature. In a retrospective analysis in eICU, adding the OmniTFT forecast of the subsequent unobserved 24 h to the complete observed record improved discrimination for incident moderate-to-severe acute kidney injury compared with the observed record alone (AUROC 0.763, 95% CI: 0.674-0.852 vs. 0.693, 0.598-0.787, ΔAUROC + 0.070, DeLong p = 0.009), and identified 73.3% vs. 57.8% of subsequent events when 30% of patients were flagged for review. OmniTFT provides a shared-backbone framework for forecasting heterogeneous ICU variables while preserving target-specific temporal configurations. Retrospective results in disease-enriched cohorts support broader external validation and suggest its potential as an EHR-integrated forecasting component for clinical decision support.

articles.title: Incidence and Outcomes of Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Patients: A Retrospective Study at a Tertiary Care Hospital.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury is common among critically ill patients and is associated with longer ICU stay, higher resource use and increased mortality. Evidence from low- and middle-income countries, including Nepal, remains limited. This study describes the incidence, severity distribution and clinical outcomes of AKI in a tertiary care ICU. We conducted a hospital based retrospective observational study at Dhulikhel Hospital, Nepal. All adults admitted to the ICU from 1 st may 2023 to 30 th April 2024 were screened using ICU registry. AKI was defined and staged using KDIGO serum criteria. Demographic data, comorbidities, ICU interventions and outcomes were extracted. Associations were examined using appropriate statistical tests. Among 1113 patients, 1064 were enrolled for analysis. The incidence of AKI was 29.6%. Patients with AKI were older (median age 60 vs 55 years, p < 0.001), had longer ICU stays (median 3 vs 2 days, p < 0.001), were more frequently on invasive mechanical ventilation (39.6%vs 26%, p < 0.001). Type 2 diabetes mellitus was significantly associated with AKI (39.0% vs 28.0%, p = 0.001). AKI severity correlated with worse outcomes including higher mortality and adverse outcomes increasing from 12.7% in patients without AKI to 38% in stage 3 AKI. Renal replacement therapy was required in 2.3% of patients, mainly in stage 2 and 3 AKI. Acute kidney injury is a common and a serious complication among critically ill patients, associated with increased mortality and prolonged ICU stay. Early recognition and targeted management strategies, particularly for high-risk groups, are needed in resource limited settings.

articles.title: Hematological indices as predictors of in-hospital adverse outcomes in patients with COVID-19.
articles.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
articles.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic required medical teams to make rational decisions with limited resources, especially in Brazil. Various diagnostic tools, clinical guidelines, and existing indices were adopted to predict the risk of death and other adverse outcomes. The objective of this study was to validate three hematological indices [neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and lymphocyte-monocyte ratio (LMR)] for predicting adverse hospital outcomes in patients with COVID-19 in an observational cohort at a hospital in northeastern Brazil between April 2020 and October 2021. Hematological indices were calculated based on admission blood counts and correlated with hospital outcomes: in-hospital death, invasive mechanical ventilation, and renal replacement therapy. The analysis determined the frequencies of outcomes, established index thresholds, and assessed their association and accuracy and factors associated with hospital survival. Intra-hospital outcomes reflected disease severity; 34.62% of patients required admission to the ICU, 26.21% invasive mechanical ventilation, 4.2% renal replacement therapy, and 21.04% died. Advanced age, ICU requirement, and higher NLR were associated with higher risk of death. Multivariate analysis identified NLR as the only index associated with worse prognosis, with a cutoff point of 5.24 at hospital admission, showing a sensitivity of 84.0% and accuracy of 86.9%. The negative predictive value of 95.52% was highly significant, assisting hospital management by focusing efforts on higher-risk patients. These findings highlight the predictive value of the NLR, PLR, and LMR indices as valuable markers for risk stratification in patients hospitalized with COVID-19, offering a broader view of prognosis and guiding more personalized management and care strategies.

articles.title: Independent correlates of vancomycin steady-state trough concentration among patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery: observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump support.
articles.abstract: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) combined with valve surgery represent a high-risk surgical population with substantial perioperative hemodynamic disturbances and highly variable organ function, leading to high variability in vancomycin pharmacokinetics. Conventional vancomycin dosing solely on renal function frequently fails to achieve target trough concentrations in this complex subgroup. This study aimed to identify independent correlates c of vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations (Css-min), and to report observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, to inform individualized therapeutic drug monitoring. A single-center retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery from January 2018 to October 2024. Clinical data and vancomycin TDM records were extracted from electronic medical records. Vancomycin Css-min was detected by enzyme-multiplied immunoassay technique. Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) accounting for within-patient repeated TDM measurements were used to identify clinical correlates of Css-min. IABP support was pre-specified and force-entered into the multivariable model based on clinical observations and pathophysiological reasoning, independent of univariate screening results. We performed a sensitivity analysis for patients with at least one TDM within postoperative day 7, prespecified interaction tests for effect modification, and binary logistic-GEE for the supratherapeutic endpoint (Css-min > 20 mg/L). A two-tailed P < 0.05 was set as statistical significance. A total of 283 eligible patients with 473 valid Css-min measurements were included. Multivariate GEE demonstrated that categorical vancomycin dosing regimen, age, ventilator dependence ≥96 h, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), IABP support, serum creatinine (Scr), and serum urea nitrogen (SUN) were positively associated with higher geometric-mean Css-min. Associations remained largely consistent in the sensitivity-analysis subgroup of patients with at least one early-phase TDM within postoperative day 7. A significant CRRT-by-postoperative-time interaction was detected, indicating that the influence of CRRT on vancomycin exposure varied across different postoperative phases. Of note, the association signal linking IABP to supratherapeutic trough concentrations (Css-min>20 mg/L) was modest and requires cautious interpretation.
