Serum I-FABP and MMP-9 concentrations were measured using commercial enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kits at baseline and on day 7. Longitudinal changes in serum I-FABP and MMP-9 concentrations between baseline and day 7, and their correlations with neurological severity (NIHSS). 73 patients (40 EN, 33 PN). Median age was 73 years (interquartile range, 64-80) and 37 (51%) were female. At baseline, I-FABP and MMP-9 levels were comparable between groups (all P>.05). Over the 7-day observation period, I-FABP trajectories diverged between groups (EN: 7.22 (2.68) to 6.69 (2.78) ng/mL; PN: 6.74 (3.09) to 7.82 (2.97) ng/mL), as did MMP-9 trajectories (EN: 11.5 (1.45) to 10.9 (2.31) ng/mL; PN: 11.3 (2.41) to 11.8 (1.87) ng/mL). At day 7, both biomarkers correlated significantly with NIHSS score (ρ=0.385 and ρ=0.440, respectively; both P<.001). Repeated measures analysis of covariance, adjusted for baseline NIHSS score, confirmed significant time × nutritional route interactions for both biomarkers (I-FABP: F[1,70]=4.22, P=0.044, P_FDR=.044, η2p=.057; MMP-9: F[1,70]= 4.76, P=.033, P_FDR=.044, η2p=0.064). In critically ill AIS patients, EN was associated with more favourable 7-day trajectories of gut barrier integrity and neuroinflammatory activity compared with PN, after adjustment for baseline stroke severity. Single-center design, biomarker sampling restricted to two time points, reliance on delivered rather than utilised nutritional measures, and non-randomised nutritional route assignment with residual potential for confounding by indication.

articles.title: State-of-the-art review: ß-blockade in critical illness.
articles.abstract: Critical illness is characterised by activation of the sympathetic nervous system which plays an important adaptive role in maintaining cardiovascular stability and organ perfusion. However, excessive sustained adrenergic stimulation may become maladaptive, contributing to tachyarrhythmias, myocardial injury, immune dysregulation, metabolic derangements, and organ dysfunction. This state-of-the-art review evaluates the role of ß-blocker therapy as a potential strategy to modulate or counteract the adrenergic response in critically ill patients. Current data suggest that their use remains highly context-dependent and controversial. There are established benefits in selected scenarios, including acute myocardial infarction, tachyarrhythmias, hypertensive emergencies, thyroid storm, and prevention of variceal bleeds. In contrast, evidence is limited or conflicting in septic shock, traumatic brain injury, acute heart failure, burns and other critical care syndromes. Concerns include impairment of compensatory cardiovascular responses, reduction of cardiac output, hypotension, and compromised organ perfusion. Furthermore, the safety and efficacy of ß-blockade appear to depend on the type and dose of ß-blocker, patient phenotype, timing of initiation, hemodynamic reserve, and whether therapy represents continuation of chronic treatment, withdrawal and re-initiation, or de novo initiation during acute illness. This review highlights major gaps in knowledge, including the absence of reliable indicators to identify patients most likely to benefit, uncertainty regarding optimal treatment targets and monitoring strategies, and limited randomised evidence in heterogeneous ICU populations. A phenotype-driven, physiology-guided approach that accounts for hemodynamic status, sympathetic spectrum and timing of ß-blocker therapy is likely required to optimise outcomes.

articles.title: Sodium Bicarbonate for Critically Ill Adults with Metabolic Acidosis and Shock.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
authors: SODa-BIC Investigators and the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Clinical Trials Group
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic acidosis is common in critically ill patients and is associated with organ dysfunction and death. Sodium bicarbonate is used to correct acidemia, but its benefit in patients with metabolic acidosis who are receiving vasopressors remains uncertain. METHODS: In this pragmatic, adaptive, double-blind, randomized trial, we assigned adults with metabolic acidosis (pH, <7.30; base excess, no more than -4 mmol per liter; and partial pressure of arterial carbon dioxide, ≤45 mm Hg without intubation or ≤50 mm Hg with intubation) who were receiving vasopressors in the intensive care unit (ICU) to receive either sodium bicarbonate or placebo (5% dextrose). Sodium bicarbonate or placebo was infused for up to 5 hours, with the infusion rate adjusted for a target pH of at least 7.30 and base excess of at least 0 mmol per liter. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event, defined as death, use of renal-replacement therapy, or persistent renal dysfunction, within 30 days. RESULTS: A total of 500 patients were enrolled in 55 ICUs across seven countries; 245 patients were assigned to receive sodium bicarbonate and 255 to receive placebo. A major adverse kidney event within 30 days occurred in 98 of 244 patients (40.2%) in the sodium bicarbonate group and in 100 of 254 patients (39.4%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, 1.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -7.1 to 9.4; P = 0.78). Renal-replacement therapy was used within 30 days in 16.8% of the patients in the sodium bicarbonate group and in 20.9% of those in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -3.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.6 to 2.7). In-hospital mortality by day 30 was 25.4% in the sodium bicarbonate group and 24.0% in the placebo group (adjusted difference, 1.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.6 to 9.2). Four patients (1.6%) in the sodium bicarbonate group had an adverse effect, as compared with none in the placebo group (P = 0.06). CONCLUSIONS: The use of sodium bicarbonate in critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis receiving vasopressors did not lead to a lower risk of major adverse kidney events within 30 days than placebo. (Funded by the National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia; SODa-BIC ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05697770.).
articles.ai_summary: Researchers conducted a randomized trial of 500 critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis and shock to see if sodium bicarbonate reduced kidney damage. The results showed no difference in kidney damage or mortality between patients who received sodium bicarbonate and those who received a placebo. The study found that sodium bicarbonate did not provide a benefit in reducing kidney damage or improving outcomes in critically ill patients.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings are significant for ICU clinical practice as they suggest that sodium bicarbonate may not be beneficial in reducing kidney damage or improving outcomes in critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis and shock. Clinicians may need to reconsider using sodium bicarbonate in these patients.

articles.title: Individualising blood glucose control in ICU patients: evidence and practical implementations.
articles.abstract: Many intensive care unit patients develop hyperglycaemia, and this is associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes. Landmark randomised controlled trials (RCTs) suggest the impact of lowering blood glucose to the healthy, age-adjusted fasting range, hereafter called tight glucose control, depends on the accuracy of the glucose control protocol and the nutritional strategy. In the context of early parenteral nutrition, a condition that induces severe, iatrogenic hyperglycaemia, tight glucose control significantly reduced morbidity and mortality compared to tolerating severe hyperglycaemia. In the absence of early parenteral nutrition, hyperglycaemia was less severe; tight glucose control, applied with a computerised protocol that avoided severe hypoglycaemia, did not impact mortality nor the duration of ICU dependency as primary endpoint in a large multicentre RCT, but was associated with a less pronounced benefit on selected morbidity outcomes. Conversely, tight glucose control, using a protocol that considerably increased the risk of severe hypoglycaemic events, concomitantly increased mortality; nevertheless, the cause of excess mortality in this trial remains unproven and other mechanisms may have contributed as well. Altogether, evidence suggests that severe and iatrogenic hyperglycaemia and hypoglycaemia should both be avoided. From a pathophysiologic point of view, tight glucose control may be superior in selected settings if it can be applied with a validated protocol that avoids severe hypoglycaemia. In the absence of such a protocol, the increased risk of severe hypoglycaemia may offset any benefit of preventing hyperglycaemia, and tolerating intermediate blood glucose targets is likely the default setting. In the paper, we suggest specific blood glucose targets that differ according to the clinical context. Future research should aim at strategies that further optimise the quality of blood glucose control and study whether these improve patient-centred outcomes, and investigate whether specific patient populations benefit from individualised targets.

articles.title: Induction Agents for Tracheal Intubation of Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tracheal intubation is a common yet high-risk procedure in critically ill patients, with as many as one-half experiencing peri-intubation adverse outcomes. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the comparative effectiveness and safety of various sedative agents used for endotracheal intubation of critically ill patients in the emergency department (ED), ICU, operating room, and prehospital setting? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis and systematic review of randomized controlled trials. We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, Cochrane, and trial registries from inception through December 10, 2025, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ≥ 2 sedative agents in critically ill adults or children undergoing endotracheal intubation. Outcomes of interest were hemodynamic instability during intubation, hypoxemia, cardiac arrest, mortality, ICU and hospital length of stay, vasopressor use, adrenal insufficiency, and first-pass success. Reviewers screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool independently and in duplicate. We performed frequentist random-effects model network meta-analysis and used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach to rate certainty in estimates. RESULTS: We included 21 RCTs enrolling 6,031 patients across ICU, ED, operating room, and prehospital settings. Compared with etomidate, more hemodynamic instability exists during intubation with ketamine (relative risk [RR], 1.31; 95% CI, 1.15-1.48; moderate certainty). Ketamine-propofol may decrease hemodynamic instability during intubation compared with etomidate (RR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.27-0.72; low certainty) and ketamine (RR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.21-0.56; low certainty). Compared with etomidate, ketamine may decrease the need for the initiation of postintubation continuous infusion vasopressors (RR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.50-1.28; low certainty). Etomidate caused increased adrenal suppression compared with other agents. INTERPRETATION: Our results show that when considering sedation agents for endotracheal intubation of critically ill patients, etomidate probably causes less hemodynamic instability during intubation when compared with ketamine. However, etomidate may increase the need for the initiation of postintubation continuous infusion vasopressors when compared with ketamine and increases adrenal suppression. The clinical importance of these competing effects remains uncertain. Ketamine-propofol may decrease hemodynamic instability during intubation when compared with etomidate and ketamine, although the available evidence is too limited and uncertain to support firm conclusions, and further randomized trials are needed. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; No.: CRD42024600739; URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/.

articles.title: Sodium Bicarbonate for Acute Metabolic Acidosis in Critically Ill Adults: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Acute metabolic acidosis is frequent in critical illness and may be managed with volume replacement therapy, sodium bicarbonate, and renal replacement therapy (RRT). BICARICU-1 and BICARICU-2 trials provided new evidence on bicarbonate therapy. We aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of sodium bicarbonate in critically ill patients. DATA SOURCES: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Medline, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating sodium bicarbonate vs. placebo in critically ill adults with acute metabolic acidosis. STUDY SELECTION: Only RCTs were selected. DATA EXTRACTION: Primary outcome was RRT; secondary outcomes were mortality, ICU length of stay, ventilator-free days, and vasopressor-free days. DATA SYNTHESIS: We performed Hartung-Knapp random-effects meta-analyses and trial sequential analysis (TSA) for primary outcomes. Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses with noninformative and weakly informative priors were used for sensitivity analysis. Four trials enrolling 1,111 patients were included. Sodium bicarbonate showed a nonsignificant trend toward lower mortality (risk ratio [RR], 0.84; 95% CI, 0.55-1.30); TSA indicated that the cumulative sample size remained far below the required information size, and the mortality effect is inconclusive. Sodium bicarbonate significantly reduced RRT use (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.61-0.78), and TSA supported firm evidence of benefit. Bayesian analyses estimated posterior probabilities of any mortality reduction (RR < 1) and reduced RRT use of 90.4% and 94.6%, respectively. Secondary outcomes remained imprecise, with a trend of toward more vasopressor-free days. CONCLUSIONS: In critically ill adults with acute metabolic acidosis, sodium bicarbonate significantly reduces RRT requirement, with Bayesian analyses suggesting a possibility of mortality benefit, although current evidence remains inconclusive. Larger RCTs or high-quality real-world studies are needed to confirm efficacy of sodium bicarbonate for mortality.
articles.ai_summary: This meta-analysis of 4 trials found that sodium bicarbonate reduced the need for renal replacement therapy in critically ill adults with acute metabolic acidosis, and may also lower mortality, although evidence is still inconclusive.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings suggest that sodium bicarbonate may be a useful treatment for critically ill patients with acute metabolic acidosis, but more research is needed to confirm its effects on mortality.

articles.title: Glycemic Ratio Is a Superior Predictor of Mortality Compared With Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio in Critically Ill Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The glycemic ratio (GR), defined as the ratio of mean intensive care unit (ICU) blood glucose (BG) to estimated preadmission BG (EPBG), may provide superior prognostic insight compared with the single admission snapshot represented by the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR, the ratio of ICU admission BG to EPAG). METHODS: This retrospective study included 4148 patients treated in a university-affiliated medical-surgical ICU from 2019 to 2023 who had >4 ICU BG measurements and a glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) measured at admission. We compared SHR and GR prognostic ability for mortality, analyzed across prespecified GR and SHR bands, and calculated observed:expected mortality ratios (OEMRs). RESULTS: We observed a more sharply defined J-shaped relationship between GR and mortality compared with that generated by SHR. Mortality in the reference band of 0.8 to <1.0 for GR and SHR mortality was 7.5% vs 10.9%, respectively (P = .0087), and for the strata ≥1.4, mortality was 25.6% vs 20.5% (P = .0376). Compared with the reference band, GR < 0.8 and GR > 1.0 had higher OEMR (P < .0001 for each), but the OEMR for SHR <0.8 and >1.0 compared with the reference band was not significantly different. CONCLUSIONS: Glycemic ratio was superior to SHR as a predictor of mortality. This study demonstrates that a mean ICU BG level representing 80% to 100% of the patient's EPBG was associated with the lowest mortality rate in a heterogeneous cohort of critically ill patients. These results may inform current BG management strategies and should be considered when designing future interventional trials in the critically ill.
articles.ai_summary: This study compared two ways to predict mortality in critically ill patients: using a single blood glucose measurement at admission, and using a ratio of mean ICU blood glucose to estimated preadmission blood glucose. The study found that the ratio method was a better predictor of mortality. The best outcome was associated with a mean ICU blood glucose level that was 80-100% of the patient's preadmission level.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings may improve blood glucose management strategies in the ICU and inform the design of future clinical trials.

articles.title: A Cross-sectional Study to Examine the Prognostic Value of Glycated Hemoglobin Levels and Glycated Hemoglobin-adjusted Glycemic Variables in Patients with Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Dysglycemia, including both chronic hyperglycemia and stress-induced hyperglycemia, has been increasingly recognized as an important determinant of outcomes in critically ill patients. However, the prognostic value of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c)-adjusted glycemic indices in AECOPD remains poorly understood. OBJECTIVES: To assess the role of HbA1c and HbA1c-adjusted glycemic indices (glycemic gap, stress hyperglycemia ratio, and modified stress hyperglycemia ratio) in predicting outcomes in AECOPD. To determine the correlation between HbA1c-based adjusted glycemic variables in patients with AECOPD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted on 102 patients admitted with AECOPD. HbA1c and admission glucose were measured, and HbA1c-adjusted glycemic indices were calculated. Outcomes, such as respiratory failure, intensive care unit admission, and mortality, were analyzed. RESULTS: Patients with adverse outcomes had significantly higher HbA1c, admission glucose, glycemic gap, and stress hyperglycemia ratio. Stress hyperglycemia ratio and glycemic gap showed superior predictive accuracy for adverse outcomes compared to HbA1c or admission glucose alone. CONCLUSION: HbA1c-adjusted glycemic indices are powerful predictors of clinical outcomes in AECOPD and can be used as simple, cost-effective prognostic tools in routine clinical practice.
articles.ai_summary: This study examined the relationship between glycated hemoglobin levels and glycemic variables in patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. It found that HbA1c-adjusted glycemic indices, such as glycemic gap and stress hyperglycemia ratio, were strong predictors of clinical outcomes. These indices may be useful in predicting patient outcomes and guiding treatment decisions.
articles.ai_significance: Understanding the prognostic value of glycated hemoglobin levels and glycemic variables can help clinicians identify patients at high risk of adverse outcomes and tailor their treatment approach accordingly.

articles.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Adult ICU Patients: A Meta-Analysis on Its Clinical Effectiveness.
articles.abstract: Critically ill patients often suffer from disrupted glucose metabolism, and well-managed blood glucose is a key determinant of clinical outcomes. While continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is regarded as a viable alternative, its overall effectiveness in adult ICU patients remains controversial. This study aims to conduct a systematic evaluation on the effects of CGM versus conventional intermittent blood glucose monitoring on glycemic management among adult critically ill patients in ICUs. Literature searches were carried out across seven electronic databases including PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang Data and VIP, from database inception up to May 18, 2026. Included studies were RCTs that compared CGM with conventional intermittent glucose monitoring in adult ICU patients. A total of 22 eligible RCTs with 1,396 enrolled patients were incorporated into the meta-analysis. The pooled estimates showed that CGM was associated with a significant reduction in hypoglycemic events (RR = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.31-0.54, I2 = 24.9%) and average blood glucose levels (MD = -0.34 mmol/L, 95% CI: -0.55 to -0.13, I2 = 68.3%). The intervention also prolonged time in glycemic target range (MD = 10.12%, 95% CI: 6.03%-14.21%, I2 = 67.5%), cut down daily insulin use (MD = -22.17 U/day, 95% CI: -26.82 to -17.52, I2 = 37.7%), and reduced total mortality (RR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.34-0.65, I2 = 0.0%). Our results suggest integrating CGM into routine ICU glycemic control strategies, particularly for patients with severe glycemic variability and high hypoglycemia risk.

articles.title: Nutrition Therapy in Critically Ill Adults.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract: In the acute phase of critical illness, adults have severe catabolism, inflammation, muscle loss, and gut dysfunction, all of which shape nutritional requirements. Early enteral nutrition supports gut integrity and microbiome health, but trials have shown that early short-term parenteral nutrition is a safe alternative when enteral feeding is not possible. Large trials have shown that early full-dose energy delivery offers no benefit over restrictive dosing and may increase gastrointestinal and metabolic complications, findings that support a restrictive nutrition strategy, especially in patients who have circulatory shock or are at risk for refeeding syndrome. Similarly, large trials have shown no advantage of high-dose over standard-dose protein and suggest harm in patients with acute kidney injury. Because adverse events are common with enteral nutrition, safe nutrition delivery requires gradual advancement, strategies for prevention of refeeding syndrome, glycemic control, and avoidance of routine gastric residual volume monitoring. Patient heterogeneity underscores the need for precise, biomarker-guided, phase-specific nutrition to preserve lean muscle mass and improve recovery.

articles.title: Bedside identification of subphenotypes in acute respiratory failure (PHIND): a multicentre, observational cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a clinically defined, biologically heterogeneous condition with no proven disease-modifying therapies. Retrospective analyses have identified two biologically distinct subphenotypes (hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory) of ARDS, with differing outcomes and responses to therapy. Rapid identification of these subphenotypes in an actionable timeframe has previously not been possible. The PHIND study aimed to prospectively identify these subphenotypes and to demonstrate differing 60-day mortality. METHODS: The PHIND study was a prospective, multicentre, observational cohort study conducted in intensive care units (ICUs) within the National Health Service in the UK and the Health Service Executive in Ireland. Adult patients aged 18 years and older with ARDS or acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure (AHRF) were enrolled within 72 h of onset of the syndrome. Eligible patients were required to be receiving invasive mechanical ventilation, non-invasive ventilation, or high-flow nasal oxygen. Plasma interleukin (IL-6) and soluble TNF receptor-1 (TNFR1) were quantified at enrolment using a near-patient benchtop immunoanalyser (Randox multiSTAT) with a run time of approximately 1 h. Together with plasma bicarbonate measured from an arterial blood sample, these values were used to prospectively determine subphenotypes on an individual patient basis using a validated parsimonious logistic regression model. The primary outcome was 60-day mortality. The study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04009330. FINDINGS: Between Nov 22, 2019, and Sept 28, 2023, 1853 patients from 30 centres were screened for eligibility. Of these, 1328 were excluded and 525 were recruited into the study, with 512 individuals included. 308 (60%) patients were male, 204 (40%) were female, and mean age was 57·0 years (SD 15·1). 443 (87%) patients were white, 18 (4%) were Black, and 16 (3%) were Asian. 490 were subphenotyped using the near-patient assay: 89 (18%) were classified as hyperinflammatory and 401 (82%) as hypoinflammatory. The primary outcome of 60-day mortality was measured in 486 patients after four patients withdrew consent for confirmation of vital status. 60-day mortality was significantly higher in the hyperinflammatory group (45 [51%] of 88) than in the hypoinflammatory group (111 [28%] of 398; risk ratio 1·8 [95% CI 1·4-2·4], p<0·0001). After adjustment, hyperinflammatory patients had increased odds of 60-day mortality (adjusted odds ratio 2·7 [95% CI 1·6-4·4], p=0·0002). INTERPRETATION: Rapid identification of ARDS inflammatory subphenotypes using a near-patient assay was feasible and associated with many clinical characteristics and outcomes consistent with those described in earlier retrospective studies, including mortality, prevalence of sepsis, and incidence of metabolic acidosis. These findings support the implementation of precision medicine approaches in ARDS and the urgent need for prospective, subphenotype-stratified interventional trials. FUNDING: Innovate UK, Randox Laboratories, and Belfast Health & Social Care Trust.

articles.title: Implementation of the kidney protection strategy in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury - a multi-center prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The international Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines recommend the implementation of a kidney protection strategy (KPS) in patients at high risk of and with Acute Kidney Injury (AKI). However, real-world implementation of this strategy in critically ill patients with AKI is unclear. We quantified timely and sustained adherence to KPS in critically ill adults with moderate-to-severe (KDIGO stage 2 or 3) AKI and explored associations with clinical outcomes. METHODS: This was a multicenter, prospective cohort study enrolling adult patients with moderate or severe AKI requiring vasopressors and/or mechanical ventilation across five centers in Europe. The primary endpoint was adherence to the KPS, which included hemodynamic monitoring, sustained optimization of mean arterial pressure (MAP) > 65 mmHg, monitoring of serum creatinine and urine output, and avoidance of hyperglycemia, radiocontrast agents and nephrotoxins when possible, within 12 h after AKI diagnosis for 48 h or until ICU discharge. Exploratory analyses examined associations between adherence and renal outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 258 patients were enrolled (median age 69 years [IQR 62-75]; 65% male; median SOFA 10 [IQR 8-13]). The complete KPS was implemented in 80 patients (31%; 95% CI, 25.5-37.2%). Adherence to individual components of the KPS varied widely with optimization of MAP showing the lowest implementation rate (33%). In exploratory analyses accounting for death as a competing risk, KPS adherence was associated with a lower incidence of AKD beyond day 7 (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.64; 95% CI, 0.41-0.99; p = 0.046), a higher incidence of renal recovery at hospital discharge (SHR 6.02; 95% CI, 4.00-9.05; p < 0.0001), and a lower incidence of RRT within 30 days (SHR 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.91; p = 0.04). After multivariable adjustment, the association with renal recovery remained robust (adjusted SHR 6.29; 95% CI, 3.08-12.85; p < 0.0001). A clear dose-response relationship was observed between the number of implemented KPS components and renal outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: In critically ill patients with moderate-to-severe AKI, the complete KDIGO-recommended kidney protection strategy was implemented in approximately one-third of patients, and full KPS adherence was associated with a higher rate of renal recovery at hospital discharge.
articles.ai_summary: This study looked at how well a kidney protection strategy was implemented in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. They found that about a third of patients received the full strategy, and those who did had a higher rate of kidney recovery. The study also found a link between the number of strategy components implemented and better kidney outcomes.
articles.ai_significance: This study is important for ICU clinicians because it highlights the need to implement a kidney protection strategy in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury to improve kidney recovery rates.

articles.title: Predictors and Mortality Determinants of Non-Thyroidal Illness Syndrome Among Patients in the Medical Intensive Care Unit in Northeastern Tanzania.
articles.journal: Clinical medicine insights. Endocrinology and diabetes
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-thyroidal illness syndrome (NTIS) frequently occurs in critically ill patients and reflects alterations in thyroid hormone metabolism without intrinsic thyroid disease. It has been increasingly recognized as a potential marker of disease severity and poor outcomes in intensive care settings, yet data from Sub-Saharan Africa remain limited. To determine the prevalence of NTIS and identify determinants of mortality among patients admitted to a medical intensive care unit (ICU) in northern Tanzania. METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study among 120 adult patients admitted to the medical ICU at a tertiary referral hospital between October 2024 and March 2025. Thyroid function tests (T3, T4, and TSH) were measured within 24 hours of admission. NTIS was defined based on characteristic biochemical patterns in the absence of known thyroid disease. Clinical, laboratory, and outcome data were collected prospectively. Associations were assessed using Chi-square tests and modified Poisson regression to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRR) with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: The prevalence of NTIS was 23.3%. Overall mortality was 42.5%, with significantly higher mortality among patients with NTIS (67.9%) compared with those without NTIS (34.8%). NTIS remained independently associated with mortality after adjustment (aRR 8.05; 95% CI: 2.27-28.56; p=0.001). Patients with NTIS were also more likely to experience prolonged hospital stays. Although several clinical variables showed associations in bivariate analysis, most did not remain significant after adjustment. Illness severity, as reflected by clinical scoring systems, remained an important contributor to outcomes. CONCLUSION: NTIS is common among critically ill patients and is strongly associated with increased mortality. It may serve as a practical prognostic marker in ICU settings, particularly in resource-limited environments. Further multicenter studies are needed to validate its prognostic utility and integration into routine clinical practice.
articles.ai_summary: Researchers studied 120 critically ill patients in Tanzania and found that 23.3% had Non-Thyroidal Illness Syndrome (NTIS), which was strongly linked to higher mortality and longer hospital stays. NTIS is a common condition in ICU patients and may be a useful marker for predicting poor outcomes. Patients with NTIS had a much higher risk of death compared to those without NTIS.
articles.ai_significance: This study highlights the importance of NTIS as a potential prognostic marker in ICU settings, particularly in resource-limited environments. It suggests that NTIS could be used to identify patients at higher risk of mortality and inform clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Combined impact of glucose variability and mineral disorders on mortality and severe cardiorenal events in critically ill CKD patients: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Elderly critically ill ICU patients with CKD face high mortality. The independent and combined prognostic roles of glycemic variability (Glucose CV) and calcium-phosphate metabolic disorders in this population remain unconfirmed. METHODS: This retrospective study contained three cohorts: MIMIC-IV (n = 1,319, development), multicenter eICU (n = 996, validation), and Chinese hospital cohort (n = 1,069, clinical validation). Multivariable Cox regression and meta-analysis were applied. RESULTS: Elevated Glucose CV independently predicted 28- and 90-day mortality with predominant early risk. Concurrent hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia indicated the poorest prognosis, and high GV produced synergistic harmful effects in this subgroup. All results were verified by external cohorts. DISCUSSION: Targeted glycemic variability management and calcium-phosphate homeostasis correction may effectively improve survival of elderly critically ill CKD patients.
articles.ai_summary: This study looked at how glucose variability and mineral disorders affect critically ill patients with kidney disease. It found that both factors can increase the risk of death and severe complications, especially when combined. The study suggests that managing these factors could improve survival.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings are important for ICU clinicians because they highlight the need to closely monitor and manage glucose variability and mineral disorders in critically ill patients with kidney disease to improve their outcomes.

articles.title: Hemoglobin glycation index and short-term mortality in sepsis: a retrospective cohort study with external validation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The hemoglobin glycation index (HGI) reflects interindividual variability in hemoglobin glycation beyond average glycemic exposure. Although stress-related dysglycemia is common in sepsis, the prognostic relevance of HGI in critically ill patients with sepsis remains unclear. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV database (n = 2,073) as the primary cohort. HGI was calculated as the difference between observed and predicted HbA1c based on admission glucose. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Findings were validated in an independent external cohort (n = 166). RESULTS: In the primary cohort, the 28-, 60-, and 90-day mortality rates were 23.25, 27.69, and 30.00%, respectively. Non-survivors exhibited significantly lower HGI levels than survivors (p < 0.001). Compared with the lowest HGI quartile (Q1), patients in the highest quartile (Q4) had a significantly lower risk of 28-day mortality (hazard ratio (HR) 0.70, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.52-0.94; p = 0.018) and 60-day mortality (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.58-1.00; p = 0.050). A similar but non-significant trend was observed for 90-day mortality (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.62-1.04; p = 0.101). In the external validation cohort, higher HGI was similarly associated with reduced 28-day mortality, supporting the robustness of the primary findings. CONCLUSION: Higher HGI was associated with lower short-term mortality in this retrospective cohort of critically ill patients with sepsis, with the strongest evidence observed for 28-day mortality. These findings suggest that HGI may provide prognostic information during the early phase of sepsis. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings and determine their clinical utility.
articles.ai_summary: Researchers studied how a measure of hemoglobin glycation (HGI) affects short-term mortality in sepsis patients. They found that higher HGI levels were associated with lower mortality rates, especially within 28 days. This suggests HGI could be a useful prognostic tool in the early stages of sepsis.
articles.ai_significance: These findings could help clinicians predict patient outcomes and make more informed decisions in sepsis care. Further studies are needed to confirm the clinical utility of HGI in this context.

articles.title: Enteral nutrition-related hyperglycemia in critical illness: cascade conceptual model and implications for precision nursing-a systematic review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperglycemia is a common complication in critically ill patients receiving enteral nutrition (EN). This review synthesizes evidence on its mechanisms, epidemiology, clinical implications, and nursing management to support precision glycemic care. METHODS: A systematic literature search identified 45 eligible studies, including randomized trials, retrospective studies, reviews, guidelines, and expert consensus statements. Given the lack of a universally accepted definition, enteral nutrition-related hyperglycemia was pragmatically defined as blood glucose ≥7.8 mmol/L occurring within 24-72 h after initiation of enteral nutrition. RESULTS: Reported incidence varies widely, from approximately 30-47% in general ICU populations to 60-80% following cardiac surgery, reflecting differences in definitions, patient characteristics, timing, and nutritional protocols. Based on thematic integration of existing evidence, we propose a six-level conceptual cascade framework, linking metabolic vulnerability, stress-hormone activation, exogenous substrate load, enteroinsular axis dysfunction, inflammation-mediated insulin resistance, and microbiota dysbiosis. Corresponding nursing strategies include diabetes-specific formulas, optimized feeding regimens, continuous glucose monitoring, and individualized insulin protocols within multidisciplinary care. These strategies may improve glycemic control; however, evidence for clinical outcome benefits remains limited and heterogeneous. CONCLUSION: Further prospective studies are needed to validate the model and refine precision nursing strategies.
articles.ai_summary: This systematic review of 45 studies examined the mechanisms and management of hyperglycemia in critically ill patients receiving enteral nutrition, proposing a six-level conceptual cascade framework to guide precision glycemic care.
articles.ai_significance: Understanding and managing enteral nutrition-related hyperglycemia is crucial for ICU clinical practice as it can lead to improved glycemic control, but further studies are needed to confirm its clinical benefits.

articles.title: Numerical and Clinical Accuracy of the FreeStyle Libre 2 System: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study in Critically Ill Patients.
articles.journal: Clinical medicine insights. Endocrinology and diabetes
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The accuracy of the FreeStyle Libre 2 system in critically ill patients needing insulin therapy remains inadequately evaluated. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical and numerical accuracy of continuous glucose monitoring (FreeStyle Libre 2) and capillary glucometry (StatStrip) compared with central laboratory glucose in critically ill patients requiring insulin therapy. METHODS: We conducted a diagnostic accuracy study, evaluating simultaneously two index tests, the FreeStyle Libre 2 and capillary glucose, compared to the central laboratory glucose (venous or arterial) as reference standard. The study included critically ill adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with diabetes or stress hyperglycemia, requiring insulin therapy, and ventilatory or vasopressor support. Numerical accuracy was assessed using ISO 15197:2013 criteria and Mean Absolute Relative Difference (MARD). Clinical accuracy was evaluated using Clarke and Parkes error grid analysis. RESULTS: A total of 157 paired measurements were collected. FreeStyle Libre 2 showed a MARD comparable to capillary glucose (10.43% vs 7.58%; p=0.14). Neither method met ISO 15197:2013 numerical accuracy criteria. In the clinical accuracy analysis, FreeStyle Libre 2 classified 100% of measurements within zones A+B on both the Clarke and Parkes grids, whereas capillary glucose achieved 97.6% and 100%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: FreeStyle Libre 2 showed numerical accuracy comparable to capillary blood glucose and consistently reliable clinical performance in critically ill patients needing insulin therapy. These results support its potential as an alternative to capillary glucose monitoring in the ICU. More studies involving a greater number of hypoglycaemic events are required to confirm its effectiveness in this critical range.
articles.ai_summary: This study compared the accuracy of the FreeStyle Libre 2 system and capillary glucometry to central laboratory glucose in critically ill patients requiring insulin therapy. The FreeStyle Libre 2 showed comparable numerical accuracy and consistently reliable clinical performance. A total of 157 paired measurements were collected.
articles.ai_significance: This study's findings support the potential use of the FreeStyle Libre 2 system as an alternative to capillary glucose monitoring in the ICU, but more studies are needed to confirm its effectiveness in preventing hypoglycemia.

articles.title: Endpoint-specific mortality associated with malignancy among adults with sepsis or septic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a major global health challenge and increasingly affects patients with complex conditions such as malignancy. Prior studies suggest higher mortality in this population, but interpretation is limited by aggregation of heterogeneous endpoints. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify endpoint-specific prognostic associations between malignancy and mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251141216). PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library and Epistemonikos were searched through 16 September 2025, for studies comparing all-cause mortality between sepsis patients with and without malignancy. Mortality endpoints were grouped as ICU, in-hospital, early, intermediate and extended follow-up mortality. Crude odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup, meta-regression and sensitivity analyses were performed to explore heterogeneity and assess consistency. Among 105 eligible studies comprising 20,089,138 participants, 85 studies contributing 101 endpoint estimates were included in the primary synthesis. Pooled estimates were elevated across endpoints: ICU (OR 1.21, 95% CI 0.94-1.56), in-hospital (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.69-2.13), early (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.59-2.06), intermediate (OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.72-3.03) and extended follow-up mortality (OR 2.41, 95% CI 1.70-3.42). Associations were sustained for haematologic malignancy, concentrated in in-hospital and early mortality for metastatic disease and more modest for solid tumours. Sensitivity analyses were directionally consistent, although risk ratio estimates were generally smaller than ORs. Exploratory meta-regression suggested that severity-related covariates may contribute to heterogeneity. Malignancy was associated with higher mortality among adults with sepsis or septic shock, with variation across mortality endpoints and clinical contexts. These findings support endpoint-specific prognostic assessment and highlight the need for future studies to incorporate more granular cancer characteristics. Because the primary estimates were unadjusted, results represent overall prognostic associations rather than independent causal effects.

articles.title: Persistent lymphopaenia in critically ill patients with and without sepsis: An Australian and New Zealand point prevalence study.
articles.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
authors: Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Point Prevalence Program and The George Institute for Global Health
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of persistent lymphopaenia, defined as an absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) < 1.0 × 109/L on both the first and second intensive care unit (ICU) days in patients with sepsis and the association of persistent lymphopaenia with advanced organ support. A prospective, multicentre, binational point prevalence study of adult patients treated in participating ICUs in June 2023 was conducted. Main outcome measures included prevalence of persistent lymphopaenia in patients with sepsis versus those without sepsis, hospital and ICU mortality, length of stay, and organ support patterns. Among 829 adult patients in 59 ICUs, 307 (37%) had persistent lymphopaenia, and 338 (40.8%) met sepsis criteria. Persistent lymphopaenia was associated with greater illness severity (mean Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score: 19.4 vs. 16.8, p < 0.001). Persistent lymphopaenia was more common in patients with sepsis than in those without sepsis (44.7% vs. 31.8%, p < 0.001); this difference remained after adjusting for predefined covariates (odds ratio: 1.51, 95% confidence interval: 1.12-2.03, p = 0.008). For patients with sepsis and persistent lymphopaenia, there was a 6% increase in mortality compared to those without lymphopaenia, although this did not reach statistical significance. For patients without sepsis, hospital length of stay was 16.5 days in those who had persistent lymphopaenia versus 14.4 days in those without persistent lymphopaenia (95% confidence interval: 0.5-3.7, p = 0.01). Persistent lymphopaenia is common in critically ill patients, particularly those with sepsis. Future prospective and interventional investigations are required to clarify the clinical significance of persistent lymphopaenia in critically ill adults and its potential as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Can Platelet Indices Predict Gram-Positive Bacterial Infections in ICU Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundUntil now, blood culture remains the gold standard for diagnosis of bloodstream infections (BSI). We investigated the diagnostic accuracy of complete blood count (CBC), particularly platelet indices, as a less expensive and more rapid alternative for the diagnosis of BSI, which allows for early proper antibiotic administration.MethodsA total of 169 patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) from July 2023 to July 2025 who had suspected BSI and were tested via blood culture (BC). Patients were classified into a BSI group (n = 143) and a non-BSI group (n = 26). The BSI group was further classified into three subgroups as Gram negative bacteremia (n = 87), Gram positive bacteremia (n = 46) and candidemia (n = 10). Demographic parameters and hematological parameters were recorded and compared between the groups. To evaluate sensitivity and specificity, we constructed receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.ResultsPatients with positive blood culture had significantly higher PCT, CRP, Neutrophil, PDW, MPV, MPV/PLT, PDW/PLT, and lower PWR, MPV/PCT, PDW/PCT & PLT/PCT compared to patients with negative blood culture. PLT/PCT, PCT, MPV/PCT, CRP, PDW & PDW/PCT have the highest AUCs (AUCs were 0.73, 0.71, 0.70, 0.69, 0.69 & 0.68, respectively). RDW, MPV/PLT, and PDW/PLT significantly increase, and platelet count significantly decreases among patients with Gram-positive compared to patients with Gram-negative bacterial infection. RDW, platelet, MPV/PLT & PDW/PLT have the highest AUC and accuracy in diagnosis of Gram-positive bacteria (AUC were 0.64, 0.62, 0.62 & 0.62, respectively).ConclusionThe RDW, platelet count, MPV/PLT, and PDW/PLT demonstrated the greatest accuracy in predicting Gram-positive bacterial infections.

articles.title: Brachial-to-Radial Pressure Gradient in Critically Ill Patients Treated With Vasoactive Agents: A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Polish Perioperative and Critical Care Research Group (PERI-CRIT)
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To determine the incidence of a significant noninvasive brachial-to-radial arterial pressure gradient (NIBR-APG) and its clinical associations in critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents. DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, observational study. SETTING: Thirteen ICUs in Poland. PATIENTS: Adult ICU patients with radial arterial catheters receiving vasoactive agents hospitalized between April 2025 and July 2025. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Invasive radial mean arterial pressure (MAP) and noninvasive brachial MAP were measured twice and averaged. A NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg was predefined as clinically significant. Baseline characteristics, hemodynamic variables, and outcomes were recorded. Among 303 patients, 49.5% were surgical admissions and 33.3% had septic shock. The median NIBR-APG was 4.5 mm Hg (interquartile range, 0.0-10.0 mm Hg). Fifty-six patients (18.4%) exhibited a NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg. Compared with patients without a significant gradient, these patients received higher norepinephrine-equivalent doses (0.23 vs. 0.10 µg/kg/min), had higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (11 vs. 10), prolonged capillary refill time (3.0 vs. 2.5 s), and higher lactate concentrations (2.7 vs. 1.3 mmol/L). In multivariable analysis, only vasoactive drug dose was independently associated with NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg (odds ratio, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.12-2.52). ICU mortality was higher in patients with significant gradients (48.0% vs. 30.1%). CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one in five critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents demonstrated a clinically significant NIBR-APG. The presence of this gradient was independently associated with higher vasoactive drug requirements and was accompanied by greater illness severity and higher ICU mortality.

articles.title: Molecular Characterization and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns of Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative Bacilli Isolated from Intensive Care Unit Patients in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
articles.abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) present a critical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), severely limiting therapeutic options. This study evaluated the prevalence and molecular resistance mechanisms of GNB in ICU patients. Hospital-acquired urinary tract infections are among the most common healthcare-associated infections in ICUs. The emergence of MDR Gram-negative bacilli has reduced available treatment options and increased morbidity. This study aimed to evaluate antimicrobial resistance patterns and characterize major resistance genes among Gram-negative bacilli isolated from ICU patients. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from 2019 to 2022 across two tertiary centers in North India. We analyzed 427 non-duplicate MDR GNB isolates from ICU urinary samples. Identification followed standard biochemical protocols. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed through Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion as per Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Phenotypic detection of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL), AmpC, and carbapenemase production was performed, alongside molecular characterization of resistance genes (blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M, blaNDM, blaIMP, blaVIM, blaOXA). In the present study, most isolates originated from the medical ICU (66.0%). Most MDR GNB isolates were from males (52%), and the majority of patients belonged to the age group > 60 years. The predominant isolates were Escherichia coli (60%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (19%), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (12%). Alarmingly high resistance rates to Cephalosporins (>90%), Fluoroquinolones (>80%), and Carbapenems (70% overall) were observed. Overall, 40.9% of isolates were ESBL producers, 24.82% AmpC producers, and 13.81% Carbapenemase producers. Molecular analysis revealed a high prevalence of blaCTX M (100%), blaVIM (66%), and blaNDM (48%). The high prevalence of diverse resistance mechanisms underscores the impact of indiscriminate antimicrobial use. Implementation of stringent antimicrobial stewardship and robust infection control practices is essential to mitigate the spread of MDR pathogens in critical care settings.

articles.title: Streptococcus constellatus-Associated Lemierre Syndrome Presenting With Cavitating Septic Pulmonary Emboli Managed by Video-Assisted Thoracoscopy.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Lemierre syndrome is a rare septic thromboembolic disorder. Although historically associated with Fusobacterium necrophorum, non-fusobacterial cases caused by Streptococcus constellatus can present with dominant thoracic sepsis and delayed recognition. CASE REPORT A 25-year-old previously healthy man from northern Ecuador presented with 7 days of dyspnea, productive cough, fever, and hemoptysis, with profound hypoxemia and respiratory distress. Chest computed tomography showed bilateral cavitating septic pulmonary emboli and necrotizing pulmonary infection, and cervical vascular imaging confirmed left internal jugular vein thrombosis. One blood culture set grew Streptococcus constellatus susceptible to penicillin and ceftriaxone; sputum and pleural fluid cultures were sterile. He required intensive care, endotracheal intubation, empiric piperacillin-tazobactam plus vancomycin, escalation to meropenem plus vancomycin during clinical deterioration while resistant or polymicrobial infection was considered, therapeutic anticoagulation, and 2 video-assisted thoracoscopic procedures for empyema and a subsequent pulmonary abscess. After 4 weeks of intravenous antibiotics, he improved and was discharged on a direct oral anticoagulant for 1 additional month, remaining asymptomatic at short-term follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Lemierre syndrome should be considered in young adults with severe sepsis and multifocal cavitating lung lesions, even without pharyngeal symptoms. Empiric therapy should initially cover oral aerobes and anaerobes; once penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus constellatus is confirmed and no co-pathogen is recovered, de-escalation to targeted beta-lactam therapy, such as penicillin G or ceftriaxone, should be considered together with drainage of empyema or abscess when present.

articles.title: Metabolic Syndrome Is Associated With Worsened Clinical Outcomes in Individuals With Necrotizing Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract: Evaluate the relationship between metabolic syndrome (MetS) and clinical outcomes in individuals with necrotizing pancreatitis (NP) and infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN). MetS affects a significant proportion of the global population and is associated with low-grade systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation. This has implications for several disease processes, but the impact of MetS on patients with NP is not well characterized. A retrospective cohort study of patients admitted with NP at a single tertiary center was performed. MetS was defined as meeting any 3 of the following criteria: BMI ≥30 kg/m2, triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, fasting glucose ≥110 mg/dL, blood pressure ≥130/85 mm Hg, and low HDL (<40 mg/dL men, <50 mg/dL women). The need for intensive care, hospital length of stay, development of organ failure, and mortality were compared in patients with NP with or without MetS. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of IPN. A total of 276 (154 MetS, 55.8%) patients were identified. Individuals with MetS more frequently required ICU-level care (38.3% vs. 17.2%; P<0.001) and longer length of stay (9.0 vs. 5.0 d; P=0.029). There was a higher risk of sepsis in those with MetS (27.5% vs. 15.6%; P=0.019), as well as respiratory failure (31.2% vs. 18%; P=0.013), renal failure (35.7% vs. 21.3%; P=0.009), and in-hospital mortality (17.5% vs. 8.2%; P=0.024). The incidence of IPN was higher in patients with MetS (39.6% vs. 23.0%; P=0.003). The presence of MetS in individuals with NP was associated with worsened outcomes, including increased incidence of IPN, sepsis, organ failure, ICU admission, and mortality during index hospitalization.

articles.title: Hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenocortical responses to critical illness: new insights with clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Critical illness profoundly affects the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenocortical (HPA) axis. In the acute phase of sepsis and other critical conditions, systemic cortisol levels rise markedly, yet circulating ACTH is low. Peripheral adaptations - reduced cortisol metabolism, decreased cortisol-binding proteins, and tissue-specific modulation of glucocorticoid receptor signaling - rather than sustained central HPA axis activation generate compartmentalized increased cortisol actions. As illness persists beyond one week, patients transition into prolonged critical illness characterized by a central HPA suppression, impaired adrenocortical structure and function, together increasing the risk for ICU-acquired adrenal insufficiency beyond 4 weeks. Although glucocorticoids, in stress doses, remain widely used for shock reversal, they exacerbate this HPA suppression and aggravate acute and long-term complications of critical illness. A better mechanistic understanding is essential to guide targeted and adequately dosed therapies.

articles.title: Application of machine learning prediction models for in-hospital mortality in diabetic sepsis patients: a study based on the MIMIC IV database.
articles.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
articles.abstract: Sepsis complicated by diabetes mellitus represents a significant clinical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Accurate prognostication of in-hospital mortality in this complex patient population is crucial for optimizing clinical decision making, resource allocation, and patient management strategies. We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database. The study focused on adult ICU patients with concurrent diagnoses of sepsis and diabetes mellitus. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated for their predictive performance: Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), XGBoost and LightGBM. Additionally, we assessed the prognostic capability of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. Model discrimination was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). To enhance model interpretability, we employed SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values to elucidate the relative importance of predictor variables. The study cohort comprised 7716 patients, with 1357 (17.6%) experiencing in-hospital mortality. Among the machine learning models evaluated, GBDT exhibited superior predictive performance achieving an AUC of 0.792 (95% CI: 0.769-0.814). This performance surpassed that of other machine learning algorithms and the conventional SOFA score. SHAP analysis provided valuable insights into the hierarchical importance of various clinical and demographic features contributing to the GBDT model's predictions. Our findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning approaches in accurately predicting in-hospital mortality among ICU patients with sepsis and diabetes mellitus. These advanced analytical techniques outperform traditional scoring systems such as SOFA. The integration of SHAP values enhances model interpretability, potentially facilitating the adoption of these predictive tools in clinical practice. Further multi-center validation studies and prospective trials are warranted to confirm the generalizability of these results and to explore the clinical impact of implementing such models in diverse healthcare settings.

articles.title: Re: Prognostic significance of the prothrombin time-international normalized ratio to albumin ratio in cancer patients with complication of sepsis: a retrospectively cohort study.
Beyond Resistance: Carbapenemase Gene Profiles and Mortality in ICU Patients with Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Infections.
articles.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) causes serious infections in intensive care units (ICUs), but the relationship between carbapenemase gene profiles and mortality remains uncertain. This prospective two-center cohort included 94 adult ICU patients with clinical CRKP infection from April to September 2026. The first clinical isolate from each patient was included. blaKPC, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaIMP, blaOXA-48, and blaCTX-M genes were investigated by polymerase chain reaction. The primary outcome was 28-day ICU mortality; 14-day and final ICU mortality were secondary outcomes. blaOXA-48, blaNDM, blaKPC, and blaCTX-M were detected in 65 (69.1%), 49 (52.1%), 19 (20.2%), and 73 (77.7%) of isolates, respectively; blaNDM and blaOXA-48 co-occurred in 39 (41.5%). Fourteen-day, 28-day, and final ICU mortality rates occured in 38 (40.4%), 48 (51.1%), and 53 (56.4%), respectively. No statistically significant associations were observed between individual genes, the presence of two carbapenemase genes, or carbapenemase profiles and any mortality endpoint; adjusted analyses of 28-day ICU mortality yielded similar findings. In the exploratory Firth model, the profile effect was not significant (p = 0.198), whereas a higher age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index and bloodstream infection or ventilator-associated pneumonia, compared with urinary tract infection, were associated with higher odds of 28-day ICU mortality. Frequent gene co-occurrence was observed; however, clinically meaningful gene-mortality associations cannot be excluded because of imprecise estimates.

articles.title: Clinical Factors and Composite Biomarkers Associated with Intensive Care Unit-Acquired Weakness: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Intensive care unit-acquired weakness is a common neuromuscular complication among critically ill patients, but associations of readily available composite biomarkers with this condition remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics, risk factors, and composite biomarkers associated with intensive care unit-acquired weakness. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 135 critically ill patients admitted to intensive care units between December 2020 and December 2023. Patients were classified into an intensive care unit-acquired weakness group (n = 57) and a group without intensive care unit-acquired weakness (n = 78) according to Medical Research Council sum score criteria. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, composite biomarkers, and hospitalization outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analyses were performed. Results: Older age, sepsis, hemodialysis, mechanical ventilation, and glucocorticoid use remained associated with intensive care unit-acquired weakness after adjustment for the other covariates in the model. Affected patients had lower albumin and hemoglobin levels and longer intensive care unit and hospital stays. The neutrophil-to-albumin ratio, inflammatory burden index, creatinine-to-albumin ratio, and serum urea-to-creatinine ratio were higher in affected patients. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed modest discrimination, with areas under the curve ranging from 0.602 to 0.665. Conclusions: Intensive care unit-acquired weakness was associated with clinical and treatment-related factors, hypoalbuminemia, prolonged hospitalization, and elevated composite biomarkers. The composite biomarkers showed only modest discrimination, and their incremental values beyond clinical assessment and clinical utility remain unestablished. Residual confounding by illness severity and nutritional exposure cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Does transfusion of blood products increase the risk of multidrug-resistant infections in critically ill patients?
articles.abstract: To investigate the association between transfusion of blood products during intensive care unit (ICU) stay and the incidence of ICU-acquired colonisation and infection with multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria (ICU-MDR-col, ICU-MDR-inf, respectively). Secondary analysis of two prospective multicentre cohort studies conducted in eight ICUs in France. Adult patients admitted to participating ICUs were enrolled consecutively from May 2019 to June 2021. All patients underwent systematic screening for colonisation with MDR bacteria at admission and weekly thereafter. Exposure to transfusion of blood products during ICU stay, including packed red blood cells (PRBCs), fresh frozen plasma (FFP) and platelet concentrates (PCs), was recorded. The primary outcome was the incidence of ICU-MDR-col and/or ICU-MDR-inf (ICU-MDR-col/inf) until ICU discharge, censored at day 28. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of ICU-MDR-col and ICU-MDR-inf, considered separately. Associations were assessed using mixed-effects Poisson regression models adjusted for prespecified confounders. Subgroup analyses were performed according to immunosuppression status at ICU admission. Among 1103 patients, 358 (32.5%) received transfusion of any blood product. Overall, 292 (26.5%) patients experienced at least one ICU-MDR-col/inf event. Transfusion was associated with an increased incidence of ICU-MDR-col/inf (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR] 1.31, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06-1.62; p = 0.013), mainly driven by ICU-MDR-inf (aIRR 1.62, 95% CI 1.16-2.24; p = 0.004), but not ICU-MDR-col considered individually. This association was restricted to PRBC transfusion. No significant heterogeneity was observed according to immunosuppression status. Transfusion of PBRCs was associated with an increased incidence of ICU-acquired MDR infections, with no significant heterogeneity observed according to immunosuppression status. These findings support a restrictive approach to transfusion and warrant further investigation into its immunological and ecological consequences in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Trends in COVID-19 Patients with Hospital Infection in Intensive Care: A Retrospective Study in Central Italy, 2020-2022.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic. This study describes prevalence and trends of AMR in patients with diagnosed severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection admitted during 2020-2022 to the intensive care unit (ICU) in Molise region, central Italy. A retrospective study was conducted, including patients aged ≥ 18 years with at least one positive bacterial or fungal culture during ICU stay. Data were related to patient demographics, ICU outcomes, healthcare-associated infections, and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles. During the 2020-2022 period, 103 ICU admissions met the inclusion criteria, yielding 268 isolations, of which 157 underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Apart from high proportion of Candida albicans, Gram-negative bacteria predominated, with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Acinetobacter baumannii among the most frequent. Resistance to beta-lactams and carbapenems was consistently high, while it ranged from 53.8% to 66.7% to fluoroquinolones and remained above 50% to aminoglycosides. Tetracycline resistance showed significant year-to-year variation, increasing in 2022 compared with both 2020 and 2021. AMR rates in COVID-19 patients in ICU were persistently high throughout the pandemic, with critical resistance levels in Gram-negatives, underlining the need to reinforce infection prevention and control measures and antimicrobial stewardship programs and align prescribing practices with World Health Organization AWaRe recommendations, even during public health emergencies.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a 24-Hour Landmark Model for 28-Day Mortality in Sepsis-Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) carries substantial short-term mortality. Differences in predictor timing, validation design, and comparators complicate evaluation of published prediction models. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 955 adults with sepsis-associated ARDS who reached a 24-h landmark after intensive care unit (ICU) admission. All-cause mortality was assessed by day 28 from ICU admission. Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-only logistic regression, conventional multivariable logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were compared. The multivariable models used 26 candidate predictors (30 encoded parameters). Five repetitions of five-fold outer cross-validation with three-fold inner tuning provided held-out predictions. Evaluation included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, classification metrics, and decision-curve net benefit. Held-out tree-based Shapley additive explanations described XGBoost predictions. Among 955 patients, 474 (49.6%) died. AUCs based on averaged held-out probabilities were 0.732 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.698-0.761) for LASSO, 0.729 (0.696-0.761) for conventional regression, 0.709 (0.674-0.740) for XGBoost, 0.707 (0.673-0.739) for random forest, and 0.581 (0.545-0.617) for SOFA alone. The LASSO-minus-conventional-regression AUC difference was 0.003 (95% CI, -0.003 to 0.010). Intervals resampled fixed predictions without refitting. LASSO had a Brier score of 0.209, calibration intercept of -0.001, and slope of 1.065. The final equation retained age, Charlson Comorbidity Index, arterial oxygen partial pressure/fraction of inspired oxygen ratio, SOFA, lactate, bilirubin, other infection site, and vasopressor use. LASSO provided moderate discrimination without a clear advantage over conventional regression. The separately tuned final equation requires source-data verification, external validation, and prospective clinical-utility assessment before clinical use.

articles.title: Scientific Output in Septic Shock According to Country Income and Gender: A Meta-Epidemiological Study.
articles.abstract: We aimed to assess trends in septic shock publications by country income and author gender. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for articles indexed with "septic shock" between January 2014 and December 2024. All peer-reviewed publication types were eligible. Conference abstracts and non-peer-reviewed material were excluded. Bibliographic data, first and last author affiliations, country income level (World Bank classification: low- and middle-income countries [LMICs] and high-income countries [HICs]), and journal prestige (SCImago Journal Rank [SJR]) were extracted. Author gender was inferred using the NamSor application programming interface (API). Of 10,352 eligible publications, LMIC-affiliated first authors increased over time (+2.13% per year; 95% CI, +1.66 to +2.61; p < 0.001) from 18% in 2014 to 37% in 2024. Women represented 35.6% of first authors and 25.0% of last authors (with around 20% of authors not classifiable by the NamSor API), with higher proportions in LMICs than HICs (p < 0.001) for both first authors (44.5% vs. 32.5%) and last authors (35.2% vs. 21.5%). Gender concordance was more frequent, with female first authors more often paired with female last authors than male first authors (31.7% vs. 21.1%). Cross-income collaborations, especially involving LMIC last authors, remained rare. Articles led by men in HICs were more often published in higher-SJR journals compared with those led by women (p < 0.001), whereas no gender differences were observed among LMIC-affiliated authors. Despite encouraging growth in LMIC contributions and female representation, major inequities persist. Strengthening equitable collaborations and supporting underrepresented groups would broaden participation and enhance the global applicability in critical care research.

articles.title: Clinical guideline highlights for the hospitalist: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Update (Adults) 2026.
articles.abstract: Guideline title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock (2026). Release date: 2026. Prior version(s): Initial guidelines released in 2004 with major updates in 2008, 2012, 2016, and 2021; the 2026 report is the latest update. Developer: Surviving Sepsis Campaign (Society of Critical Care Medicine [SCCM] and European Society of Intensive Care Medicine [ESICM]). Funding source: SCCM and ESICM; no industry funding. Target population: Adults with suspected or confirmed sepsis or septic shock in hospital and acute care settings.

articles.title: Role of Mitochondrial Impairment in Sepsis-Induced Platelet Activation.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced mitochondrial impairment has been described in different organs, in both animal models and humans. Excessive radical oxygen species (ROS) could be involved in this phenomenon. As a result, antioxidants have been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy, although results remain controversial. Platelet hyperactivation is considered a central pathogenic mechanism in the development of sepsis-induced organ damage. In this study, we aimed to determine whether mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to platelet hyperactivation during sepsis. We also evaluated the effect of ROS scavenging using the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO. Laboratory investigation. University Hospital. Patients with sepsis/septic shock (n = 3/7), nonseptic burn patients (n = 10), and healthy control subjects (n = 10). Platelet mitochondria and isolated platelets from healthy donors were treated in vitro with plasma from patients with sepsis/septic shock and healthy subjects, before and after preincubation with MitoTEMPO. We measured platelet oxygen consumption rates in isolated human platelets using the Seahorse Extracellular Flux Analyzer. Platelet mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity was measured in mitochondria-enriched fractions by spectrophotometry. Platelet aggregation in platelet-rich plasma was analyzed using light-transmission aggregometry, and leukocyte-platelet adhesion in whole blood by flow cytometry.We found that incubating platelets with septic plasma significantly reduced basal, maximal, and adenosine triphosphate-linked oxygen consumption rate. Incubation of platelet mitochondria with septic plasma also reduced platelet Complex I activity, compared with healthy plasma or plasma from nonseptic burn patients. This decrease was associated with an increase in Epinephrine-induced platelet activation. Preincubating platelets with the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO significantly reversed these effects. Our results show that the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO prevents mitochondrial dysfunction and enhances platelet activation induced by septic plasma in human platelets in vitro. This may help in designing new therapeutic approaches to prevent sepsis-induced organ damage mediated by mitochondrial dysfunction and platelet hyperactivation.

articles.title: Delay From Hypotension Onset to Appropriate Antifungal Therapy Initiation Is the Critical Determinant of Outcome in Candida Septic Shock.
authors: and the Cooperative Antimicrobial Therapy of Septic Shock (CATSS) Database Research Group
articles.abstract: To determine the effect of delays in initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy from the initial onset of persistent hypotension to the outcome of Candida septic shock. Retrospective cohort study. A total of 32 academic and community hospitals in Canada, the United States, and Saudi Arabia (July 1989 to June 2018). A total of 850 adult patients with culture-positive Candida septic shock. None. Out of 850 patients with Candida septic shock, 69.2% patients (589) received appropriate antifungal therapy after the onset of persistent hypotension. A strong relationship was observed between the delay in initiation of pathogen-appropriate antifungal (PAA) therapy and hospital survival. The adjusted odds ratio of death was 1.045 per hour of delay (95% CI, 1.035-1.056; p < 0.0001). The survival rate was 86% when an appropriate antifungal for the isolated pathogen was administered within 2 hours of the initial documentation of persistent hypotension. Thereafter, hospital survival decreased an average of 5.0% per hour for each hour of delay to 10-12 hours of delay. In a multivariate analysis, which included the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score and epidemiologic/therapeutic variables, the time to initiation of appropriate antifungal therapy emerged as the single strongest predictor of outcome. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrated that the adverse effects of delayed antifungal treatment were consistent across various subgroups, including different types of infections, pathogens, and antifungal drug classes. Median time to appropriate antifungal therapy was 32.3 hours (interquartile range, 11.2-66.0 hr), with only 16.9% receiving therapy within 6 hours of hypotension onset. Administration of PAAs within the first hours of documented hypotension significantly improved hospital survival. Less than 20% of patients received appropriate antifungals within 6 hours of documented hypotension.

articles.title: Prevalence, Clinical Correlation, and Antifungal Susceptibility of Candidemia Patients in Various Intensive Care Unit's of a Tertiary Care Hospital in Jharkhand.
articles.abstract: Candidemia represents grave healthcare-associated fungal infections. Being an opportunistic pathogen, Candida is becoming a cause of significant morbidity and mortality in patients at greater risk. The aim of the present study was to examine Candida isolates collected from blood cultures in intensive care unit patients at a tertiary care hospital in Jharkhand and to illustrate their various properties and its clinical correlations along with various antifungal susceptibility profiles. In this prospective study of 12 months, Candida isolates from blood were differentiated by conventional methods and compared by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight and VITEK 2 compact automated system. Findings were clinically correlated with various parameters like death, patients requiring assisted ventilation, and number of hospital stay days. Out of 985 positive blood cultures, 95 were Candida species (9.64%). Seventy-nine isolates were Non-Albicans Candida (83.15%) and 16 isolates were Candida albicans (16.8%). Candida tropicalis 30 isolates (31.5%) was isolated, followed by Candida glabrata, Candida parapsilosis, and others. Mean age of the patients was 18.67 years. With a mortality rate of 45.2%, children were mostly deceased, accounting for 58% of all the deaths. Male predominance is seen, constituting 72% of all the deaths. C. tropicalis and C. glabrata were the most common organisms leading to death, both contributing 31% each, while C. tropicalis is the most common organism due to which patients required assisted ventilation. These isolates were susceptible to common antifungals. Judicious start of antifungal drugs in patients of high risk is very important. This study will help clinicians to opt for best antifungal agents in the management of candidemia shortening hospital stay days.
